storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
In solitude, one must act as a team. The twenty-four minds are crowded together—they whisper and chuckle in the dark, tearing at 24's soul, craving to devour her.

The stench from the corner sewer, the cotton drifting through the workshop, the stale black bread... The past has long faded, and no one remembers the ordinary worker from the East District. She has finally shed her weary body, only to step into a new quagmire.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
Awakener ID: MA-C06
Danger Level: A
Special Containment Procedures: MA-C06 is currently housed in Awakener Observation Room 7 with dim lighting. Fearing mind control by @3, MA-C06 refuses to sleep, only provided with a chair.

Due to good behavior and friendly attitude, MA-C06 is allowed to use the greenhouse and explore parts of the campus with an Investigator escort.

—"Awakener Containment FileMA-C06"

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Mythag uses the silver extracted from the bodies of the deceased to create the Awakener.

The Sculptors' Association induce the formation of silver from living bodies and refine it into the Awakener.

These are two entirely different ideologies. The latter, while having an extremely high ceiling, clearly violates ethical standards, thus becoming a taboo Research that persists despite prohibitions.

After the Wax Museum incident, 24 was brought back to Mythag. She spent a long time in the campus observation rooms and research labs, necessitating personal supervision whenever she went out.

Undoubtedly, this is an extremely uncontrollable living Awakener. During the subsequent observation period of half a year, 24's body continuously split into many personalities.

She suddenly found herself with unfamiliar friends and enemies, bought many strange items, and even learned to speak Chinese without realizing it.

Her life is never short of "surprises".

"24 is a discrete function composed of a series of isolated points," Doll commented, "Do not believe every word she says."

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
24 discovered that their home had been robbed less than a month after moving in.

First the cheese, then the bread, the milk, the tomatoes... the food in the house always seemed to dwindle, little by little, without a sound.

She waited patiently for several days, and at last caught the culprit—a mouse. Weaving left and right past the traps she had set, it snatched up two mushrooms and vanished behind the cellar door.

24 opened the cellar door and descended the damp, moldering steps, only to find that they led down into an underground waterway.

The mouse scurried into the shadows, mushrooms in tow. 24 followed, and caught a glimpse of bright eyes in the darkness—like those of a wolf pup. The child was wrapped in tattered cloth and covered with old newspapers, shivering all over in the near-freezing air.

Something pricked faintly at 24's heart.

"Mushrooms are best not eaten raw. You'll get sick."

The child remained silent.

24 went and cooked a pot of mushroom soup, set a small bowl of it on the table, and went to bed. She had to be up by 6 a.m. every day for work, with hardly any time to rest.

When she woke the next morning, the bowl sat exactly where she had left it—but the soup was gone, every last drop.

After that, 24 would occasionally cook a little extra to share with the neighbor downstairs. In return, the child would sometimes leave her small gifts—trinkets and toys found from who knows where...

And so a quiet, unspoken understanding was formed between them.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
On a snowy day that November, 24 fell ill.

After a week of grueling work, she came down with a severe fever and lay in bed for days on end.

In her daze, she seemed to hear little mice whimpering near her ears. After an unknown stretch of time, someone was standing at her bedside.

She recognized those eyes—it was the child from the sewer. Covered in mud, the child held out a grimy little pill to 24.

"For you. Take it," the child said bluntly, her voice surprisingly pleasant—so it turned out she was a girl.

24 looked at the scrapes on her elbow and face but did not ask where the pill had come from. She simply held the girl's hand tightly.

The girl mumbled awkwardly, then said in a cool tone, "I won't leave. I'll go once you're better."

Even when I'm better—don't leave.

24 answered silently, in her heart.

The first snow of winter fell over Londinium for an entire week. On the day it finally stopped, 24 was very happy—because not only had her fever broken, but she had also gained a sister.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: II

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: III

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Ponder
voiceLines.content: Huh? I'm still alive... You... You really won't steal my organs or use me for experiments?

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Reflect
voiceLines.content: {Male=Sir,Female=Madam}, you are truly kind. Sadly, I have nothing to repay you with, worthless as I am...

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight
voiceLines.content: ...Just a little further, and I'll be completely separated from "them"?

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate
voiceLines.content: I am feeling it... The Source of Uncleanliness... One step closer to Our true form... Ahhh, I shall tear this world apart!

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Florish

voiceLines.title: Affinity: I
voiceLines.content: I feel fantastic right now. What? You say my mind has been taken over by something else? N-no way... uh...

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II
voiceLines.content: Heh, that woman is so scared of me coming out that she doesn't even dare to sleep at night. Relax, I wouldn't kill you—not while you're giving me gifts. Who am I? Of course, I'm "24," hahaha!

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content: Please don't worry. We'll all share a steak and a bed, and never cause you any trouble.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content: I used to work until midnight every day—spinning, washing, cleaning, babysitting, even scavenging... I would do anything to earn money. Back then, living was merely surviving. Now, we have fresh food, warm bed, and a kind master like you... It's beyond my wildest dreams.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content: There are many "me" inside. Happy, sad, angry... They love sponge cake, hate Londinium's rainy days. They all go by "24," and they all adore you.

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
Until the fury of history burned everything away, Agrippa was the brightest jewel in Capua.
She does as she likes, and her whip always comes down hard on the silent gladiators. She hates being looked at straight on—it lays bare the weakness underneath. But when it comes to breaking in a slave, Agrippa is a professional. Perhaps you'd care to inspect the twenty whips of assorted design in her bedroom. She had them prepared especially for you.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
@3Built in the Second Samnite period, decorated in the exquisite Third Pompeian and Lemovician styles, this is a typical residence of the wealthy merchant class during the Roman era. Featuring two courtyards and four triclinia, @1@1
.....all reduced to ashes in the famous slave uprising... According to contemporaneous anecdotes, a massive pale spider was sealed beneath the ruins, referred to by locals as the "God of the Maze," and they firmly believe that those who tread upon the spider's territory will become disoriented among countless passages and entrances, ultimately becoming hosts for its offspring.

An interesting horror story, but it will not deter us @2@1
—Excerpt from "@2Archaeological Notes on the Ruins"

.....The situation is dire, Sir Goodman. Moretti and his party have been missing for several days now. We all understand this has nothing to do with the legend of the "God of the Maze," yet it is indeed unsettling. We have decided to end the investigation early and return to Durham.

Additionally, the archaeological team discovered a cluster of Silver-like objects in the ruins, which may be related to the @1 you mentioned earlier...

—Excerpt from Clarkson Johnson's "A Letter to Goodman"

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Arithmetic: Zero points. Aurita even scored 2 points.

English: Failing. It took a long time to understand the difference between "shift" and "bullshit."

......

History: Failing. Claimed Caligula was the most outstanding Roman emperor because he built many arenas.

Danger Rating: C. Shows a degree of aggression when interacting with other Awakeners. Not a serious threat; no special attention needed.

Notes: This individual has almost no self-care abilities (another victim poisoned by slavery), requires constant attention, and must not be allowed to use snowflake cream as a dental cleaner again.

—Excerpt from A.F. 313, "Mythag Annual Student Profile."

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
Even as the gladiators burned the training grounds to the ground and hung her parents' heads on the high wall, Agrippa could not believe it—where would these low, docile slaves find that kind of nerve?
In Rome there were only two sorts of people: those who enslaved, and those who were enslaved.
Agrippa had been lucky. She was the daughter of the man who owned the largest gladiator school in Capua. She was cruel, arrogant, untouchable; there was nothing she did not dare do, nothing she could not do.
And now she was a panicked rabbit huddled in the corner of the cellar, and the revelry outside sounded no different from hell.
A slave revolt. What a strange phrase. Agrippa was only fifteen. There was still far too much in the world she did not understand.
In the shadows she saw a pair of eyes glowing red. That was Uvhash, the school's greatest earner, kept chained underground for years because he was too dangerous.
The two of them had never gotten along, and no one knows what they said to each other that night. When the bloody, fire-lit night was over, Agrippa was found dead deep in the dark, no one beside her. The slaves had not killed her—something had drained her blood, and not a drop was left.
Her head came off in the end, of course. They hung it beside her parents', all of them streaming in the wind, turned toward Rome.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
It was... blinding light and waves of heat, an orgy of pleasure with nothing held back.
The cheering hummed in her ears like surf, and down in the arena the fighters bathed in blood and glory.
The girl went home sullen and did what she always did: raised the whip and brought it down without mercy on the dull-faced gladiator in front of her.

This was her arena.

No exhilarating duel, no flowers, no applause. The towering champions were the tamest of deer, and every curse, all her rage, was swallowed into a dark hollow that gave nothing back—not even a breath of wind.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate
voiceLines.content: I hear someone calling my name: Agrippa, Agrippa, Agrippina...

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Florish
voiceLines.content: I saw... It climbing up from the darkness of the well; countless eyes appearing on its flesh egg. They stared at me, calling me... Maze God!

voiceLines.title: Affinity: I
voiceLines.content: Unbelievable. My home has perished like this... That was the great Rome! You must have heard of it!

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II
voiceLines.content: I was an hour late for this meeting—and I blame those insipid do-gooders who abolished slavery! Now there's no one to comb my hair for me!

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content: If I were you, I'd lock all the Awakeners in cages! Once mad dogs break free, they always bite their master first!

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content: Don't ask me that again! I was careless, let the gladiator escape, and got my entire family killed! We were reduced to ashes, like the Roman Empire!

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content: Keep your pity to yourself! I despise it, and I absolutely don't need anyone's sympathy! If you keep looking at me like that, I simply won't be able to resist tormenting you. You don't want things to spiral out of control, do you? So, be a good slave, listen, and obediently become my gladiator...

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Mythag

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Like

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Hate

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
Do not come close. Do not touch. Do not look at her directly. Do not pity her. Perhaps some creatures were only ever meant to live alone in the dark.
It is not what she wants. But if her frail body, her timid voice, her childish clothes move you to look tenderly into her eyes, you will fall into stillness and silence forever.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
According to the "Cataclysm Event Record III," the Keeper brought back this piece of Silver Core from the Londinium Orphanage. Accompanying the Silver Core was a tiny, patch-covered teddy bear.

This Silver weighs about 2.1 grams, is slender and smooth, resembling a teardrop. Those who come into direct contact with the Silver will fall into a Stasis State, maintaining the posture of touching the Silver until Awakened by someone else. To prevent accidental contact, Researcher Doll kept this Silver in a closed glass orb and replaced the teddy bear's eyes.

"It looks as if it has been crying every day."

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Jenkin pressed against the crack of the door to the counseling room, straining to listen.

Sylvia's voice was gentle and warm, while Aigis's sounded like a mosquito's whimper, intermittent and hard to decipher.

"Aigis, you need to learn to say no."

"But I... don't want to be a burden... I want to... repay..."

"Aigis hasn't been a burden to anyone. You see, Keeper allows you to move freely in school without any restrictions, isn't that a sign of trust?"

"You promised me not to casually agree to unreasonable requests from others. Especially from Caraboo, helping her with her confinement and cleaning will only cause trouble for our Keeper, okay?"

"Jenkin, how did you get in here?"

"J-Jenkin! I... I agreed to Caraboo myself! C-Calm down!"

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
On a morning twelve years ago, in the East District of Londinium, an infant girl bundled in layer upon layer of scarf appeared at the door of the Workhouse. In the East District, where everyone was busy saving their own skin, that was hardly rare. What enraged young Sarah was that in the bite of that winter, whoever abandoned the child had been cruel enough to wrap the scarf over her mouth and nose as well. And the baby neither cried nor fussed. If those clear, bright eyes hadn't blinked a few times when Sarah patted her, Sarah would have taken her for dead.
Just as Sarah was resigning herself to becoming yet another well-behaved child's "big sister," the director at the time handed the baby to a tailor in the East District market for one Leonian Florin.
"We can't afford to feed that child. As a tailor's daughter she'll have a hard time of it, but at least she'll learn a trade."
A trade—for a child not two months old?
Sarah felt her empty stomach and said nothing against the director's decision.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
Afraid of light, afraid of being looked at, afraid of love, afraid of being held.
Longing for light, longing to be looked at, longing for love, longing to be held.
If only she could not hurt anyone. If only she were no trouble to anyone. If only she were clever, like T'yog. If only she were brave, like Jenkin. If only she were like—
Then the sun would not burn her, and no one would find her loathsome. Wouldn't that be so?
And so the doll, carrying worries that can never come true, reaches a small hand, pale to the point of transparency, out of the shadow toward the edge of the light.

voiceLines.title: Awaken
voiceLines.content: H-Hello... Nice to meet you. My name is Aigis... P-Please don't mind me! Just pretend I don't exist...

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: I
voiceLines.content: T-Thank you... for everything you've done. I will do my absolute best... to not let you down!

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: II
voiceLines.content: A treasure that glitters like candy wrappers... I will cherish it dearly.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: III
voiceLines.content: I have grown stronger... I'll use these eyes to paralyze the enemy!

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Observe
voiceLines.content: What can I help you with...?

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Ponder
voiceLines.content: P-please don't look into my eyes... I don't want to hurt you... I'm a monster, after all...

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Reflect
voiceLines.content: I-I feel so uneasy... being looked at like this... Are you not afraid of my curse?

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight
voiceLines.content: I am very anxious... unsure if I can ever meet your expectations...

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate
voiceLines.content: Your gaze is burning me... Have I caused you any trouble?

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Florish
voiceLines.content: I... I understand your intention. Though I'm still clumsy, I will fight for you with all I have!

voiceLines.title: Affinity: I
voiceLines.content: Sorry, if I'm causing you any trouble, I'll leave immediately!

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II
voiceLines.content: Can I stay here a little longer? I will remain quiet, make no sound, and try my best not to disturb you...

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content: Thank you for allowing me to stay here. If there's any way I can repay you, please let Aigis know. Would you like some tea?

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content: It's so warm that I don't want to leave. When I'm alone, it's truly dark, cold, and frightening...

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content: Aigis... Can I really return to the crowd? I'm not ready yet, but you've already accepted me... In that case, please continue to look after me... Keeper.

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
Alva is very happy with her prosthetic.
"After that battle, I never expected to stand again. Getting another chance to fight for what's right is an honor."
As for the low moans that come from her room at midnight—once the sun clears the horizon, let them be as if they never happened.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
A.F.18@1/@1/@2 Infantry Regiment, the Kingdom of Remouahe, Port Alexandria
The situation in Port Alexandria is stabilizing. The 3rd and 4th battalions, along with three companies of musketeers, have crossed the canal to proceed to @4 for the next stage of operations. Now only the 1st battalion and a company of musketeers remain in Port Alexandria.

A squad encountered rebels during a patrol and quickly dealt with them. They brought back an interesting trinket that looks like silver but is heavier. I've stored it in the safe; the commander will like this gift.

.....

Day 13 of the garrison, soldiers from various companies are showing abnormal behavior, including but not limited to attacking comrades, officers, destroying inventory, and military equipment. These soldiers, along with the earlier madmen, are now under my direct supervision in confinement.

Their eyes are bloodshot, and they drool, looking more like pitiful animals than soldiers. Madness is spreading here; I'm worried it will become a plague.

.....

Day 30 of the garrison.

To date, 370 soldiers have shown mad behavior. After 20 days of severe hysteria, 331 of them developed limb numbness and paralysis. Their aggression remains strong; two military doctors were bitten while trying to treat them.

The madness continues to spread. I've reported the situation, hoping for swift action.

.....

The Committee took over the Alexandria garrison for 10 days; people still fall into madness, my brothers one after another. Why are only we suffering this damned plague? Why are the locals fine? Why do the rebels who hassle us remain unaffected?

My head hurts more and more, and the doctors are helpless—they fell into madness before me and became those biting monsters.

I fear I will also go mad.

They say we have to wait for the Mythag University people. Damn them, we fought for our country, we shouldn't be treated this way.

.....

I know now, I finally know. It's a vengeful spirit within that piece of silver, seeking revenge on all who invaded this land. That one-legged woman wants us to leave, wants us all gone, to return everything here to its original owners. Yes, yes, it should be this way, we never should've come, never started this war, I @1@3@4@2@1@2@3
— Excerpt from the "@2 Infantry Regiment 1st Battalion Acting Commander's Log"

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Hannah: Ms. Alva, you've been with Mythag University for quite some time now. The students adore you—a good many girls have pushed love letters at me to pass along. Shall I read them out?
Alva: That's really... ahem. I mean, thank you, everyone? But wasn't I here to talk about my day?
Hannah: Who knew our instructor had such an adorable side! I may have to hide off campus once this runs, or the jealous girls will corner me. All right, back on topic. Would you tell our readers what a day in the life of Mythag's most charming instructor looks like?
Alva: I'm afraid I'll disappoint you. My day is very ordinary. I'm up at four to train, so the leg gets used to moving.
At six I go to the dining hall. An Awakener's body doesn't need food, but I still... call it a habit.
From eight to noon I drill the investigators in combat technique, and sometimes I put the Keeper through extra work. Afternoon training shifts with the class schedule—some days it starts at one, some days at three.
Once a week I find time to go see Nautila and have her tune the prosthetic. She forgets things easily, but her work is excellent. After every service, the pain eases a great deal.
Hannah: And what do you do for fun?
Alva: Fun... that's honestly a bit of a foreign concept to me. Though lately I've gone down to the sea with Aurita and the others. Being around kids that uncomplicated always leaves me relaxed. And swimming does wonders for physical conditioning. Back when I was a recruit, my drill instructor—
Hannah: And that's all we have room for today! If you want to hear more about Ms. Alva's past, keep an eye out for the next issue of "Daily Life in Mythag"!
—Excerpted from "Daily Life in Mythag," a special interview column in the Mythag Daily

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
She spent her girlhood in an army camp.
Like every child raised among soldiers, she believed in the glory of the legion without question and made it her whole life. Her world was simple: what the commander approved was right, and what the commander forbade was wrong.
"Turn your swords on the enemy, and we will give this land its true freedom. Cut down the armies that march against us, and spare them no pity. What we sacrifice now buys the peace and prosperity of tomorrow."
She trained on those words, and she went to war on them. One desperate rescue left her with a ruined leg and the title of war hero. Decorated, she was pulled back from the front to train recruits, with no idea what that ruined leg was about to show her about the world.
When her maimed leg was made a thing to sneer at, Alva left the army in a fury. Only out on the streets did she see what the commander's shining speeches had really been: liberation was a pretext for invasion, and in those foreign lands people were being torn apart.
This was not the country she had dreamed of. This was not the bright future without blood or tears.
So she raised an atoning blade against her old comrades, and swore to fight for justice that was real.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
It isn't that Alva never doubted her own justice—but those dazed days and nights left her with perfect clarity.
What seems unreal is real.
Where she began has never changed. The justice she fights for was never an organization that became an invader, never some man shouting slogans. It stands, plain and upright, inside her own conviction.

Every life, every innocence, every dream and ambition and small bright hope turns to ash the moment the guns open up.
What war takes never comes back; it gnaws through everything good like a devil out of hell.
So those who start wars to feed their own appetites must taste that same annihilation. There will be true heroes, carrying a greater cause, fighting selflessly for a future bright enough for everyone.
That is what justice is worth.
...

What's wrong gets corrected.
The sacrifices have to be worth something. These severed legs and the phantom ache of what's missing have to be worth something.
Whatever was destroyed, she will take back with these new limbs.
The small, fragile things will never lose their light.
All of it for the utopia that truly holds no blood and no tears.

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
An ocean spirit who once faced demise in solitude has found a miraculous second life on land.

Whether naturally optimistic or choosing to forget to escape suffering, her guileless innocence exudes an irresistible charm that draws people to her side—perhaps this is a subtle ploy of hers to expand her "circle of friends."

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
During the investigation along the southern coast of Cornwall, I discovered a derelict village unmarked on any known map. Upon investigation, we confirmed that it had been "erased" by an outbreak of dissolution.

In the village, we collected a large number of anomalous marine specimens, including carnivorous giant clams, heat-resistant sea angels, and most baffling of all, "amphibious jellyfish" found everywhere.

In a dilapidated house that had become a jellyfish nest, we recovered a fluid Silver Core weighing approximately 11.85 drams. While extracting the core, our team was attacked by mutated jellyfish; fortunately, their glands had decayed, posing no neurotoxic threat.

—<Italic:Record of the Third Biology Department Field Survey, A.F. 308>

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Don't expect much from the intellect of jellyfish; Aurita cannot comprehend what she has experienced. All she can affirm is that she once lived in that deserted village. Whenever the past is brought up, she deflects the conversation by feigning understanding, so Aurita contributes little to the study of D-Phenomenon or cataclysmic anomalies.

However, as a rare harmless Awakener, Aurita is deeply cherished by the faculty and students of the Awakener Department. Even Professor Czort, the lead researcher in Dissolution biology, takes particular care of her.

By the way, she gained the ability to split and proliferate after merging with the jellyfish's collective consciousness. Even if what proliferates are just ordinary jellyfish, Aurita excitedly holds up her "companions" to boast door-to-door—though, unable to distinguish between individuals, she remains blissfully unaware that the "new friend" she presents each time is the exact same jellyfish.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
March
Welcome to the Atlantica Touring Aquarium! I'm Aurita, your guide for today—please watch your step as you board the jellyfish caravan!

Displayed here in the tanks are rare jellyfish from tropical waters. Ta-da! Please take a look—

April
Wh-what happened... Where did everyone go... Curator! Curator! The jellyfish—Aurita's jellyfish are all gone!

The aquarium never had jellyfish exhibits? But I clearly remember...

May
Since there are too few exhibits and no guests, we can't keep the business going... <Italic:sob>... Goodbye, everyone...

If—if we ever go on tour again someday, please come find Aurita!

June
Aurita is so tired... Am I sick...?

Oh...! The jellyfish! Sorry, Aurita can't scatter diatoms for you all right now.

Once Aurita feels better, let's all swim together again...

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
A fishing village with crystal-clear waters, a shoreline adorned like the Milky Way on a midsummer night, and the lighthearted laughter echoing from a touring caravan—these memories of a world that no longer exists flash back from time to time, only to be promptly cast aside.

As long as companions keep appearing by her side, new memories can always be made. Besides, the jellyfish are always there—at least, that is what Aurita believes.

After all, to drift and propagate, and face down formidable threats through sheer numbers, is both the nature and the destiny of the jellyfish.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
A.F. 3@1, January.

On the Devil's Reef off the eastern coast of the Agló Republic, local fishermen reported they had salvaged "a strangely shaped corpse"—short and hunched, with protruding eyeballs, partially hardened skin, webbed fingers, and the most bizarre feature being symmetrical red marks on either side of the neck. If it weren't for the student uniform it wore, it would be hard to consider it a "human corpse." 

When the investigators arrived, the strange corpse had already been burned by frightened fishermen as an omen, leaving only a suitcase that was quite popular among students at the time. The suitcase contained no change of clothes, only some illegible manuscripts, a compass, and a photograph of a middle-aged woman.

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Since the @2 incident, Caecus has made his peace with us and joined the Awakened Studies program as an outside auxiliary. His grasp of @1 is fragmentary at best, yet he is only too glad to display it and share it.
Around Tulu, Miryam, Goliath and their like he is nothing but humble; every other race—humans above all—gets a dark, unfriendly look. The researchers who have read his file understand where the bitterness comes from, but some of the hotter-tempered Awakeners have no patience for it. It usually falls to Sylvia to step in and talk everyone down, and a certain trust has grown up between her and Caecus along the way.
Under her guidance, Caecus has discovered a new virtue: "the forbearance of a higher race." He now lets provocations pass without a word.
"That child talks about his human mother often, and always fondly. They say a mother is the yardstick a child measures the world by—his hostility toward humans wasn't born in him, it was taught to him. So really, all he's short of is a little guidance and a little care." So Sylvia wrote in her counseling notes.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
Caecus hated humans. He hated them even as a child.
He once pulled a drowning little girl out of the water, and the other children called him a monster for it. When he kept well away from them, they chased him down shouting "stinking frogman."

In all those bleak years, the one thing he had to look forward to was a letter from Uncle Orne. Orne's learning was vast, and it came with an endless supply of ghost stories that left little Caecus spellbound. It did not last. A few years on, Uncle Orne simply vanished.
Then, at sixteen, Caecus went back to visit his grandfather's house and happened upon Orne's manuscripts. At last he understood the noble meaning hidden in the twisted markings on his skin.
Hah. Humans. Lowly creatures in the end, all of them.
After that he stopped despairing. He waited instead—waited for the day his destiny would come for him.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
You must have had this dream too. A fortune drops into your hands out of nowhere, or some absolute power does—enough to grind everyone who ever sneered at us, everyone who ever hurt us, under your heel.
And then you wake, and reality is still there, endless, and you sink one layer deeper into despair.
But my dream was real. My destiny came for me.

Don't you see? You are the weak ones.

A frail body and a withered soul can't carry noble blood? No. That simply isn't possible. The name Orne is the glory and the emblem of our @2. Granted that blood and that name, I am no longer the freak anyone could humiliate—I am a @1, with noble blood in my veins.

So... please... stop looking at me that way. I can't breathe when you look at me that way...

storySections.content:
Let’s dance! Dance a merry dance, dance a wild dance! Laugh along with her, and stoke the atmosphere to fever pitch.

And then—it's time for the star to take the stage.

There, where the spotlights converge, the mad magician has already slipped her hand into her top hat. As for what she will pull from that endless void—be it a cascade of colorful ribbons, a flock of white doves taking flight, or the razor-sharp claws of some dreadful monster... I'm afraid only she can tell.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
April 1, A.F. 3@2, Silver Core Storage and Management Room, Mythag University Awakener Department, Londinium
Silver Core G411, along with Silver Core G410, was purchased by Lord Dexter from the "Lady Narcissus." The core measures 1.85 cm in length and 0.4 cm at its widest point, with a shape resembling a rhombohedron. Regardless of the angle or position from which it is observed, G411 emits bright yellow rhomboid ripples that radiate outward from the observer's visual focal point.

Prolonged observation may cause the observer to experience mental disorientation, diminished emotional responsiveness, and even lead to Puppetman Syndrome (potential symptoms include complete emotional apathy, loss of volition, severe malnutrition or even death resulting from suppressed appetite). Prompt psychological and emotional intervention is required should such symptoms manifest.

Although its negative effects are milder compared to most Silver Cores, hermetic containment is strongly advised. Direct observation upon retrieval should be strictly avoided to mitigate the risk of G411-induced affective disorder.

—Excerpt from <Italic:Mythag University Silver Core Storage Records>

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
"Tired of the mundane parks? Bored with dull animal exhibitions? Then come to Casiah's Magical Carnival! For kids who love animals, there are tenor-singing lions, ballet-dancing flamingos, acrobatic elephants, and the world's one and only donkey tamer! For couples looking to rekindle the spark, try our unique Live-Horse Carousel for a rare romantic experience! And for the brave souls who crave genuine thrills in their lives, we dare you to challenge the Mirror Maze, hand-designed by the carnival's very own mistress! If you manage to take away those 41 mischievous visitors who never came out, you can win great prizes!

Besides these exclusive entertainment facilities, Magician Casiah will usher you into a spectacular world of revelry, featuring sawing-in-half illusions, human vanishings, extreme escapes, and more magic! Lucky audience members may even be invited on stage to experience Master Casiah's exquisitely refined cutting techniques up close and personal. Guaranteed to shatter your perception of reality and render your ordinary daily life utterly flavorless! And best of all? Every last bit of it is absolutely free—FREE! Your joy is all the reward Master Casiah could ever ask for!

To all at the Mythag—Master Casiah will be waiting for you this weekend on the open ground behind the cafeteria. Don't you dare miss it!

Note: Once entering the carnival, attendees must fully experience it; mid-way exits are not allowed. Those with low stress tolerance or fragile mental and cardiac conditions should enter with extreme caution.

The carnival is not responsible for any symptoms such as loss of appetite, missing limbs, lost eyes, or abdominal ruptures that occur afterward."

—<Italic:Grand Opening: Master Casiah’s Magical Carnival!>

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
From her childhood, Casiah exhibited an extraordinary talent for mimicry.

No matter how intricate the dance, she could replicate it flawlessly after just one viewing; no matter how complex the magic trick, she could master it with only one lesson. Voice, facial expressions, even smiles and the subtle aura a person carried—Casiah could perfectly replicate them, even to the point of being utterly indistinguishable from the original. Had she been born into different circumstances, or found a different calling, that gift might have carried her toward an entirely different life.

Unfortunately, she was just a child growing up in an obscure, low-rent circus. The circus people only thought of profiting from her talent, while the patrons outside the tent—they came only to purchase joy, with no pity to spare.

No one cared for Casiah's happiness, but fortunately, Casiah did not care either. Every time she observed the laughing audience, the bickering troupe members, the fortune teller silently weeping over her photos, she felt only a detached curiosity: Why do they make these faces off-stage? Why do they keep performing when no one is watching? Why do they call it a "manifestation of emotion"?

What is happiness? What is sadness? And what does it feel like to experience the despair and terror of impending death, just as the "benefactor" who slit her throat once spoke of?

As a human, she could find no answers. But as a child of magic, as a being capable of collecting "emotions" from others, perhaps she could finally gain an experience she had never possessed.

Thus, she founded the Magical Carnival and brought it around the world.

People come to purchase joy, yet pay with every last desire.

"Roll up, roll up, come one, come all—step into my carnival! For just a little joy, just a little sorrow, you'll witness the greatest spectacle this century has ever seen!"

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
Casiah reached into the hat, and it was empty.

Casiah reached into the Gate, and it was empty.

Casiah reached into her chest, and it was empty.

The collected joy and sorrow, fear and fury, the warmth and chill of human connection, the buzz before the show began, the cheers at each dramatic twist, the whistles at the highlights, the applause at the final bow, and the hollow silence as the crowd dispersed—all slipped away from this hollow chest, leaving no trace of ever having existed.

Staring into the mirror, Casiah began to mimic the audience's expressions. The wrinkles at the corners of her eyes, the flexing of her cheeks, the exact curve of her lips—everything was identical to theirs, yet utterly devoid of any true sentiment.

<Italic:If only I could feel it... If only I could transcend mere mimicry... If only I could become one of them... Or, if only someone... could stay...>
Then surely this "void" in her chest would finally be filled.

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
If born into an ordinary family, Castor might have grown into a modest young man as warm and steady as a tree. But now, he is the only one among the twins who retained a complete body and soul; he remains silent like a stone, waiting to bury that ember the two of them shared in their youth deep within, never giving up, never wavering.
Those already matured wings, capable of stirring up a storm, are now retracted in dormancy, as a bird quietly awaits the moment the cage door opens to once again soar in the sky.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
While carrying out a mission on a remote, barren, and little-known plateau far from Londinium, I happened upon an astonishing account in a mountain village with only a handful of residents remaining.

On the night the monster appeared, the sky itself seemed shrouded by an eerie shadow. Fog rolled across the ground, and deep within the clouds, a dim green hue emerged—this was by no means a mere natural phenomenon, but the projection of something alive, something breathing.

From deep within the desolate mountains, bristling with tall trees, a sudden roar—a howling shockwave—erupted. That shriek, belonging to no known creature, stirred fear from the deepest recesses of human instinct.

A massive shadow swept swiftly overhead. The entire mountain shuddered beneath that sky-blotting form, and every branch and leaf trembled in unison, producing a synchronized, whisper-like rustling.

<Italic:"I saw it! Those long, densely packed tentacles, those eyes glowing green—that was without question the source of the horror in the sky. It discovered me, even locked its gaze firmly on me! I truly thought my life would end at that very moment, but perhaps it had just finished a full meal. Before I blacked out from suffocation, it mercifully turned and left.">

This is the only interview with a confirmed eyewitness. The villager, still deeply mired in nightmares to this day, refused to recall further details. However, from the available evidence, this massive dark-green monster—aside from destroying part of the mountain forest like a passing hurricane and leaving behind a few beast skeletons with only traces of blood remaining—showed no greater aggression, behaving much like a predator feeding normally. Perhaps its approach toward the village was driven by nothing more than idle curiosity.

But in the face of any unknown horror, we must prepare for the worst. I will continue my investigation on the @3 Plateau for a period of half a month. Should any other noteworthy signs of danger arise, I will append them to the mission report at once.— Excerpt from <Italic:"Mythag Overseas Investigation Notes, A.F.3@2 Annual Compendium">

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
The experience of interacting with Castor often reveals two strikingly contrasting extremes.

At first glance, his overly serious and composed demeanor closely resembles that of a middle-aged clerk who has spent twenty years working at Londinium Bank: rigid, unromantic, drained of all vitality by monotonous work. When he frowns, he indeed carries a saint-like presence—calm yet exuding authority without raising his voice.

However, upon deeper interaction, you'll discover that all his seemingly conservative behaviors stem from an extremely limited knowledge base and an unparalleled level of bluntness, to the point where he takes any joke directed at him completely seriously.

He often clutches a thick notebook, ceaselessly questioning the Keeper as if he were a toddler still learning to speak. Faced with such earnest and sincere gaze, most people find it difficult to express disdain for those naive questions.

Beyond scriptures related to various beliefs, Castor is insatiably curious about any new knowledge, especially regarding modern society and science; he has even developed a strong interest in experimental research. After being ruthlessly ignored by Doll: Inferno, he turned to relentlessly pursue poor Winkle, who tries to escape from him daily.

If he were in a school classroom, he would be the kind of diligent student adored by teachers—he does not see studying as a burden, but rather views the freedom to absorb interesting knowledge as a heartfelt joy.

However, while the teacher might feel content, some boastful Awakeners become infuriated when faced with his endless logical inquiries, unable to answer them, leaving behind a bewildered Castor reflecting on the profound difficulty of learning and the long road ahead.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
What is the price of pursuing freedom and escaping the church? The twins anticipated horrifying punishments, even the loss of their own lives, but they never expected that the most painful thing was never the physical torture, but the flaying of the soul.

Castor stared with bloodshot eyes as Pollux's treasured, lively and magnificent wings were brutally torn off. His own lips were bitten raw, and he waited in madness and guilt, craving for the same pain to befall him.

However, Juliette merely waved her hand, and the severely injured Castor was taken down like a broken sack, thrown into a pool filled with d-slime for the "sin-effacement rite."

The black, viscous slime soaked his injured body, seeping into every wound and covering every feather, making it even harder to breathe.

In the cycle of wounds repeatedly corroding and healing, the image of the torn-out wings spiraled in Castor's dazed mind. He sat in the small cage in agony, wishing he could bear all the torment for his brother. He wished he had been the one to have his wings pulled out that day, yet later he resolutely thought that he must use these wings to fly with his brother towards freedom again.

Castor endured day after day in this hellish pool; time became unperceivable through pain. It felt like waiting for dozens of years, waiting until Castor nearly died again, before he finally crawled out from that dark hell. The eager eyes he faced were met with a cold and disdainful gaze.

"Stop looking at me with that disgusting look! Let me give you another piece of advice, Lord Castor. You and I are merely serving as the Twin Divi of the Lightbearer together. Leave me alone unless you have a serious matter to discuss. It gets annoying, you know?"

Castor did not understand why his brother had completely forgotten him, but he finally realized the meaning of Juliette's deeply meaningful gaze when he left the pool of sin—because she now tightly held the collar that could control him, a guarantee of her absolute confidence.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
Twins are born with nothing but each other, yet Castor continues to savor the taste of loss. Hurt, forgotten, and betrayed—his silent heart is not made of iron, yet he keeps getting back up.

"But it's okay. I'll hold on to your share too," Castor said, looking at his disfigured brother with blind faith. In his heart, he clutches tightly to that faint flame, tirelessly resisting the knife-like wind and snow.

One day, he will climb to the peak of freedom and use his wings to touch the sky's low-hanging curtain. He believes that at the end of that thorny path must lie the bright daylight his younger brother promised him in childhood.

voiceLines.title: Awaken
voiceLines.content: Greetings. I am Castor... Was there more I should say? Forgive me—words don't come easily. If you need anything, just ask.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: I
voiceLines.content: These dark feathers grow heavier each day.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: II
voiceLines.content: Will these cursed wings ever find the strength to take flight again...

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: III
voiceLines.content: Thank you... for the key to my freedom. For letting me grasp my own fate.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Observe
voiceLines.content: When we were children, the rules weren't this strict. Sometimes, Pollux would go off and say something, and magically get a handful of candies. That sweetness... it feels like this moment now.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Ponder
voiceLines.content: Theology lessons under Albino and the Light Watch filled our days. I dreamed of shorter scriptures—fewer verses to stumble over, fewer reprimands.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Reflect
voiceLines.content: The High Priestess... Juliette. She was gentle with us then. Her warm smiles made disobedience unthinkable. A pat on the head silenced all protests. We didn't want to let her down. Yeah, don't worry, I don't feel that way anymore... You may pat my head instead.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight
voiceLines.content: Even before that book, we wondered about the world beyond the lake's island, the scarlet walls. Yet when Pollux suffered, I didn't resist. I lack his courage. Unlike Pollux, I am much more cowardly and clumsy.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate
voiceLines.content: So much unseen... so much undone. Those desolate deep green lakes and the thick fog that lingers on will no longer hold us back. Oceans, cities, farms from the book's pages... I'll see them. With Pollux. With you.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Florish
voiceLines.content: These wings are fully grown now. So sturdy, so powerful. Now I can carry both Pollux and you. Call for me when you wish to fly.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: I
voiceLines.content: Your generosity unsettles me. The expensive books, the meteorite crystals you gave me... is there a price? Sorry, please forgive my suspicion. I shouldn't doubt you like this.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II
voiceLines.content: We weren't allowed to talk to other people since childhood. "Friend" was a foreign concept to me... until recently. Pollux and I were everything to each other: brothers, friends, fellow prisoners, each other's only solace. Now... perhaps I should make some new friends.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content: How should friends get along? Pollux likes ordering me around when he could do those things himself. And I'm willing to help him with those tasks, it's our way of hanging out together. If you want, I'll do something for you too.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content: Do I... sound stupid? Sorry, please forgive my ignorance. My knowledge begins and ends with the Lantern's doctrines. Teach me your likes and dislikes—I'll commit them to memory.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content: When you hear the leaves rustling in the trees, you'll know I'm by your side.

voiceLines.title: Chat: Touch
voiceLines.content: Would you like to touch my feathers? Sure, go ahead. Should I extend them further?

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Crisis
voiceLines.content: I was immersed in that black, sticky ooze for a long, long time—so long that I forgot about time itself, so long that even Pollux forgot about me. It didn't bring physical pain... just dread, watching my soul dissolve away.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Mythag
voiceLines.content: A school without Theology? Where you choose lessons... skip them? It sounds like a dream.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Like
voiceLines.content: Sorry, I didn't mean to zone out... You asked me what this feather is? This is... His most prized thing... and now mine. Do you like it? It's pretty, right?

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Hate
voiceLines.content: What I covet most is how you effortlessly trust your companions. Being forgotten... betrayed... the wounds never fade.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Keeper
voiceLines.content: Could you teach me how to trade? How to exchange items and how to manage the currency obtained—it's truly a profound subject. Gaining freedom is just the start; Pollux and I still have a lot to learn to live independently. May I rely on you?

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Jenkin
voiceLines.content: That master thief offered to teach me the best survival skills for just five hundred Leonian Florins... Have I been deceived? No, I believe this is knowledge worth learning, and it's precisely what Pollux and I are lacking... Is it a money issue? I understand. Then, how about I go negotiate with her and pay her four hundred and fifty Leonian Florins instead?

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Doresain
voiceLines.content: Ah, I heard he's a master chef... The knowledge of making food is indeed very necessary. Although I'm not that particular about food, Pollux is extremely picky. I should find some time to learn from him... I shouldn't go? Why? The food that mister makes looks delicious though.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Daffodil
voiceLines.content: A store that can fulfill any wish, overflowing with countless treasures... It makes one hesitate to approach. Not that I doubt the lady's power, but "to obtain something, one must pay the corresponding price"—this is a lesson Pollux and I have learned through bitter experience, time and again.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Karen
voiceLines.content: Now that I reflect on it, the maids carrying lanterns weren't so different from Pollux and me. We all lived shackled by invisible chains, quietly submitting to our fate. Yet that green maid... she was different. There was a lightness to her, as if she genuinely took pleasure in her duties. Maybe... maybe she had already discovered true freedom.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Pollux
voiceLines.content: Pollux... The Lantern filled his mind with poisonous ideas, but he's actually kind. It's not that he's selfish... He's just terrified. Terrified of losing the Lantern's approval, of vanishing without that fragile sense of identity. His desperation to please them... it's the panic of someone clinging to the only "self" he's ever known.

voiceLines.title: Investigation Begins
voiceLines.content: Witness this will of mine—this hunger for freedom.

voiceLines.title: Investigation Success
voiceLines.content: At last... I've seen the stars from those pages.

voiceLines.title: Investigation Halted
voiceLines.content: Guess I never... made it out, huh...

voiceLines.title: Skill: II
voiceLines.content: Wind, carry them to death's maw!

voiceLines.title: Special Skill: I
voiceLines.content: Vanish with the wind!

voiceLines.title: Rouse
voiceLines.content: All birds find their sky eventually.

voiceLines.title: Exalt
voiceLines.content: You can't destroy me!

voiceLines.title: Over-Exalt
voiceLines.content: Let the Cataclysm come. This immortal flesh will stand unbroken!

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
Her ethereal beauty is always reminiscent of the bird of heaven, spreading its glossy wings towards utopia as her white dress flutters with caressing breezes.

However, does the girl who perches on the mast ever imagine herself flying in the azure sky?

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
On July 3, A.F.3@1, being invited by the Nathaniel Forbes Green Foundation, Mythag University participated in the investigation towards the "ghost ship" Sona-Nyl.

Upon boarding the barque which had been declared sunk ten years ago, the communication signal from investigator Fingal Johansen had immediately out of reach.

On July 10, A.F.3@1, the university eventually managed to get him. Located at the northern shore of Leo Heights with 300 nautical miles away from the original destination, investigator Johansen declared that he lost sense of time and space at the second he stepped on Sona-Nyl, and could not recall anything that happened onboard.

Investigator Johansen can hitherto only vaguely remember a word: Elysian.

Due to the unharmful nature of the ghost ship itself, Mythag University decide to terminate the investigation today (A.F.3@1 year, December 24).

"File: Investigation of the Sona-Nyl Crash."

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Grabbed by Doll upon the moment of joining the university, Celeste has undergone a series of comprehensive assessment.

As an Awakener summoned from non-standard process, Celeste's mental state is incredibly stable. However, neither her spirit intensity nor her Gnostic index which evaluates the strength of slivercore meets the Awakener's standard.

Yet she still emerged into this world as an Awakener, like a flower with invisible petals brusts in abysmal nothingness.

Although no abnormalities has shown in daily activities or field missions, data record reveals Celeste's concerning situation: her will, already faint, continues to evansce.

By now, the Awakening Department is organizing a small order to sustain Celeste's existence by supplying religious belief. Those who are interested in joining and proficient in aquatic activities could contact Teacher Sylvia for further infomation.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
On the thirty-first day following the celestial bird, Sona-Nyl sails into a sea shrouded by streaming mist.

Celeste perches high on the mast, gazing upon her people below. Notes of the lutanist drift in sweet melodies. Songs praying for a smooth journey echo betwixt.

She does not aware of their destination, nor does she evaluate how much wealth and fame bestowing across the sea. She does not care whether the prayers are pious, nor does she unsettled by the rumors about her power, circulating surreptitiously around the sea. Being asked to bless the voyage, she does not need words to complete her duty.

And when the music ceases and the mist lifts, the sailors behold only a resistless raging sea. Lightning tears through the sky. Black rain pours down, bursting thunders of gigantic spray. Rushing torrent captures the fragile barque and throws it into the gaping abyss.

"God has forsaken us!" Kindreds scream in desperation. Bellows imprison her into the lightless dungeon.

Neglected and derelicted, the protector is left alone unquestioned with her failed duty, and one last lingering confusion.

Why... why did the barque sink?

The chain that once manacled her to the mast drown into the roaring splash. She plummets into the depth...

Like a white bird with snapped wings flaking from the sky.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
Our good friend, the resourceful Hannah Peaslee, somehow dug up the research materials on Celeste. Thanks to this audacious reporter, both the originally confidential materials and her brief interview with Celeste has now spreaded into every corner.

After reading the confidential materials, Hannah posed a question to her usually emotionless face.

"Most Awakeners have unfulfilled wishes, which lie in their basic motivations for cooperating with the university. However, your wish section is blank in this material. Don't you have any desire to accomplish anything? Or what is your meaning as an Awakener?"

"I have, I do have."

The girl's expression showed no cracks, as ethereal and noble as usual. If it were not for that brief answer and the anxiety within, the reporter would have almost thought that she miss the question.


"I will find my wish... everyone wishes so. Therefore I will find it."

Her soft voice resounded, delicate and fragile like an easily shattered dream.

voiceLines.title: Awaken
voiceLines.content: My name is Celeste. I'll always be here, as long as you still need me.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: I
voiceLines.content: As you wished, my existence has grown more tangible.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: II
voiceLines.content: It has arrived... the white bird circling in my dream.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: III
voiceLines.content: Hmm... the sea water is quite warm tonight...

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Observe
voiceLines.content: Do you wish for me to set sail once more? I am willing to do so... if you do not mind my past failure.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Ponder
voiceLines.content: I seem to hear the rowers' shanties again... and sense the familiar scent of home.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Reflect
voiceLines.content: Please follow the trail of the birds of paradise; the destination awaits ahead in the azure blue.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight
voiceLines.content: The destination, be it treasure or port, makes no difference to me. My purpose is only to ensure your safe return.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate
voiceLines.content: Thanks to your favor, even the raging seas now feel less daunting. I shall brave them to bring you my steadfast blessings.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Florish
voiceLines.content: I often gaze at the horizon, imagining the scenes on that distant land—the one I draw closer to but can never reach. If that day ever comes, please come with me to see it.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: I
voiceLines.content: Duty and destiny are much alike. Neither can be easily cast aside, nor is there any need to cast them aside.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II
voiceLines.content: My past was routine and calm, like the seas near the equator; there is nothing worth mentioning.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content: My wish? Ensuring safe and peaceful voyage—does that not suffice? I have never had any other wishes... but I will consider it carefully and tell you later.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content: Miss Ramona once said that I don't need to accommodate everyone. I do not understand... Does it mean my protection is no longer needed?

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content: I was brought to the ship and entrusted with the mission of the ship's maiden many years ago. Since then, my life—and its meaning—have been beyond my control. I've been told that I should live for my own wishes, at least in this second life as an Awakener... Would you help me? Help me become selfish, help me find my own wish.

voiceLines.title: Chat: Touch
voiceLines.content: Would you like to sink together with me?

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Past
voiceLines.content: Ah... Are you talking to me? My apologies, I was lost in memories of the view back when I was bound to the mast. Would you mind repeating your question?

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Miryam
voiceLines.content: Blessing the voyage for most people makes no difference to me... except for that woman. If possible, please arrange another route for me.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Faros
voiceLines.content: That would be a dangerous person to have on board... No, I mean purely from a navigation safety perspective...

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Dissolution
voiceLines.content: I was punished for failing to protect the sailors, who were lost to their families forever. They named me the chief culprit of the tragedy... Is this what Dissolution is?

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Mythag
voiceLines.content: Thanks to Miss Hannah, I was able to observe the choir practice. Hymns and sea shanties are quite different; during my years of blessing voyages, I've never heard such a unique melody...

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Like
voiceLines.content: The full moon's golden light always enchants me: beneath it, the sea catches the light and shimmers beautifully as the mysterious, gentle wind blows, weaving a romantic and dreamlike vision.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Hate
voiceLines.content: It's getting a bit noisy... are those the students? They are much like albatrosses, you see? They have endless vitality, as if their journey never ends...

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Keeper
voiceLines.content: My relationship with you is like that of a sail and a ship. Without the ship, the sail shouldn't exist; without the sail, the ship can hardly voyage far. Is that not true?

voiceLines.title: Investigation Begins
voiceLines.content: Souls without protection, I shall grant you final peace.

voiceLines.title: Investigation Success
voiceLines.content: Everything went well. You may raise the triumphant sails.

voiceLines.title: Investigation Halted
voiceLines.content: So my protection, too, may fail at times...

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
Everyone wears a mask; she chose the one that numbs the heart best—

She smiles gently, she speaks gently, and every look and every word lands exactly where it needs to, until the patients who come to her for counseling believe with all their hearts that they have found the one person who understands them, the one who will show them the way.
That is enough.

A moth doomed to burn does not need to know how it ends. It only needs to keep following where she leads.

And inside that warmth that looks so much like salvation, the fire takes hold, and there is no turning back.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
I don't believe Robert put a gun in his mouth. No. I don't believe it.
He was decorated for valor. He closed murder cases nobody else could crack. He was a veteran agent with an iron will. And he was getting married soon—the two of them loved each other. So there has to be something behind this. Someone killed him and dressed it up as a suicide.
Whoever did it, I will find them, and I will make them pay. I owe him that as his brother, and as an agent.
...
The scene gave me nothing, so I came back to our hometown—the last place Robert went before he died. After asking around, I learned he had gone up into the mountains.
As for why, I suspect it has to do with the local custom: every family's firstborn is taken into the mountains by their parents for the coming-of-age rite.
Our parents moved away when we were still children, so Robert never went through it. I think the weight of starting a family of his own woke some old sense of obligation in him.
Either way, I'm going up there. I set out the moment I finish writing this.
...
There is a vast structure cut into the mountain. I can't tell what age it belongs to. I can't tell anything about it. All I know is that the rituals here have never once stopped. The severed limbs, the pupae—ugh. I can't write any more.
...
These pupae... no. No. That isn't my grandmother, my grandfather, the people my family came from... I can't have a monster's blood in me. Aaah—
...
...The monsters at the ritual have found me. They mean to make me one of them!
...
If anyone finds this, kill me. Now, right now...@2
...
Praise be to great @2, hssss @2... praise the blind and idiot @4... hss hss hss... @1 hssss...
—Excerpted, with omissions, from the diary of the late Agent @3

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
"Thank you, Clementine. I feel so much better. You understand me better than anyone in the world."
The Keeper hears something like that almost every time they pass Clementine's counseling room. However the patients and Awakeners look going in, they come out light on their feet and smiling.
Once, walking by, the Keeper even caught her counseling a stray cat that had wandered in by mistake.
The results speak for themselves. Everyone who sits down with her comes away singing her praises, and her influence spreads fast. It also brings complications—
"Good afternoon, Keeper."
Clementine is waiting with a smile on the one road you have to take, and you aren't surprised. That communicator of hers, ringing and ringing, says everything. Her patients trust her completely, and somewhere along the way they became her eyes and ears, helping her get what she wants, one way or another.
"I'd wager that if you decided to run this city, your patients would hand you the mayor's chair without asking a single question."
Clementine only smiles the joke away.
"None of that interests me."
And it truly doesn't. Which is a mercy.
Otherwise the dark little things confessed in that room would be enough to tear the city apart.
"For now, the only secrets I want are the ones buried deepest in you, Keeper."

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
The truth is that the real Clementine died the instant that great, long-dead will took her as its host.
What broke from the cocoon on that altar of blood and torn flesh was something newborn—great in essence, far beyond any human life.
A new life with old memories. A body grown on this planet, a soul born in the depths of the universe.
The contradiction bewildered her, but not for long. The hunger in that soul soon left no room for thought.
Human food was tasteless. Only memories of suffering went down at all, and the more torment and despair they held, the sweeter they were.
That was the moment she understood how she was meant to live.
"Tell me. The pain, the despair—show me all of it."
She sat behind her desk, watching each patient with pure malice, her face so gentle that anyone would lower their guard.
Camouflage. The mask an insect wears when it hunts.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
At first the smallest scraps of suffering were enough for her.
Then the craving for something sweeter began to seep into her sessions, a little more malice folded in each time.
It gathered like a river and broke its banks, and it drowned one island of a mind after another.
And still it wasn't enough. Nowhere near enough.
Only when that ancient dream wakes will the whole world become an ocean of pain, and the joy of it be complete.
So she burns, she prays, she waits.
When everything falls into chaos, she will bow her head and savor the purest grief this world can offer.
Even if that ocean drowns her too.

voiceLines.title: Awaken
voiceLines.content: Forgive my intrusion, I simply sensed a low psychological energy and came to check on you. Now, Keeper, shall we embark on a journey through your mind?

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: I
voiceLines.content: If you seek my thoughts, you may be disappointed. I'm better at listening than I am at offering commentary.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: II
voiceLines.content: Ah, I heard His voice... those murmurs, every syllable filled with the utmost agony.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: III
voiceLines.content: I will remember the pain of this moment... recalling and savoring it again and again.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Observe
voiceLines.content: Psychiatrists once cured patients by drilling open their skulls with a trepanation technique... Please, relax. That was long ago. We have since developed far more methods to delve into the mind.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Ponder
voiceLines.content: First, let's listen to some music. How do you like this melody? Soothing and gentle. Now, let your body and mind resonate with the music, entering a state of spiritual relaxation.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Reflect
voiceLines.content: Your vision is probably filled with bizarre hallucinations now, which is quite normal. Draw them out, and your subconscious and instincts will reveal everything.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight
voiceLines.content: Next is Philip Pinel's moral therapy. You must express your innermost desires and fears. It's a necessary procedure to unshackle the mind and restore dormant humanity.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate
voiceLines.content: Remember those fears, detail your feelings of pain. The essence of emotional impact therapy is to face pain directly and conquer it. Here, I'll wipe away your tears. Take your time. Tell me those memories in detail...

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Florish
voiceLines.content: Congratulations, you have been healed. Yes, those hallucinations and illusions are normal; they are proof of your recovery.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: I
voiceLines.content: Weavers, lawyers, barons... I'll never turn a patient away for a fee. To me, they are all merely patients in need of healing.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II
voiceLines.content: Poor Mr. White. His family kept him in a pigpen because asylums in the neighborhood were full. I treated him for free, and after that, he finally realized he was a person, not livestock. He then reclaimed his dignity, with his own hands.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content: Hydrotherapy, electroconvulsive therapy, restraining therapy... those are not treatments, but torture. So, I've been treating the patients in those hospitals my way, pro bono. Eventually, they all achieved recovery and found true freedom.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content: These patients have given me beautiful memories. Next, it's your turn, Keeper. I've already chosen a perfect ending for you. It will be the most exquisite consultation of my career.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content: I admit I underestimated you. Your existence is pain itself. This time, there's no need for follow-up visits. I want to stay by your side and see the outcome firsthand.

voiceLines.title: Chat: Touch
voiceLines.content: To understand each other, one must open their heart. Touch here, and my silver heart will open for you.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Crisis
voiceLines.content: Mental illness is not exclusive to this era; it transcends time and space. Dissolution is the same. Both transcend the boundaries of human cognition, don't they?

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Mythag
voiceLines.content: This place is filled with traces of history, and to some extent, history represents memories... painful memories of the departed.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Like
voiceLines.content: A dark room, all alone, along with the countless painful whispers constantly echoing in my mind... this is the best way to enjoy time.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Hate
voiceLines.content: A numb soul holds no interest for me. Their souls are already dead. No matter how much one stirs them, there will not be a ripple.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Keeper
voiceLines.content: As a fragment of that existence, you carry Their scent... A beautiful scent, filled with pain. It makes any memory of yours taste incredibly delicious.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Aurita
voiceLines.content: Though it may be impolite to say, talking to that child only bores me. You can only ever see one expression... a smile.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Aigis
voiceLines.content: Aigis looks much brighter now. Of course, if my little guest needs help, I'm happy to offer it. I mean, genuine help.

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
She is the flag that flutters high as the ship sails, guiding its course; she is also the dirge that holds to its duty until the very last moment, when the ship sinks beneath the waves.

Her responsibility, her duty, her life—all are bound to the ship; nothing else remains.

For guiding the course is the very meaning of her existence.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
No one knows where that ghost ship lies, nor can anyone confirm whether "it" truly exists. The only clue I have is that ivory head sculpture, which seems to possess some sort of strange magic.

Ever since I came into possession of it, I have had the same dream every night—yes, the dream of that ghost ship, drifting somewhere unknown. Its hull burns with a glimmer that writhes like a living thing, as though opening a gateway to dimensions beyond mortal reach. Upon waking, I can still recall those blasphemous, pathological whispers.

How I wish I were mad, or that I could forget those bizarre sounds—sounds that no human throat could ever produce. But I cannot.

That cursed dream, that cursed flicker of intellect, torment me without rest. And so I must find "it," led by the ivory sculpture. Frtunately, the professors from Miskatonic will walk this road with me, and together we shall seek out the ghost ship and the St. Elmo's Fire—that is what they call the writhing glimmer.

Wish me luck. May the Lord watch over us.

—Excerpt from <Italic:Miskatonic Supernatural Phenomena Investigation Archives>

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Corposant's daily schedule is very fixed; you just need to be at a specific place at a specific time to find her.

Generally speaking, Corposant gets up at 6:00, takes a cold bath, and does exercises. 7:00 is breakfast time, and besides oatmeal and pickled fish, a large amount of caffeine supplements is also required.

From 9:00 to 12:00, it is Corposant's study time; she will revise nautical charts or calibrate equipment during this period. When the class bell rings, Corposant will come outdoors, waving a flag as a traffic officer, which greatly alleviates the road congestion during lunch.

Corposant's lunch time depends on the "traffic conditions, " but no later than 12: 30. After a short break, at 14:00, Corposant will appear at the seaside on time, observing wind direction and weather. At this point, attention should be paid to the movements of Corposant, Faros, and Celeste, to avoid them "commandeering" the museum model ships or luring passersby out to sea.

Dinner time is at 19:00. To numb her sleep cycle, completely destroyed by long-term sailing, Corposant needs to consume a large amount of alcohol and sleep-inducing tinctures. Only in this way can she successfully fall asleep at 22:00; otherwise, she will force herself to stay awake to deal with possible "accidents" during the voyage.

Consequently, situations resulting from this include, but are not limited to, the phenomenon of St. Elmo's fire going out of control, leading to the entire area shining like daylight, or abnormal, uncontrolled area voltage, machinery running erratically, fires, etc.

<Red:Note, during this time absolutely do not let Erica and Corposant come into contact with each other!>

Finally, a criticism notification:

After Corposant's arrival, Winkle made several attempts to extract and study @2 at Corposant's chest as a light source. A verbal criticism has been issued; if any abnormalities are found, be sure to inform the Keeper in time.

—Keeper %player%

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
Before learning to speak, having grown up on a cruise ship, Corposant could already mimic the rhythm of waves crashing against the ship.

Sometimes the rhythm was "splash, " sometimes it was "boom, " like a lullaby sung by nature, making her feel secure, making her feel familiar, making her yearn.

She always understood the "mood" of the sea quicker than others, always read the "language" of the clouds quicker than others, and everyone said she was a natural "navigator."

In reality, when she first heard the term, young Corposant couldn't understand. She only instinctively wanted to help the captain and sailors who took her in, wanting them to return home safely, not to be lost to storms or disasters from other ships.

The navigator who understood her wish said, "Become a navigator, Corposant, become a navigator, fulfill your duty, and then your wish will come true."

The naive Corposant nodded, and thus, that navigator became her mentor. He taught her how to observe the stars, how to calibrate the sextant, and told her the ballads passed down through generations of navigators, those ominous ballads.

"I don't want to be embraced by saltwater, that's too cold, nor do I want to become phosphorescence." Young Corposant objected.

Her mentor didn't teach her anything further, just touched her head and smiled.

Because time will teach her the meaning of the "navigator's" duty—

She is the sole guide on the vast ocean, the only hope.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
Until the last moment, Corposant was diligently fulfilling her duties, yet the ship she piloted still sank.

Every night, she dreams of those lost passengers: water flooding into the cabins, sea monsters' Tentacles rampaging, people drowning, jumping overboard, kneeling for one last guidance, but hope was lost.

This brutal reality reproaches her, tortures her—she has desecrated her profession.

For this, she must be punished, and the lightning that eternally entwines and torments her is the retribution. But it's not enough; she must atone for her negligence.

Fortunately, the great entity provided the answer: when the Divine Realm descends, the world will become paradise.

"So, to quell the eternal roaring of the sea, for the innocent buried at sea, for guiding the direction of all beings, I request the Divine Realm's arrival."

This is her last, final navigation.
