storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
"Welcome to Lady Daffodil's Exchange Shop. We barter goods and collect heads. Our rates are perfectly fair—fair to all, no deception."

Amidst the swirling gray mist, the woman gently tapped the ash from her antique wooden pipe. Beneath the swaying brim of her hat, a flickering smile hovered at the corners of her lips, laced with ambiguity.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
Daffodil sold herself to the Silver Core Research Laboratory of Mythag University at a staggering price.

Before that, the laboratory head Doll had repeatedly expressed strong dissatisfaction with the one-way communications that only Daffodil could initiate.

But only Daffodil and a certain deceased high-ranking member of Mythag University know how such a "one-way communication" was established through a dangerous transaction.

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Daffodil's whereabouts at Mythag University are nothing short of ghostly. After all, she possesses taboo knowledge of interdimensional travel, allowing her to come and go as she pleases, entirely unfettered by Black Pool's Silver Core Hub.

She routinely deals in mysterious instruments and materials of dubious origin, and sometimes assists other Awakeners in briefly evading the oversight of Mythag University.

Later, through negotiations, she opened her own "Worry-Relief Shop" in a disused room beside the infirmary on campus.

Of course, all goods for sale must first be registered and vetted by Mythag University.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
On a street corner in a port city sat a tiny exchange shop, run by a proprietor skilled in handling mysterious events.

Not long after the flood, Daffodil—who was not yet known as Daffodil at the time—arrived near St. Peidro. Soon after her arrival, victims of the "mysterious head disappearance" began to surface throughout the harbor city.

The owner investigated, tracked it down, and after exhausting every measure to subdue it, struck a bargain with it. The shopkeeper promised it her own head upon her death, but until then, it must serve as her assistant and could no longer hunt at will.

And so the creature, after a thousand years of wandering, began to work and live by her side.

It had once immersed itself in the memories of countless heads, tasting both fleeting joy and festering resentment. But this absurd happiness was merely a pastime to while away its prolonged existence, masking the profound, drifting loneliness.

Only while accompanying the shopkeeper did it experience genuine friendship for the very first time. It realized that infinite heads offered nothing but a hollow comfort; only true human connection could fill its perpetual void.

However, this brief happiness lasted less than ten years. The shopkeeper, who had never once set aside her work, passed away unexpectedly.

And so it severed her head, inheriting her appearance, shop, and name, becoming "Daffodil."

From that day forward, Daffodil embarked on a journey with her little exchange shop. She continues to claim heads as payment from those who seek her help, keeping them as private collectibles.

But she never hunted at will again.

Never again.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
In the gray, viscous Sea of Primordial Essence, emptiness prevails; the notions shared by travelers crossing dimensions remain confined to abstract descriptions and imagination.

It wants to confirm with its own eyes the "places of human yearning," to witness the magnificent wonders of the mortal world, and to experience the bittersweet nuances of human love and loss.

Yet above all, it desires a specific person, someone to cherish, someone to trust.

A fair trade means equality, detachment, and accounts settled—not a fraction more is paid, nor a fraction less taken. But it yearns for something different—an unconditional trust to bridge the divide, to break through cautious probe, to thaw the lingering ice.

It had found that, then lost it. But it would find it again.

Oh dear... what you wish for comes at quite a price, doesn't it?

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Florish

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content: Oh, curious about my secret? This name, this body, this face, this voice—they all came from a woman from San Pedro, to whom one of my skulls once belonged. She struck a deal with me... After her death, I became her. As for her whereabouts... well, that is my most exquisite collection, you know.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content: I wasn't always like this; she gave me a new life. In that sense, you have also given me a second life, so I will treasure your head as well.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content: Seeing how hard you're working, I almost feel guilty about collecting my reward too soon. So, I'll allow your head to stay where it is for now. But don't forget, it's already reserved as my personal property, okay?

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Mythag
voiceLines.content: My shop exists in any dimension, any location in the universe, and of course, it can be here. Besides, I like those careless children in Mythag.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Like

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Hate

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
Flasks must be washed until they look new. A bench scorched in an experiment must be sanded until it shines. The balance is recalibrated every third day. Her zeal and reverence for science, for the secrets of the world, make her expect as much from everyone and everything around her.
Herself included, of course—after all, not everyone can embrace death calmly and ask to be made an Awakener.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
Doll is indispensable to Mythag University, and to the field at large.
Of all the Awakeners in the school's care, she has neither the steadiest Gnosis Index nor the greatest strength in a fight, but she is without question the calmest and most rational of them.
For Awakeners who were once human, the first stretch after "coming back" usually brings confusion, panic, and mania. Doll seems to have skipped that adjustment entirely.
On her second day awake she was back in the laboratory, and within a year she had compiled a technical manual that brought together outer-realm knowledge and human learning.
These days Doll spends half her time advancing Silvercore Technology and the other half "cleaning up after idiot students."
—Incidentally, under the influence of a higher-dimensional presence, Doll wrote that Technical Manual in some unknown language. The translation is proceeding in an orderly fashion, in whatever spare time she has.

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
"Comments with no mercy in them." "Failing papers." "Research reports that don't pass."
In decades of teaching, Doll has signed off on graduation certificates for a handful of students at most. Most give up in the face of her impossible standards and transfer to another professor, and over the years Professor Doll's reputation has spread accordingly.
Still, some students believe the standard is how she picks her disciples: only the most iron-willed deserve to hold the key to the door of truth and walk beside her as she lifts the veil off the world.
So even though the odds of graduating under her are almost nothing, applications to study with Doll keep flying into her office.
Sometimes, when Ramona is pulled in to help read through them, she can't help thinking it isn't such a bad thing that the students believe that.
As far as Ramona can tell, Doll simply holds human students to the standards of an Awakener. Nothing more.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
Doll's arrival was the one moment of glory Mythag University ever had in the eyes of the outside world.
Scholars everywhere lamented that even a talent sent from heaven could not escape worldly chains—that she had let some nobody university buy her for money, and taken on the stink of coin.
While the world tore into her for supposedly selling herself, Doll was getting something at Mythag worth more than gold.
She was allowed past the border of material science, close enough to touch the veil over reality, and beneath that veil lay what she would give her life to reach.
Researching Silvercore Technology is no safer than dancing on a knife's edge, and Doll became its most serious, most tireless, most gifted dancer.
When the D-Mark appeared, the dancer did not stop. She used what time she had left to keep turning, letting her own steps settle and crystallize.
Until the Dissolution Phenomenon wrecked her body, reached her mind, and ate into her reason.
Even then, she was still far too distant from the center of the truth.
And so that star, its flame of life gone dim and its hunger for knowledge still blinding, left these words behind: "Awaken me, before the world forgets me."

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
A new star of science and knowledge rose out of an ordinary working-class family.
Most of Doll's childhood was filled with the pulse of cylinders and the turning of gears.
But a love of machines was never going to carry a girl up the harsh slopes of science.
What set her on the path of knowledge was a plague.
An unknown madness tore through the city. Hospitals overflowed, morgues buckled, and no one felt safe.
"There isn't enough ground in the whole city. Dig up Grandma or burn Mother—you have to pick one."
And so Doll watched her mother disappear into the fire.
Unlike the others burned that day, the handful of bone fragments and ash she had once called "mother" held something more: a shimmering silver mass, still flowing.
"I want to know whether I can ever see her again."
"I want to know whether her kind soul is somewhere inside that."
"I want to know whether that silver is the origin of life, the essence of the soul."
"I want to know whether everything in this world begins from the same point."
Until she has her answers, Doll will not bow to the Dissolution Phenomenon.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV

I wanted to figure out what force is controlling me?" ...Though I find this novel's plot unsatisfying and its fictional science laughably naive, after reading it, you should grasp my motivations... Wait, you haven't read this book?

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
The founder of Necrovia, the eternal king of ghouls. 

His banquet is worthy of the deepest anticipation—grand dining hall, elegant dance, and those exquisite dishes handcrafted from corpses will surely be unforgettable for your entire life.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
The abandoned cemetery in the northwest of London County has been listed as an absolute forbidden zone by local residents since AF 3@2.

According to archived reports from The Times and Scotland Yard's missing persons files, 37 people have gone missing in the thick night fog of the cemetery in recent years, including: Cyril, a habitual grave robber with a taste for noble tombs; Cook, a shivering vagrant seeking shelter; Officer Grayson, who stumbled in during patrol; and White, the Oxford scholar who studied how medieval bones were laid to rest.

All vanished when the fog grew thick, leaving not even a scrap of fabric for search teams to find.

Prior to AF 3@2, the MTC had always treated the area as barely worth noting in their ledgers.

That changed when the Duke of Derbyshire—Samuel Curzon, that notorious patron of unnatural studies—failed to return from his midnight visit.

Royal inquiries have a way of focusing attention, and soon a special operation was mounted.

In July of AF 3@2, Elias ThOrnn led twelve armed agents and three silver-equipped mediums into the cemetery's hungry mists.

Their anti-hypothermia medication hissed in its cases; their directional locators spun like dowsing rods in a haunted well.

After advancing precisely 1.2 kilometers in tight formation, they found it—a hexagonal entrance hidden beneath the shattered statue of the Ghoul King, its stone face worn smooth by centuries of bad weather and worse company.

Five thousand steps down (each counted twice by nervous lips) brought them to the temple.

Where they expected charnel houses and stacked bones, they found instead 800 square meters of impossible precision: floors flatter than mathematics, air cleaner than a surgical theater.

Only the altar broke the perfection—2.3 meters of granite carved with endless thorns, wreathed in black mist that clung like cobwebs to something moving inside.

There knelt the Duke, dressed for dinner but quite dead, showing no marks save those left by perfect preservation.

When the mist was disturbed, he came apart like sugar in tea—dissolving until even the mass spectrometers wept empty data.

Then the mist turned its attention to the living.

Every investigator heard the same voice—cultured, gentle, the sort that might recite poetry before the cutting begins:
"Please do not seek out Necrovia. Please do not disturb the King of the Ghouls during his meal."

"Consider this your final warning."

They awoke outside the rusted gates, equipment intact but all recordings curiously blank.

Later, the MTC chairman and Miskatonic's occult dean would visit, then quietly declare the matter closed.

The cemetery now only punishes those who come seeking secrets; mere wanderers get off with nothing worse than lost hours and strange dreams.

But sometimes, when the fog rolls in particularly thick, the locals swear they can hear something chewing below their feet.

——Investigation Report on the Abandoned Cemetery of Etherington

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
After leaving Necrovia, Doresain demonstrated remarkable adaptability within human society. This was inevitable; for him, human society was not a new beginning, but rather a return.

His speech, mannerisms, demeanor, and etiquette were flawless, maintaining the aura of a monarch while showing none of the arrogance typically festering in those who have held power too long.

Doresain does not avoid social interaction, yet he shows little interest in topics like politics, economics, or academia. The only thing drawing him to such occasions is food.

Beyond mere appreciation of cuisine, Doresain takes visceral pleasure in the kitchen process itself—from ingredient selection and preparation techniques to spice usage and heat control. His vast culinary knowledge and refined taste captivate everyone he converses with.

They come to realize all their previous decades of dining were nothing more than hurried survival, no different from beasts eating merely to stay alive. Even those unfortunate souls born without a sense of taste can experience food's artistry through his descriptions, achieving what he calls "a rebirth of flavor perception."

This revelation is inseparable from Doresain's impeccable manners—he understands with crystal clarity the differences between human and ghoul culinary preferences. He respects these species distinctions and has no desire to impose his own tastes on others.

"Some people always regard difference as heresy," he remarks, the ghost of a smile playing about his lips. "In my city-state, such behavior was considered profoundly inelegant. I celebrate individual differences. It is precisely through these variations that we discover food's greatest beauties."

Then the purple mist around him swirls as he adds, voice dropping to a intimate murmur: "But you are different, Keeper. As such a singular being in this world... I believe you, above all others, might experience unparalleled beauty in the act of eating, just as I do..."

As he speaks these words, Doresain's smile flickers through the violet haze like the grin of some elegant, patient serpent whispering in your ear, waiting to lead you out of—or perhaps into—a very particular Garden of Eden.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
When Doresain awoke in the sunless temple of Necrovia, pain slithered through him like a nest of awakened serpents. The poison's work was unfinished, its blades still carving hymns of agony from his abdomen outward, thorned and relentless. He'd known his father's wine was tainted—had seen the old king's trembling hands, the shadows whispering behind his eyes—yet he drank it anyway, smiling as the bitterness kissed his throat.

Clever. Kind. Unshakable. By every measure, Doresain had been the perfect heir. But in a city where the living called corpse-eating a sin, even princes were not spared the pyre. He'd tried to teach them—the poetry of decay, the sacrament of bones—but understanding was a bridge between worlds, and his family had burned it long ago.

He never expected to open his eyes again. Yet here he was, choking on a new torment. The black mist coiled around him, alive with teeth and hunger, peeling him apart layer by layer. It gnawed. It sculpted. His flesh regrew only to be stripped anew, a grotesque dance of devouring and rebirth. His scream was soundless, lost in the temple's hollow belly.

Then—a flavor. Unimaginable. Divine. Amid the rending and the howling dark, it bloomed on his tongue: the god of Necrovia was feasting on him, and the taste was ecstasy. Pain dissolved. Poison became ambrosia. The god's laughter echoed in his marrow, their suffering and rapture now one and the same.

For seven nights, the feast endured. When Doresain rose at last, the altar's chill still humming in his veins, he felt no rage, no sorrow. Only gratitude. His murderers had given him a gift—the exquisite last meal of his own flesh, the delirious joy of being known.

Beyond the temple, the full moon hung like a bone-white hook. Necrovia knelt in the dark, and its new king smiled.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
He had once believed that his entire life existed for the pursuit of ultimate deliciousness.

The duties of a crown prince, the estrangement from loved ones, the weight of moral teachings... He had cast all this pain aside in his relentless quest for culinary perfection.

From prince to monarch, from mortal to divine, his hunger never waned. He mastered every cooking technique, could detect the most fleeting nuance in every corpse's flavor profile.

He attained everything he desired, yet after each ephemeral moment of satisfaction, that hollow feeling remained - like a flavor just beyond his palate's reach.

It wasn't until he consumed Celina's corpse and glimpsed her lingering soul that understanding came.

The stories etched in flesh before death's arrival, the unfinished yearnings that clung to bones - these were the missing ingredients he'd been chasing, the true essence he'd been tasting without realizing.

"Eating is remembrance; every feast a reunion between departed and living" —these are the words carved into Necrovia's throne. He will grant those who seek his protection remembrance and eternal rest.

voiceLines.title: Awaken
voiceLines.content: Ah, what an unforgettable scent... I simply cannot wait to welcome you into my sanctuary.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: I
voiceLines.content: Your fragrant aroma is positively intoxicating.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: II
voiceLines.content: Thank you so much for your enthusiasm. The honour is all mine.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: III
voiceLines.content: I see more impending deaths. The other side is becoming ever clearer...

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Observe
voiceLines.content: I preside over death, but please, do not misunderstand. I never create it; I merely follow in its wake, harvesting the choicest morsels left behind..

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Ponder
voiceLines.content: I am no barbaric beast who gorges on raw flesh. The consumption of death is a solemn and elegant affair. You must commune with and truly understand each ingredient's unique flavour.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Reflect
voiceLines.content: No perfume compares to the human body's own natural fragrance. To know a person by their scent is a simply divine pleasure.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight
voiceLines.content: Different ingredients demand different preparations. The organs, they need to be marinated. The tendons in the legs are best stewed. Fatty parts are perfect for fermentation and ageing, while the more delicate pieces can be fried, roasted, or even transformed into beautifully sculpted jellies. These choices are all about discretion. For without preserving and accentuating the ingredient's natural flavour, there is no respect.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate
voiceLines.content:
The pairing of dishes also holds great importance.
The juxtaposition of sour with sweet, crisp with tender, light with rich, and delicate with coarse, creates a layered flavour and a textural contrast that leads to different sensations upon entry, mastication, and when savouring the aftertaste.
This is the endless and wondrous pleasure a proper meal provides.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Florish
voiceLines.content: Have I finally piqued your interest? Do come, my dear guest, join me at my table and partake in this grand banquet. Allow me to guide you as we savour the delicate afterglow of every spirit together.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: I
voiceLines.content: Shhh, please, do be quiet. Let's listen to the voices of the departed.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II
voiceLines.content:
Do you know?
Every life has a long-lasting echo as it fades.
They vary in pitch and tone, stretching little by little from the moment death arrives until they dissipate into the heavens and earth, much like a sighing cry.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content:
Before every meal, I converse with the departed. For them, being eaten and savoured with true sincerity is a continuation of life and their final, most glorious moment.
Like how I long for them, they, too, long for me.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content: You can't smell yourself? Ah, what a shame. You're missing out on the sweetest, the most sublime... Oh, my, what is it? Why are you pulling away?

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content: Rest assured, {Male=Mr.,Female=Miss} Keeper, I'll remain by your side until the day your life meets its destined end. On that day, I will, with all due solemnity, consume your body piece by piece. And your soul shall reside within me, forever.

voiceLines.title: Chat: Touch
voiceLines.content: Do you, too, crave the taste of my flesh, dear Keeper?

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Crisis
voiceLines.content: My people and I revere the beauty of permanence. Dissolution slowly weathers a living person, wiping away all traces of their existence... Such cruel torture should not be allowed.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Mythag
voiceLines.content: I adore the classic beauty of this institution's Gothic clock tower. And the Awakeners here, ah... They exude an aromatic flavor I've never tasted: a perfect blend of departed fragrance and a trace of living scent. It truly makes me crave a little bite.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Like
voiceLines.content: The deceased who have found peace are beautiful and fragrant. Their beauty isn't in the flesh, before or after death, but in their souls. Those souls' enlightenment regarding death, their longing for life, and their desire to be remembered are the delicacies I have always dreamt of.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Hate
voiceLines.content: There was a man who slowly carved away a young girl's flesh, fingernails, hands, and feet, all while continuously healing her. He didn't want her to die, nor did he want her to live. I could not, of course, grant him a peaceful death. So, I gave him a taste of his own medicine. I wonder how many years he's been trapped there... For someone who desecrates death, this is quite fair, isn't it?

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Keeper
voiceLines.content: No adjective can describe the intoxicating fragrance of your body. It is like the tart aftertaste of a rich Bordeaux wine, and the thick aroma of a mellow, buttery sponge cake. The day of your death will perhaps be the most important event of my remaining time.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Leigh
voiceLines.content: While that lady's enthusiasm is very touching, her body has a sort of over-fermented, damp smell. Even though she keeps begging me to have a taste, it simply does not suit my palate. How vexing.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Pickman
voiceLines.content: Like me, Mr. Pickman is in pursuit of immortalized beauty. We could have become closer friends. But he sees eating as a violation of preserved eternity. Such a narrow artistic philosophy.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Food
voiceLines.content: Why are you so wary of me? You needn't and shouldn't be alarmed; to feed on a living human goes against my aesthetic.

voiceLines.content: Who shall grace my dinner table today, I wonder?

voiceLines.title: Investigation Success
voiceLines.content: I shall bestow upon you the honour of becoming tonight's feast.

voiceLines.title: Investigation Halted
voiceLines.content: Truly delicious food is always worth the wait.

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
Doll once studied her in exhaustive detail, but nowhere—not the torso, not the limbs, not the skull, not the pelvic cavity—was there any part capable of producing sound. How she speaks at all has become one of Mythag's countless unsolved mysteries.
Most of the time she can hold an ordinary conversation. Now and then, though, that mysterious voice seems to have a will of its own, and what it says makes the skin crawl and the blood run cold.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
On A.F. 297, @1, @1 03:47, an unexplained explosion occurred southeast of @3 Republic @1@2@1 town. The shockwave triggered a 3.8 magnitude earthquake in the area, noticeable shaking reached villages 5 kilometers away from @1@2@1 town.

After the incident, @1@2@1 town lost contact with other regions, and surrounding residents could not recall the town's location. Based on this, the Committee dispatched members for investigation, and dissolution material was detected at the edge of @1@2@1 town.

After sealing off the small town, Mythag University investigators performed dissolution body clearing operations and recovered the E-1929 Silver from a strongly dissolved area suspected to be the explosion's center.

E-1929 is particularly unique; its Gnostic index has been in an irregular fluctuation state for an extended period and emits a ticking sound like gears, only maintaining brief stability when linked with mechanical fragments recovered from the strong dissolution area. Based on this characteristic, the Mythag University Awakening Department wrapped E-1929 in mechanical fragments and quickly awakened it once the Gnostic Index tended to stabilize.

—<Italic:"E-1929 Silver Acquisition and Awakening Report Summary">

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
At 18:00 yesterday, room CB-101 in the basement of the Prince Building at Mythag University was vandalized by unknown parties. The reinforced door was badly damaged, black lightning-shaped scorch marks were left across the walls both inside and out, and the room itself was in ruins.
"A momentary surge of current can leave marks like these," said Dr. Adams of the electrical engineering department of the scorching on the walls. "It would take an enormous voltage. An ordinary apparatus capable of that would be huge—far too big to hide. But with a Silvercore... anything is possible."
Since Silvercores are kept year-round under the strict guard of the Awakening Studies Department, it is hard to imagine anyone using one privately without being noticed. And so attention has turned instead to the Awakeners, who carry Silvercore energy inside their own bodies.
"If you ask me, she did it, no question," one Awakening Studies student told this paper on condition of anonymity. Asked who exactly he meant, he grew nervous. "You know—her. The one they call the Tick-Tock Man! Haven't you heard that current running through her body, on and on? I hear 'current' and I think of her. Has to be her."
Plenty of students voiced similar suspicions. But the Awakener who moves like a clockwork doll and wears that uncanny smile is not without allies: several Investigators have publicly stood up for Erica, urging everyone to keep to the facts and the evidence, and not to harm others over personal prejudice.
Dr. Sokolova, acting head of the Awakening Studies Department, declined to comment. The investigation is ongoing.
—Excerpted from the Mythag Daily, "A First Look at the CB-101 Explosion"

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
Hannah: As you see it, is there any difference between you as an automaton and you now?
Erica: That version of me retained "emotion."
Hannah: What sort of emotions, exactly—if you're willing to share?
Erica: I'm sorry. I do not understand the question.
Hannah: Uh, I mean—if the question feels too personal, you don't have to answer.
Erica: I cannot perceive "willingness." My apologies.
Hannah: Then... please tell me what you felt at the time?
Erica: Flesh-and-blood self survived an explosion: happiness, delight.
Discovery that my mind had been transferred to and stored in a mechanical doll: tension, excitement.
Discovery that my consciousness was slipping out of control, together with a strong urge to destroy: tension, fear, protection.
Hannah: Protection?
Erica: I am very sorry. The detailed record has been lost.
Hannah: A different question, then—one all our readers want answered. Why do you have no emotions now? What happened?
Erica: Sanity could not be restored through the Spiritual Link, for reasons unknown. The university took the necessary measures: all emotion suppressed by Silvercore-assisted apparatus. Aggression and danger reduced. Intelligence retained. Usability retained.
—Excerpted from the Mythag Daily, "Awakener Faculty Interview: The Tick-Tock Man"

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
Hannah: Do you remember what happened before you were taken apart?
Erica: The automaton's behavior began to go out of control, gaps appeared in its consciousness, and during those gaps it would destroy everything everything everything will be buried under current and flame
Hannah: Erica?
Erica: ...
Hannah: I can't be lucky enough to run into the "Tick-Tock Man Effect" myself... Erica?
Erica: Head module back online. My apologies for the interruption.
As I was saying, the automaton noticed that the threat it posed to humans was steadily growing, and since it still regarded itself as human at the time, this caused it great pain.
Hannah: When you said "protect" earlier, did you mean protecting humans?
Erica: The automaton wished to protect. Yes.
Hannah: Then why didn't you tell me that just now?
Erica: ...
Hannah: Do you want me to ask something else?
Erica: No. I am no longer troubled by emotion. I can answer.
Once it recognized the danger it posed, the automaton tried to short-circuit its body before each lapse in consciousness, to reduce the chance of the body causing destruction on its own.
The protection failed in the end. The human friend died.
The automaton felt sorrow, regret, despair.
The automaton self-destructed to ensure it would cause no further destruction. The Silvercore was then recovered by Mythag University and used to make me: Erica, chassis number EA307881.
—Excerpt from Hannah Peaslee's recording, "0711: An Interview with the Tick-Tock Man"

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
Faint is a faded, hard-to-hatch seed.

People pity her for her flaws and love her for her weaknesses.

Yet those who knew she had chosen to remain in the shell, had long since turned to dust—stardust.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
In June of A.F. 282, acting upon an investigation request submitted by the Mystea Treaty Committee, we dispatched a survey team to the New Leonia region.

Since the meteorite impact a year ago, the area has experienced an abnormally elevated mortality rate.

Furthermore, investigators discovered several species of mutated flora at the impact site. Instrumental analysis confirmed that these plants contain high levels of radiation, suspected to have been introduced by the meteorite.

However, no extraterrestrial minerals were found within the impact crater. According to villager testimony, on the third day after the impact, a group of scientists in white coats dissected and removed the meteorite in its entirety.

(Note: Suspected to be a non-governmental scientific organization; identity remains unverified.)

Following coordination between the Committee and local authorities, all residents have been evacuated, and the area has been officially declared a prohibited living zone.

According to calculations by the Mythag University Physics Laboratory, this residential ban must remain in effect for at least 80 years.

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Faint saw the student secretly weeping in the laboratory.

She wasn't Faint's favorite student, but she was undoubtedly the one who liked her the most.

The girl never minded Faint's resistance and aloofness, nor was she afraid of Faint's uncontrollable abilities.

She would spend her entire allowance on sweets, just because she was worried that Faint didn't have enough energy; she would wear the clunky protective suit just to comb Faint's tangled hair.

... <Italic:I must repay her>, Faint thought.

So, Faint did what she could.

—<Italic:If she was just worried about failing exams, then I'll just threaten the others into failing instead, right?>

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
Among these sisters, one of them should never have been born.

On the Desolate of the Lyra constellation, Faint and Tinct spent half their lives shrouded in malice.

But who is the unacknowledged one?

Sister Faint is powerful yet uncontrollable; the life force she plunders seems to flow away like a river, leaving her to barely survive by licking the remaining dewdrops.

Sister Tinct is beautiful yet struggles to be independent; her life is as stubborn as duckweed, yet rooted nowhere, causing her to revolve around her sister.

Perhaps they both believe they are the one who should not exist. It's just that Faint made her decision earlier—using her own life as a threat, she forced her sister onto the journey of departure.

"Leave, Tinct. Don't let me hold you back."

"You shall sing among the stars, becoming the most dazzling color."

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
Do I deserve to have wishes?

If I do, can I become a part of my sister?

To make her whole, to make us whole.

Only then could I express "love" without reservation, and she could embrace "love" with an undivided heart.

Dear Tinct... perhaps this is what I, as the firstborn child, should do for you...

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
Beware: a siren's mesmerizing charm lurks under her seemingly calm and rational words. Never show curiosity towards the unique appearance beneath her malformed helmet; never forget her long-lasting dissatisfaction with this humanoid body.

Her gleaming light once lured moths to its molten warmth. Her burning fire once guided the lost to their doom. Now, only confusion flickers in her lighthouse.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
The past three years have seen a large number of shipwreck incidents in the Monge Triangle sea area, accompanied by several cases of totally missing.

According to a sailor's testimony, a "woman with a glowing head" has been witnessed on the deck of the victim vessel during the rescue operation.

The field investigators rushed to the Monge Triangle sea area, but his ship had lost contact after arrivial. When the reinforcements finally found the spearhead ship, it had already lost power, drifting by the current towards the center of the Monge Triangle. All crew members were severely dehydrated and feeble. Massive hallucinations with acute intensity have been reported.

During the medical examination of the crew, a Silvercore was found among Investigator Ivors' personal belongings. The investigator himself consistently denied any contact between the ship and any Awakener.

The Silvercore was later sealed by the Awakener Department, numbered 6291-S-S-01, scheduled to use as teaching materials for pre-investigators in A.F. 315.

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Like a real lighthouse, most of the time her presence is nothing more than a steady glow at a corner, peaceful, isolated. Her words only illuminates when confusion stirs the air, while her guidances clearer than nautical navigation.

Only when she meets with other Aequor visitors does the light reveal her shadow, twisting under paranoid madness.

In contrast to her serene and intellectual appearance, Faros has unexpectedly profound knowledge in ocean voyages. Despite the unresolved suspicions of abducting and sacrificing sailors, she has assisted the university in revising numerous nautical documents under the Keeper's supervision.

According to feedback from sailors of cooperative vessels, Faros's revisions, though effective, often (though not clear whether she is intentionally or not) steer the course towards the Monge Triangle.

The university has then prohibited Faros from accessing any ocean-related materials.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
The radiance of devotion illuminates her pilgrimage. A glorious ascension for the most devout follower of her true lord. A golden promise for the most loyal subject of her king.

It collapses. The Divine Realm is a sinking lie, a fortress without foundation, a vine drifting away from its soil. Her dolor billows. Her desolation turmoils. The remaining faith in the Divine Realm cannot keeps Faros afloat anymore. The poor wanderer eventually drowned.

Diving deep into the sea, her love and hatred agitates into swelling waves. The water whirls and spumes and eddies, splendor as the ceremony fireworks in her memory, a festival almost like a solace.

Her final torched gaze before being beheaded by the hero, must have been cling to the Divine Realm she couldn't forgo.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
Return to her home, trace back to her origin, reunion with her lost dreamshe doesn't care how does her wish reflect in people's words. Even her body has altered to an Awakener, tides of her homeland still clamor in her soul.

The breath of sea-bottom volcanoes dissipated from her ears. The ocean's dreams writhing with ecstasies obscured from her eyes. Only her obsession with the Divine Realm still gleaming, more glorious than ever.

Mind her docility, a mere temporarily disguise. Her king's throne calls to her, like a lighthouse reaches through the aeons; her sacrifice will always be everything, like a wick's devotion to the light.

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
Genius and madness are a hair apart. She was once the brightest mind Mythag had, and her fall came like a great tower coming down; out of the rubble of all that reason crawled nothing but a raving fiend.
She still puts on the vestments of science as she always did, pouring life, humanity, love, and ruin into the crucible, cooking up a poison to destroy the world.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
Until the whole truth came out, no one had ever suspected that Doll was the one behind that string of appalling disasters.
Inside Mythag and out on the Dissolution front, she had always been the mainstay, the lamp at the top of the tower—the one thing everyone believed would never move.
As one star after another in humanity's night sky was broken and scattered by Dissolution, that unwavering lamp was cruelly snuffed out as well, and became a hand in the shadows, working with the same darkness it had once held back.
Tornadoes, floods, great earthquakes... crude murder was far too inefficient for a genius's plans. With her intellect not diminished by a single degree, she remade the Silver Technology she had once been so proud of into lethal instruments for "moving the world," and sent one gift of ruin after another into places Mythag's eyes could not reach.
By the time she was captured, her corroded brain could no longer control the doll's body with any precision. The face that had once been calm as still water was full of twisted, uncanny expression, as though meeting her eyes would be enough to drop a person into madness.
Without ever agreeing on it, everyone chose to ignore her occasional blurred muttering, even though it may truly have given away the truth of the world.
Because what happened to her had proven once again that human beings, in the end, cannot live without meaning.

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
As this Genesis Awakener, formerly the "Brain in a Vat," has a history of breaking free of the S355 restraint unit, Director Czort has carried out its transfer into a new type of specialized Dissolution restraint unit.
The unit is located deep in the Black Pool. No other instrument or object is to be present within a thirty-meter radius of it, and the Black Pool monitoring team is to run inspection rounds at least once every sixty minutes.
Monitoring shows that the Awakener remains conscious at all times and has almost never been observed to sleep. She has attempted to tell patrol members about the illegal Silvercore modification experiments she previously conducted; one team member fell into madness after a brief exchange with her.
All patrol teams now consist of three members. Contact or conversation with the Awakener is strictly forbidden, and soundproof ear protection must be worn for the full duration of the round.
...
This Awakener's confidentiality classification has been raised to the highest level of Awakener custody. No one with knowledge of her may disclose any information about her within Mythag or outside it, and no one may visit without the Director's approval and personal escort.
—Excerpt from the Mythag Black Pool Monitoring Team Report Log

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
As someone working at the very front of Dissolution research, Doll always knew perfectly well that the footsteps of annihilation were closing in behind her—and when it came to being dissolved, she knew the subject better than anyone. 
Her search for the truth advanced and failed, advanced and failed, until she slowly came to suspect that the human body was blind by its very nature: no one who belonged to reality could ever see what lay on the far shore, however hard they tried. 
Then, as the black sludge unmade the body, might it also lead the soul to that far shore? 
She sat in silence with the maxims on those ancient stone tablets and let Dissolution eat into her brain vat. Whatever waited at the end of the road, there was no turning back now. 
Fortunate and unfortunate at once: she staked her own existence and won her way to the inside of the world—and in that instant, truth, void, and ruin drowned her all together. 
In a single blink she witnessed everything the universe held: the nature of Dissolution, the truth of the world. Everything she had wanted all her life was there for the taking. 
Every article of scientific faith, every rational conviction, burst like a bubble. The iron wall of her mind collapsed all at once. 
The genius called Doll was already gone. What stood there now was only a living husk with the void inside it.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
All meaning scatters like sand, the world's false curtain falls away before her eyes, and everything returns to the first darkness.  
In the last performance on that lightless stage, the dancer of science goes on dancing with everything she has.  
She no longer minds that Dissolution is slowly eating her, because the ending of the piece was written before it began.  
As always, she will give the world every ounce of her genius, by the method that comes closest to truth.  
Press her a little and she will insist she still loves humanity and the world—that she means to end all suffering here, and bring people home to where they truly began.

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
Her memory has been steeped in blood since the day she was taken to prison. 
Whatever was ordinary and warm before feels like a lying dream now, blurred and split apart, driven into her flesh as so many sharp pieces. 
She can't recall the gentle arms or the worried face anymore; all that stays in her is hatred, and a question, and no end to either. 
Pain, humiliation, betrayal... what was any of it for? 
She asked, day after day, and no one ever answered, right up to the day freedom came. 
So she will find the answer herself: she will put the question to every filthy heart, one at a time, tearing it from the wailing, screaming chest that holds it.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
I seem to have fallen into something supernatural. I will set down everything I find here...
We were wrapping up the last of the excavation at Evrotas. I woke to find every other member of the team gone, and the town itself thrown back a thousand years overnight.
Buildings that collapsed ages ago stand whole again, the place restored exactly as it once was—down to the countless residents, all of them bones now.
Excitement, shock, and terror seized me at once. I have seen more bones than I can count, and still I cannot stop shaking at the sight. Anyone else in my place would be far more frightened than I am.
Every soul in this town appears to have been butchered by a single killer. Bones sprawl across the streets and lie heaped inside the houses. The town gate is shut fast, for reasons I cannot explain, and the ground before it is choked with those who tried to flee and were cut down anyway—a small hill built of bone.
There are no exceptions. Men, women, the old, children... all of them broken, bodies or skulls smashed in by some enormous blunt weapon. Standing over these dried bones, for a moment I could see the blood running through the whole town.
What happened here?
...
I searched everywhere, dazed, and found nothing—until I entered the town prison.
The carnage here is worse than anywhere else. Whoever did this tore the place apart in a towering rage. There is writing on one wall, dry and brown and twisted, as though someone dying had scrawled an accusation in blood. I studied it carefully. I believe it reads: evil spirit.
An evil spirit? Does that name the killer, or did this town truly suffer something supernatural?
One person slaughtering an entire town is beyond belief. Perhaps only a real demon could reap so many lives so cruelly.
After I left the prison, something about the town had subtly changed. I keep catching the smell of blood, faint, then gone, then faint again.
As I searched for a way out, chains rang through the town without warning, as if something heavy were being dragged along behind them.
The evil spirit! It's the evil spirit... it has found me! I ran until my lungs burned, but wherever I went, that awful dragging of chains followed.
I cannot run anymore. I am under a table in someone's house with the door locked, and still the chains come after me. I can hear it. It is getting closer...
I want so badly for this to be a dream, for all of it to be gone the moment I wake. Wait... the sound has stopped. Perhaps it has left?
...
Researcher's note: The legible handwriting ends here. All that remains are three final words, badly distorted. Our best reading of them is:
The door opened
—Excerpt from the diary of a deceased member of the Evrotas archaeological team

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
No one who meets her for the first time thinks of coming closer or saying a word; instinct screams at them to get away.
She is utterly mad—or rather, a beast, wholly and completely.
Given the choice again, she would probably rather be a beast than live through what she lived through as a person.
She trusts no one. When those crimson eyes turn on you, there is no suspicion in them, only indifference and the intent to kill.
Suspicion is beneath her now. Everyone is equally vile in her eyes.
If you want one piece of advice for dealing with her, it is this: never try to tame a real beast. There is nothing tame in her, and at the first opening, her claws and fangs will go straight through your throat.
Run before she notices you, and pray her next prey is someone else.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
Under that lady's care and teaching she grew up kind and gentle, every inch a noblewoman's daughter. Then, for a single thoughtless kindness shown to a slave, her "parents" cast her out without a second thought.
The Spartans had never accepted her, and her own people hated her to the marrow.
Overnight she was a traitor to everyone, with no place left in the world that was hers.
In the prison, malice came off every one of them, thick as a contagion—and not one of them had ever met another before.
The torment in that lightless place felt eternal. She came to dread anyone drawing near, and sleep never came; only when she blacked out could her eyes close in peace, and opening them dropped her straight back into the nightmare.
What had she done wrong? How had it all come to this?
Her resentment had nowhere to settle, and she could find no logic in her fate.
Was it because she was guilty?
But if she was guilty, then everyone else was ten times guiltier.
Hatred piled up day after day into rancor, and rage burned through her blood night and day until, at last, it burned away the cage that held her.
The chains that had bound her for years now wound around one screaming throat after another. They had long since become part of her body, and they served beautifully. Blood-slick chain in hand, she went hunting filthy souls, one by one.
Red. Red. Warm red, reeking red.
See? She had always known. Not one soul among them was clean.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
Everything she met in this world seemed arranged to hurt her. Kindness, forbearance, pity, trust—every soft thing was cut out of her and thrown away, still trailing raw flesh.
Forgiveness was never in her vocabulary. Blood and hatred can be answered with only one thing: someone else's blood and hatred.
Blood for blood—the fairest law there is, and one that warriors and slaves alike hold to.
A volcano silent for a thousand years erupted in a single night. A hand reached up out of the underworld and hauled itself onto the soil of the living.
A vengeful spirit, come to run rivers of red through the world of men.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: II

voiceLines.content: Such sweet hatred, when seasoned with the blood of foes, is surely the most exquisite dish in the world.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight
voiceLines.content: I think I just heard those who claimed to be my masters wailing again. How delightful.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Florish

voiceLines.content: All who tried to control or use me ended up in the underworld at my own hands—I don't mind sending you there as well.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II
voiceLines.content: Do you think a few honeyed words and a few days of false kindness will make me willingly don the shackles again and become your plaything?

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content: Yes, I did grovel before those people; there's no denying it. They took advantage of my ignorance, and I made them pay for it.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content: I only regret not impaling their corpses on stakes and hanging them on the walls! I will spare none who betrayed, trampled, or insulted me!

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content: You have always clung to that amusing trust and stayed by my side... Fine, perhaps putting you to use isn't a bad idea. But remember this: I cannot tolerate any betrayal, especially from you.

voiceLines.content: The Bloody Chain of Slaughter, Tisiphone's Messenger, Blade of Hatred... I don't care. That's just what they called me. Well, I certainly don't mind living up to them.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Like

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Hate
voiceLines.content: Look at these shackles on me—they're not decorations, but reminders. Reminders of betrayal and humiliation.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Keeper

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
She calculated the speed of a sword stroke, the angle that would carry her clear of a blow.
She calculated whether an escape plan could work, and the odds that the world still had a future to reach.
Right to the very end, she never gave up the arithmetic.
Just as she never gave up walking that road where no one else walked.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
■ File Number: AF315-C01
■ Awakener Codename: @2 Walker
This Awakener was first observed in A.F. 315, @1.

During the initial "Artificial Domain" experiment, influenced by the psychic resonance of the homogenous object, the "Artificial Domain" based on the Spirit Realm of our university's @2-level student Ramona Dexter unexpectedly broke through dimensional boundaries.

At that time, the Keeper confirmed the existence of the world outside dimensions for the first time in that "Artificial Domain" and also confirmed how @2's power would affect Ramona Dexter.

Thereafter, researches on the "Genesis Awakeners" was officially launched by the Awakener Sciences Research Institute.

Meanwhile, the planning of the teaching plan for new Power Control course for Ramona Dexter is also on the agenda.

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
"Ramona" is very restrained about showing herself. As she said, she borrows Ramona's body to step into this world only when the Keeper calls her.
She comes and goes in a hurry; apart from battle, she seems to want nothing more to do with our world.
Is she afraid of the nightmares that keep hold of her? Or afraid of growing attached to what she has already lost... We have no way of knowing.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
She was born into a fate others envied: an orphan raised as the sole heir—how fortunate.
She had a mind that startled everyone: speaking at one, arguing at two, and starting on the world itself at three.
She had talent that drew admiration: nothing she read was ever forgotten, and every sword she lifted became technique. At an unbelievably young age, she passed Mythag University's brutal preparatory program with perfect marks.
She had comrades she could trust at her back, comrades who would walk into the dark and the unknown beside her.
<Italic:She had...>

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
While she holds Ramona's body, "Ramona" never walks the campus.
Lotan's bold generosity, Ogier's shy loyalty, William's cool composure, Doll's exacting rigor... no one keeps those moments closer than she does.
But she never forgets: none of it belongs to her anymore.
The woman she is now must give every scrap of her attention to guarding another person marked by fate... and through that, another world teetering on the edge, another innocent version of herself.

voiceLines.title: Awaken
voiceLines.content: If you can still see me as "Ramona"... then please continue to use that name.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: I
voiceLines.content: Please don't worry.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: II
voiceLines.content: In the end, I'm only...

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: III

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Observe

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Ponder

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Reflect

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate
voiceLines.content: Is that the sound... of the clock's hands turning?

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Florish
voiceLines.content: When the final bell tolls... will I still be here?

voiceLines.title: Affinity: I

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content: I don't regret becoming this, Keeper; I'd choose it again. But I am afraid... afraid that the "Ramona" I used to be will leave no trace behind.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V

voiceLines.title: Chat: About @2

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content: He is but a giant. His silhouette awing, his power indestructible. His weapon a colossal blade that no one else can lift. His victories, gleaming like oiled fur on the blade's fang, nourished by countless wars and savage sacrifices. His prize, a mountain of heads severed from his enemies and kin, crowned only by his own head on top.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
On April 2, A.F. 3@2, a temple remain in the Ashdod region was vandalized.

As the only one who had university education, I, a mere visitor, was invited by the regional administrator to participate in the architectural assessment of the ruins. Haha, I should never let them know that my "university" isn't quite what it seems.

On the afternoon of April 3, I entered the center of the temple. Ancient Semitics used it as a place of worship, and their pagan belief once flourished among the pillars before lost in history.

Yet what appeared before me was a sculpture that could be mistaken by no one. I clearly knew that the folds on its clothes should indicate the texture of striped linen.

However, its both hands were broken, its head severed from the body, and its lower limbs shattered on the threshold. Mucilage covered everywhere like the trace of a sticky slug. Upon inspection, there were few peculiar scratches buried within, accompanied by a giant, webbed footprint.

The pagan belief may still circulate nearby, but a formal investigation is not urgently necessary. I will extend my stay in the Ashdod region.

Fin@1@2sen, "An account of a trip around five cities of the Philistines"

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Goliath is tyrannical and ruthless, but his power is undeniable. According to Miss Erica's battle records, his brutal brawn can no doubt guarantee his advantage even in isolated and vicious situations. I believe that Goliath does not care about the level of his partner's ability just because no one can hold a candle to him in his world.

However, everytime Goliath faces Miryam, fear always seeps from his eyes uncontrollably. It's hard to imagine what kind of existence would evoke such awe from this despotic ruler and brutal former-king.

Additionally, he has shown unusual concern for Miss Murphy. Sometimes he was witnessed to wander around the university's surrounding maze, maybe waiting for Murphy to return from her mission. Sometimes he would distantly observe Murphy's condition, seemingly worrying about possible injuries during her tasks.

Miss Peaslee also notices this. Once she said to me half-jokingly, "Hey, don't you think he's trying to be an ordinary father?"

"Observation record from an intern researcher"

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
A scar jagged across his neck. A declaration of death for his people, while a coronation of majestic power for him.

When exile marks his failure, bitterness drown his breath; when despration hollows for surrender, and tides clamor for sacrificehe prays to the God for the power. His transcendent power.

Thus the God's apostle accepts his prayer, severing his head as an offering.

Thus the God's apostle acknowledges his prayer, emplacing the remnants of immortal on his exposed cervical spine.

Thus the God's apostle answers his prayer, leading him into the sanctum of eternity.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
Beheading death's cold embrace, he survived and transformed. The glitter on his blade fades. The mask of apostle conceals his savage expression.

He did revere instinctively when that miracle manifested. But no god could capture his fear, and no cult could earn his faith.

A giant should not yield to others. A warrior should not lower his head.

His past already wreathed in dust, his war still longing for final triumph. The desire for conquest run through his veins, etching into bones like a sigil bearing the bestowed power. Perhaps, one day, death will end his dominion. Perhaps, one day, he will rise to the sole supremacy.

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
At first glance, Hameln always reminded you of a kind of Eastern porcelain—white, luxurious, with graceful curves and a wave-like gentle sheen, yet somewhat cold to the touch.

Beneath that respectable, meticulous exterior lies a soul of extreme, empty purity. His entire life revolved around a single thought, like a machine programmed with one command, devoid of all other responses.

To him, everything was merely a sequence of musical notes.

Play, play, endlessly play.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
A.F. 31@1, @1, @2, a famous tycoon who loved collecting music was found dead in his study by his butler late at night. There were no visible wounds or signs of poisoning on his body, and a strangely satisfied smile lingered on his lips.

Following extensive examination by forensic experts, the death was ruled an accidental one, as the room was locked with no way to get inside.

However, doctors could not provide a reasonable explanation for why this robust tycoon, who was in good health and even enjoyed horseback riding, suddenly died on such an ordinary and quiet night. Under pressure from his family, the police handed over the case to the Committee.

Initially intending to quietly resolve the matter, the Committee unexpectedly detected traces of Gnosis on scattered sheet music found on the tycoon's desk. The eerie sheet music was sent to Mythag posthaste, where research identified it as fragments of the lost second half of the famous "Requiem in A Minor." The final page of the score remained incomplete, with numerous frantic drafts scattered around, seemingly attempts by the tycoon to complete it.

Scholars at Mythag speculated that this attempt to complete the score caused the tycoon's descent into madness and eventual death, completing the awakening ceremony in an unconventional manner and prompting its immediate sealing.

For a long time, Mythag found no evidence of this unknown Awakener appearing or causing harm, causing the case to gradually fade from investigators' minds and into obscurity.

Only scholars in the field of music continued to yearn for the sealed half-sheet, hoping for the legendary composer to emerge.

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Hameln did not always appear before students. Even though he was willing to attend Mythag's musical events and guide the less adept students, most of the time, he played alone in a soundproof room or in secluded woods.

Except for official events, he called all of his playing simply "practice," as if the practice was endless, and the perfect performance would never arrive.

 People praised his work, "Such a diligent and humble master," they sung, intoxicated by its melody.

Yet, Hameln never knew humility; his words were always straightforward and overly harsh.

Such an obsessive pursuit of perfection in music made his classes a primary source of stress for students, earning him the title the "devil's teacher."

If, for some reason, you wished to get his attention, simply play the wrong note, and his frowning expression would be upon you almost immediately.

He bore no grudge against those he "tormented," merely imposing his passionate, impossibly perfect standard upon them, even if it was much milder compared to what he demanded of himself.

He was like a horse with a carrot dangling overhead, forever striving for somethung unattainable.

Except for pausing for the elegant dancer, he rarely initiated contact with other Awakeners. However, he always displayed a surprising patience with requests and initiating conversation.

Perhaps it wasn't indifference that hindered him, but too narrow a mind.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
Talent seemed to be a rare favor of destiny. Hameln had never witnessed it in anyone around him during his long adolescence. It became a vague image—a symbol driving him forward under his father's whip.

He firmly believed that relentless diligence was the endless ladder to the perfection just out of reach. Even when he stood at the pinnacle of the world stage, it remained an unchanging truth.

This was until he met someone that could stand beside him.

"What a dazzling genius!" they cried: this gift of so-called talent was not within him, but another.

From festering envy and jealousy, he suddenly felt an indescribable confusion and helplessness.

Without such talent, can I still reach the perfect end?

The rungs of the ladder of diligence had suddenly turned to ashes, while the door to perfection remained ever distant.

He often lingered outside the crowds that swarmed this genius, deliberately aloof.

But whenever he looked in that direction, he always silently rehearsed his greetings.

Those mediocre insects always surrounded them, murmuring malicious whispers.

He was far too clumsy, silent for so long without being able to argue.

Words meant little, he thought. Let music be his medium—for only music is the perfect language; surely they would understand.

However, fate was a fickle beast, and would always come to reclaim the gifts it had so generously given.

Geniuses die young, and yet the mediocre still stand.

In the past, provocations and scheming had never shaken him in the slightest.

Yet at this moment, looking at the stack of unsent, unsatisfactory music scores, he could only shed tears of anger.

Hameln suddenly understood: before reaching this perfect kingdom of heaven, he must use all means available in world below.

Fortunately, compared to those mediocre people, he already possessed the intellect to do it.

After all, in his eyes, everything was nothing more than a calculation, like notes arranged on a score.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
His life was monotonous and dull, with loneliness as a contant companion, alongside feelings of resentment, confusion and hatred that had long been digested since before he could even remember.

Now, he has become one with music, transcending mere passion—unavoidable, inescapable.

All that remains to him is music.

Keep moving upward; do not look back at those nine hundred and ninety-nine steps behind.

After all, he has already touched the ultimate melody, the destined flute.

Accept this endless flow of music, and let it saturate your soul and dreams.

For he has long since used his own soul as an instrument to resonate with yours.

What I mean is, if commanding Awakeners is a performance, you're doing well.

voiceLines.content:

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Your Commonalities
voiceLines.content: In terms of technique, strategic planning and music conducting are no different. Humanity, emotion, desire... they are as clear and docile as notes on a staff, displayed before my eyes, dancing along the path of the baton. To understand music is to understand everything.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Reason and Order
voiceLines.content: Rationality and order paved the way. I walked upward and opened the gates of the hall. Beyond them, neither remained— truly eternal music transcends reason.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Dissolution
voiceLines.content: Each of us hides a melody in our hearts, trapped by reason and the body, only to be fully expressed in madness.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
The Evrotas archaeological team has been plagued by a mysterious illness for ten days, and the situation remains dire.

The illness strikes without warning and with ferocious intensity. Patients typically experience severe hallucinations, accompanied by a loss of bodily sensation and sensory deficits that worsen over time, eventually leading to partial or total paralysis. While the contagion appears confined to the archaeological site on the west bank of the Evrotas River—affecting mostly workers and resident scholars—authorities cannot rule out the possibility of further spread.

A former worker revealed to reporters that symptoms had already surfaced fifteen days ago—on the very day the "Evrotas Shackles" were unearthed. Readers following the news may recall these well-preserved, rust-free shackles that clearly originate from an ancient civilization. They arrived in the Kingdom of Leonia yesterday and have been handed over to Mythag University for further research. The link between the illness and the shackles, however, takes on a distinctly supernatural tone.

"Everything went wrong at the camp the moment we dug them up," the worker noted. "Many had nightmares of a girl bound in a cage by chains... This is a curse—the curse of the shackles! There is no other explanation."

As of today, relevant authorities have cordoned off the area. The Evrotas excavation has been completely suspended.

—<Italic:The Ancient Curse? Mysterious Illness Sweeps the Evrotas Archaeological Team.>

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Helot is a sharp, cold blade.

Awakeners who have worked with her say she's an effective weapon, strong and always mission-ready. Once given a kill order, no matter how powerful the enemy, she will break through and take the enemy's head.

But that's all.

She might protect her team, but it's just following orders, not out of care. She doesn't trust them; they can't trust her to guard their backs.

What they don't know is that to her, turning a blade on allies is despicable, contemptible, and deserving of punishment.

Having tasted the bitterness of betrayal herself, she would never turn her sword against her comrades.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
The girl wears a plain dress, her skin still stinging from the rough scrubbing earlier. She doesn't understand why soldiers brought her here; a noble master's house is no place for slaves to come and go freely, and she is far too young to serve here.

The lady in the snowy white gown sits poised in the chair. The girl lowers her head, trembling with fear and nerves.

"I knew I wasn't wrong..." the lady says, "So much like her... truly."

Like? Does that mean she looks like someone else?

"Perfect. Simply perfect." The lady claps her hands happily, "It shall be you. From today on, I am your mother. Do you understand?"

Mother? But she already has a mother. Her mother was at home, crying out loud when she was taken away.

If so... what about her mother?

Confusion swirls in the girl's mind. She wants to ask, yet she understands all too well: a mistress's word was a slave's command, and disobedience meant severe punishment.

"I understand, Madam."

"What a good child. Let me think... I'll call you Helot. Do you like that name, Helot? I'm sure you do. Come, put on this dress and show it to mommy."

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
The lady who deigned to lower herself took her hand, promising to give her all the love in the world.

She believed in the lady's gentleness and the master's indulgence, trusted every smile and every hug, unaware that in their eyes, she was merely a pet—something to be discarded the moment it posed any threat.

They were the ones who cast her into a cage, shattering her trust to pieces. But neither the warden's whip nor the torment from her own people hurt as much as the betrayal from her loved ones.

Hate, such hate! She hated them for using lies to win her genuine heart, hated them for using her life to create this painful farce. If trusting others led to this, then she would forever rely on no one but herself.

Her trust is reserved for herself alone.

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
A rose thorn tears the page of the poem and leaves a colorless smear of blood. The smell of alcohol drifts and lingers; invisible flames spread in every direction.
Inside that fire, Horla holds the last canto in her hands, writing a silent footnote to the end of the genius poet who hid herself away in the greenhouse.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
At the beginning of A.F. 3@2, during the renovation of the city named Cité, an anomaly was discovered in a fire-damaged garden: ashes climbed the burnt walls of the greenhouse like vines, and the ash roses blooming on the vines shimmered with a metallic hue.

Following the trail of the vines, an investigator from Mythag University retrieved this Silver. The moment she touched the silver powder, her fingertips were scorched black without any pain, but tears inexplicably rolled down her cheeks.

The weeping came without reason and dissipated into the ashes in an instant.

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
There is a strange magic about Horla. Anyone at the university with a love of poetry and beauty is drawn to her without meaning to be, and gathers wherever she is.
She does not like to publish her poems, but the students of Mythag still find ways to get hold of a line here, a fragment there. Whatever comes off her pen sweeps the campus within days.
At first light someone recites her words softly beneath the bell tower; at dusk Nymphaea sits on a bench in Mythag Square, turning the pages of her collection; after nightfall students crowd into the auditorium to rehearse the verses she wrote.
Yet however warmly she is invited, Horla rarely spares these gatherings a look, let alone attends one. The mournful recitations, the occasions that end in tears—they leave her at a loss.
"Have I spread more sorrow again?"

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
This is a city of flowers and poetry. Here a tender love poem is worth a bunch of freshly cut roses—or a week's bread for a family of three. And when a masterpiece appears out of nowhere, it means some genius poet is about to be famous.
She had once been a gardener, her days spent among fertilizer and dead cuttings. Now she savored the flattery and adoration her elegant verses brought her. She gave up the garden entirely, even locked the greenhouse and let no one set foot inside it.
When people asked, all she would say was that her "inspiration" was kept in there.
They were born to nothing, the children of servants loyal to the nobility. When the Constante Federation was founded and the old aristocracy was purged, they lost their place in the world along with it.
One of them had been a lady's maid, raised at her mistress's side, and she showed a gift for words very early—but what business did a servant have with poetry?
The world around them was changing by the day, and a talent for verse could not keep a girl alive. All of it left her more out of place, more melancholy, more sorrowful.
Then the gardener held out her hand—that hand torn open by thorns—and gave her a garden. In that tiny kingdom the two of them spent the happiest days of their lives.
The quiet life began to change with a poem the gardener received.
Her friend's talent was so moving. She wanted more people to see this poem written for her.
The shy, melancholy friend refused to sign it, so the gardener put her own name at the bottom—"If it gets published, they'll need a name to send the money to."
The gardener began to change with that first payment.
She could not understand how she had gone, so suddenly, from protector to burden.
She could not understand why her friend collected all the love and all the praise without effort, while her own labor counted for nothing against such talent.
Her head clouded by wanting and envy, she began using her friend's trust to coax the poems out of her. There was no going back from a lie like that. The seed had been in the gardener's heart from the beginning; it sprouted as the genius poet's name spread, and it budded at a street interview—devoted admirers pressed her about the secret, aching feelings hidden in the verses, and the gardener, who could not read the poems at all, broke into a sweat and fled. Late that night she came back to the greenhouse, and there, under her friend's worried look, the flower of panic opened.
After a fire that shocked all of Cité, the genius poet announced she would write no more, and vanished with the wealth and fame she had won in so little time.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
"Horla, from today on, I'll keep every poem you write, safe and sound. And from now on, I'll trade you my flowers for your poems!"
"Colette, you'll come back for me... won't you?"

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content: Forgive me, I lost myself in memories again. Please, do not look sad. It is your turn to narrate your story. Do you feel like writing a poem? Will your adventures, your experiences, your joys, your sorrows, flow like a gentle stream from your mind to your fingertips?

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content: I was but a fleeting watermark on parchment, yet our encounter has caused me to linger. Perhaps this is a miracle. I will treasure this miracle and compose timeless poems for you.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Hate
voiceLines.content: There is nothing in this world to hate. The golden years deserve praise, while the decline of old age deserves pity; the finery of youth is enviable, while tattered remnants evoke thoughtful reflection.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Her Pain

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Her Poems
voiceLines.content: Poetry and flowers are probably the same thing, are they not? Both are fleeting yet eternal. In this boundless world, they capture the most unforgettable moments in a small space... I think everyone has fallen silent for a poem, just as they pause to admire a flower's bloom.
