storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
She always arrogantly refers to herself as the "Divine Mother," coldly and hostilely keeping everyone outside her safe perimeter. It's difficult for those meeting her for the first time to connect her with the spoiled little princess.

"But they are essentially the same person," the Keeper, however, stubbornly insists to everyone. "You'd know if you ever saw her wolf down a cupcake alone."

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
Recorder: Erich von Werner
Date: November 7, 19@1
Coordinates: 68°14′S, 67°10′W
Due to an unusual number of floating sperm whale carcasses in our route, we were forced to land on this cursed island of ice. Below a glacial waterfall in the south shore fjord, the expedition team discovered the remains of a fifty-foot-long cephalopod. Its body was a deep indigo blue, densely covered in phosphorescent, luminous blue concentric rings, the edges of which secreted a thin layer of mucus. After we sampled and purified the substance, an unsettling quantity of blue crystals precipitated from the mucus.

The suckers on the creature's arms exceeded two feet in diameter, and the inner walls of the suckers were etched with patterns resembling an unknown script. The main nerve cord was in a semi-transparent, gelatinous state, maintaining a faint pulse even in the -30°C environment (see attached Figure D-7). Dr. Harris, the accompanying biologist, attempted to collect a tissue sample from the nerve cord, but the moment the scalpel made contact, the entire carcass instantly disintegrated into powder. Indigo-blue dust became visible, suspended throughout the laboratory.

During the voyage home, Dr. Harris developed persistent delirium. He repeatedly drew geometric shapes combining spirals and polyhedrons on the cabin walls, screaming, "They are spawning beneath the Antarctic ice sheet!" On the morning of the second day, a patrolling crew member found him drowned in the ballast water tank. Autopsy revealed his alveoli were filled with indigo-blue microorganisms (identical to the octopus corpse dust). The captain ordered the incineration of all clothing that had come into contact with the samples.

May no one else ever touch the nightmare lurking beneath the ice.

— Appendix No. 37, Antarctic Expedition Log

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
After being awakened, Murphy: Fauxborn frequently has a dream of escaping. In the end of that dream, she holds her "Mother's" dagger and plunges it through her own chest under the brilliant moonlight. The dream then abruptly ends, and the moment she opens her eyes, they meet the gaze of the ivory statue at the foot of her bed.

In Mythag, Murphy: Fauxborn acts like a younger version of her "Nurturer." She wears white mourning clothes year-round, rarely laughs or speaks lightly with others. Only when the conversation turns to her preference for sweets does a crack appear in her flawless, saintly facade.

<Italic:(Archivist's Annotation: I hope next time she wishes to enjoy cupcakes, she will ask for it immediately, rather than leaving a note requesting delivery to her room after everyone's afternoon tea has ended.)>

She maintains a distance from any Awakener with relation to the Seafarers. Unlike her other-world counterpart, she never deliberately avoids contact with them; however, the frozen, emotionless expression and thinly veiled hostility in her sarcasm subconsciously drive away those who don't want a confrontation.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
Murphy: Fauxborn has died once before.

It was not a willing step through the threshold called "Divine Descent"; she witnessed the "God" being born from her own chest. How ridiculous: it was a hideous, unconscious, and unknowing mass, yet she was forced to give up her vibrant, splendid life for it.

More ironically, the twisted fate remained relentless. At the moment the God was born into the world, she accepted the unwilling sacrifice through intense pain. After a long period resembling sleep, Murphy opened her eyes in astonishment, only to find the scene before her identical to her final moments.

"Murphy" died. "Murphy: Fauxborn" was Awakened.

Her Linker is a squirming blood clot, deaf and mute, that she herself gave birth to.

The God gives birth to the Princess, the Princess re-conceives the God, and the God reawakens her remains. A pathological fate clings tightly to her, an endless, unbreakable cycle. Her devout mother is ecstatic, the Seafarers prostrate themselves in prayer, and her dignity is restored, more glorious than ever before.

But the original "Murphy" is truly gone forever. The girl who once, with a burst of foolish innocence, attempted to rebel against an unfair destiny, now embraces the crown of vanity she once despised and boards a cruise ship that can never reach the other shore.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
"I am the Daughter of God, and simultaneously the Bearer of God."

This is how she confirms her authority. Only by maintaining this universally admired dignity can she preserve a precarious balance. So what if it's hypocrisy? So what if it's a delusion? Who isn't living in the "present" moment?

Murphy holds the swaddling cloth, which conceals the grotesque Divine Fetus, and acts as the God's proxy, speaking one lie after another:
"He has descended." "The Divine Realm will rise." "Please wait for the next moment of Stellar Alignment."

Rather than letting others' hypocrisy fabricate an illusion, she would rather decorate this prison with her own hands to a likeness she finds acceptable. As long as the "Mother," "Companions," and "Servants" she desires are still by her side, whether it is superficial deference or insincere mystification, she accepts it and finds it sweet.

"My name is Murphy, the Princess who bore the God. Regarding Lemuria, regarding the Seafarers' long-cherished wish... you need not inquire. I have my own arrangements."

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
She always seems to be circling that motorcycle of hers, the "Phantom"—a screw tightened here, a line adjusted there. The work has no end to it. Plenty of people tell her the repairs could not possibly be better, and still she buries herself in it, day after day.
The reason is a feeling she cannot account for: that something is still missing.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
A.F. 3@2, a D-phenomenon occurred in coastal towns of the Agló Republic, spreading outward in a spiral from the port, affecting an area hundreds of meters wide and causing @1 deaths.

Investigations traced the phenomenon back to a fishing boat that set out on A.F. 3@2 @1 @1@1, catching a silver-patterned cod-like creature.

The creature's soft body ruptured when cut by a sharp tool, releasing fluid laden with shell fragments and other residues. Upon reaching the port, shell-like growths had appeared among the catch but were ignored until a fisherman perceived himself as a shell, twisting his body and ending up hospitalized. Only then was the event reported.

Mythag personnel later located the source of the phenomenon at @4 cannery, removed it, and secured Silver O-36.

—<Italic:"Awakening System Silver Acquisition Report: O-36">

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Three months after she was Awakened, the Investigators and the Keeper threw Nautila a party—not to celebrate her arrival, but to celebrate her finally remembering the name of Mythag University.
She forgot it again the next day, but a party can always be held twice. Who knows—give her another three months and it may actually stick.
Nobody can say whether Nautila's goldfish memory is an aftereffect of Dissolution or the result of a damaged Silvercore. Short-term memory isn't all bad, though. For a mechanic who takes her work seriously, forgetting which screw she has already tightened means tightening every screw again—and again, and again. Machines that pass through Nautila's hands tend to come out sturdier than the rest, and to last far longer.
Doll adores her for it. Not everyone can do a repair job that holds for ten years.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
When night fell, Nautila and her mother would slip into the storeroom, take up their tools, and work on the monowheel they were piecing together from saved-up parts: the Phantom.
"Why don't we just buy one?" she asked as a child, looking up at her mother and her tools. "Then we could leave on our adventure right now."
Her mother took her hand and, while teaching her how to lay down a fast, clean weld, said:
"Machines are like people. Every one of them has its own temper, its own character. Only the ones that truly understand us will stay with us for the long road."
"Like friends?"
"Apart from the part where we build them—yes. Like friends."
The great wheel had to be strong and the engine had to last, because once they set out, they would not turn back easily. They were going to cross the whole world together, on one enormous adventure.
Illness took her mother and left behind a repair shop full of tools and empty of everything else. Nautila held the unfinished Phantasm and swore she would finish her mother's dream and her own, with this cold friend at her side.
Until the last voyage.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
A.F. 315, January, @2
Dr. Sylvia suggested that I jot down my thoughts in a notebook to help train my memory. Everyone says doctors know a lot and can surely help me. So I'm counting on it; tomorrow, I mustn't forget the purpose of this notebook! 

 Today, I completed the production and assembly of the exhaust pipe. Now it can exhaust air without interfering with the auxiliary hose's movement. This should be the last step, right? At least I haven't found any issues so far, but I can't rule out forgetting a screw somewhere... That's right, I must have forgotten something—either a screw or a pipe, or maybe bearing lubrication? Engine oil? Honestly, I've always had this nagging feeling that something's off with the Phantom. It's always... lacking? Is that the word? It misses a crucial component, even more critical than the engine. Without it, I can't set off, can't embark on that journey into the unknown, because that is ours. @2 
 Why am I saying ours? Who am I with? Did I... have someone? I remember, it seems like... @2 @4 @3 
 Uh, my head hurts so much. 

 But this notebook feels quite useful; that way, I can continue recalling from here tomorrow, and who knows, maybe I really will remember? 

—The only entry in Nautila's diary.

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content: The body this will projects still keeps the shape of a girl who died too young. Rotting hems, pale skin, eyes clouded with the shade of a former life—without a word, they tell of a past tangled up in sickness and suffering.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
It is a souvenir Professor Dexter brought back from a trip to the Febvre coast.
Febvre has a mild, humid sea climate, and the century-old Sevada Sanatorium sits right on the shore; every year, countless travelers choose to spend their holidays there.
Inside this glass bottle, water-stained and tangled with seaweed, lies a little clear powder. It is not a message in a bottle from some shipwreck, nor one of the local sand trinkets. Professor Dexter noticed it at once: the bottle holds Silvercore powder—in other words, a will lodged inside it.
He says he bought it from a local fisherman, who told him, evasively, about the strange things that had been happening lately. A few days earlier, heading out at dawn, the fisherman ran into an odd swarm of fish. It was neither spawning season nor wintering season, and still the shoal gathered in one place and would not leave. When he hauled the heavy net up, he found a strange bottle in it. He thought it a curiosity, and at the same time felt faintly uneasy, as if the thing might curse him with bad luck. For days afterward, not a single fish could be caught in those waters.

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
She treats every person and every Awakener with great kindness, never showing any signs of aggression. Most of the time, she stays quietly in her room, gazing out the window. At her bedside, we discovered several well-worn classical novels, along with handwritten essays and poems on notepaper, written in a delicate, graceful hand.

"Compared to that Maiden, I am clearly the lucky one." She whispered to the shimmering campus pond, facing the setting sun.

She rarely takes part in outdoor activities—though rather than saying she is unwilling, it might be more accurate to say she simply doesn't know how. That Maiden-like Awakener seems to lack a great deal of common knowledge about everyday life.

On several occasions, we also witnessed her conversing with the fish in the fountain in a strange sound—like bubbles being exhaled, or the hoarse gurgle of someone drowning. Yet her expression remained calm and serene, as if she were exchanging comfort with a dear friend. In that moment, we all believed she had found true peace.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
One step, then another, I walk slowly into the water. The nurses at the sanatorium never let me come this far. I hope the escape of a patient who will soon be unable to pay her fees does not earn her too much blame.
The last of the sunset lies on the sea. The tide comes in and lifts the hem of my dress, gently. The water is warm—warm as a mother's arms.
My body has never felt this light. There is a burnt-out volcano in my chest, and nothing moves in it now but the sea wind.
"Come home."
I hear the sea calling me in my parents' voices. They went to the far side of the ocean to earn the money for my treatment. If I had not been born with this unfortunate body, they would never have had to work so hard. If I could vanish into the sea some moonlit night, without a sound... I thought about it countless times, but the thought of their grieving faces always stopped me.
Then one day, on a moonlit night, the ship my parents were on vanished into the sea without a sound.
"Come home."
I put every bit of strength I have into walking faster. The sea has always taken in every suffering soul without complaint, and for me, wherever my parents are is home forever.
When the night closes in from every side, I breathe freely for the first time in my life.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
I love the sea. The sea at Febvre. The Prussian-blue sea. The sea that sends up a warm, damp wind. The sea that looks like an oil painting through the window frames of the sanatorium. The sea that carries the sails home. The sea that mothers countless lives.
Now, at last, I have come back into the quiet water—back to before I was born, back into the womb, wrapped in my mother's waters. The currents gather up the unlucky pieces and put me together again among white bones and coral. Fish of the deep swim through me, listening to those sighs about fate and suffering.
Mother—if I could be born into the world one more time, could I be a little happier?

voiceLines.title: Awaken
voiceLines.content: Greetings. I am Nymphaea of Febvre. You have granted me a new body, allowing me to finally breathe freely... How may I repay this grace?

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: I
voiceLines.content: I feel much better now, thank you for your kindness.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: II
voiceLines.content: Do you think I might become stronger, too?

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: III
voiceLines.content: If it pleases you, I would like to present a pale purple water-lily as a token of my sincere gratitude.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Observe
voiceLines.content: I would be grateful for your effort.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Ponder
voiceLines.content: My body feels warm, as if gently enveloped by the sea. It is truly incredible.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Reflect
voiceLines.content: Can this feeling truly be called "happiness"? I... never dared to hope for it before.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight
voiceLines.content: To be saved by you, I often feel a happiness that terrifies me... Please tell me this is not a dream, and that you will not vanish into the sea without a trace, will you?

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate
voiceLines.content: The sea has its own language. Just like this... I can sometimes chat with the little fish in the pond about our hometown. If you are curious, I can help translate for you.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Florish
voiceLines.content: Next time, let us go see the sea together. Febvre is fine; I can be your guide. Or anywhere else, even to the ends of the earth—I want to go with you.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: I
voiceLines.content: During my time at the sanatorium, I tried making friends, but people were reluctant to approach me... Is it because of this bone-eroding "poison"? Please, be careful when you come near me.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II
voiceLines.content: The sound of the bell carried by the night wind brings such peace. Would you like to sit on the stone chair and listen for a while? I will properly prepare your seat with a scarf.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content: Have you heard of "sea burial"? In my old town, there was a custom of submerging the deceased into the sea; the ocean became everyone's final resting place. As for me, I returned to its embrace early...

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content: Withering before blooming, like a water-lily... Seeking peace in the cold, raging tides, too timid to pursue my own happiness... That is the kind of person I am, Keeper.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content: I once grappled with this dilemma: Is pain longer than life itself? If so, is a peaceful slumber happier than tormented wakefulness? After waking, I too was ensnared, until you brought me this safe haven...

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
Every word he speaks is an act of loyalty; every move he makes, an act of virtue.
Though courtesy, honor, and self-discipline are carved deep into his soul, this Virtue Knight still wears the face of a child.
But there's no need to worry. Even if the price is being erased forever, Ogier will give everything he has to carry out his lord's orders.
May that day never come.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
A.F.2@2, November, a major earthquake struck the Beren region.

The next day, two professors were ordered to head to the disaster area to search for the missing Mythag investigation team.

The team was last active along the Mare Internum coast, primarily tasked with exploring, excavating historical relics, and searching for possible leads related to the "D-phenomenon." 

On November 8, at the location where team members were reportedly last seen, Professor @2 discovered an unrecorded palace ruin and recovered a Mythag-standard silver key, numbered I-@2, but did not find any team members.

On November 9, two Silvers were unearthed at the site, which were later taken back to Londinium and sealed due to their historical value, to be Awakened on another day.

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
"If it's your first investigation, take little Ogier with you!"
That's the advice the veterans always give a nervous new Investigator, which says plenty about how well liked Ogier is among students and faculty alike.
His stiff, old-fashioned manners cause the occasional incident, but he and his Investigator always end up finding the same rhythm, each holding the other up. In recent years it has become something everyone at the school simply agrees on: a rookie's first mission should be Ogier's mission too. Jokes about him make the rounds among the students—"Ogier brings a cloak for the female Investigators," "Ogier blushes at the sight of a bare leg."
The name "Death Knight" is fading from memory, buried under trust and warmth. All that's left is one small thorn, lodged in the boy's heart.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
Hardly anyone at the school still remembers that the boy was once called the "Death Knight."
Only at midnight does that day come back as a nightmare and creep into his dreams.
The Dissolutes overrunning the campus. The bell tower coming down. The "Keeper," barely breathing.
"Don't cry, Ogier. This isn't your fault..."
The cavalry overrunning his homeland. The palace in ruins. Black blood running from the princess's fingers.
"Don't throw your life away for me, Ogier. You've done more than enough..."
The grit of memory carries pain with it, and it scours the boy's soul.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
—How could it not be his fault? What he did was nowhere near enough.
Driven by that self-reproach, Ogier takes on twice as many missions as any other Awakener, burying "death" under the "virtue" everyone praises him for.
The endless work, the grateful words of young Investigators—they almost seem to wash the grief out of his soul.
But the sickness is only crowded deeper into the shadows of his heart, where They fester and stink, quietly drawing the knight toward a black mire.
"Um, sorry? Hello?"
Someone comes up to Ogier like a shaft of sunlight, or a breath of wind.
"The seniors said Ogier would be coming with me and Ramona on my first investigation. Is that right?"
He cannot protect the princess a second time—but he has been given another chance to protect a "Keeper."
"My name is Ogier. It is my honor to be bound to you by contract. I will guard your life with my soul. I swear it today, and I will never forget it."

voiceLines.title: Awaken

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: II

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: III

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content: You ask why I don't play with the other children? It's hard to say... In my past life, I rarely had a chance to play. My only companion was the princess I served... Oh! To speak of another ruler before you, my lord, please forgive my slip.

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content: Sweet laughter like a silver bell rings hollow, and a small body takes shape in the failing candlelight. She is the terror and the longing of the guilty, sweet rain and poisoned wine to the dying, bringing sweet pain and romantic madness. The crack of the whip that never leaves her hand, landing on bare flesh, is the wicked music of the dark.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
Awakening Material: Silver Core #G752a, unearthed from a festering mud heap at the ruins of Londinium's Newgate Prison. Investigator @2 accidentally slipped on a shattered skull while walking through the dim, grimy prison corridor and stumbled upon it by chance.

The awakening result deviated from expectations—what emerged from the black D-Slime was not some vicious death-row convict or a hulking executioner, but a petite young maiden with a sly smile.

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
"Watch out for Pandia. She is nothing like she looks. She's a demon."
That warning was paid for in the blood and tears of a long line of Investigators.
Pandia is forever laying sweet traps, coaxing researchers and Awakeners into master-and-servant contracts, then wringing out their feelings and their souls for her own amusement.
Talking to Pandia gets nowhere. She insists she only makes, shares, and scatters the seeds of pleasure with each new lover, and that every contract was signed willingly on both sides. After all, she lets her slaves taste the sweet fruit too.
Still, there is one thing at the school Pandia cannot face. Whenever Sorel passes her dormitory door, Pandia falls abruptly silent, no matter what she was talking about a moment before. Rumor says Pandia once took a bad beating while trying to seduce Sorel, but what actually happened remains a mystery.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
"You who have sinned—this is the abyss of appetite, the floor of hell. Here the black hounds howl, here the stench spreads, here the death bell tolls. Your reckless desires and your cruelties have brought you together in this place, and what waits for you is suffering and death."
Pandia once worked at Newgate Prison, the most oppressive, the grimmest, the most sunless filthy corner of all Londinium. Men whose hands had been red with blood were put in irons and stripped of their dignity; in the maze of the cell blocks they knelt and begged her, kissed her boots, and humbly called themselves her servants.
Each time a new hanging was set, she would send for the condemned so they could admire the road's end. While the man on the rope twisted and died, she liked to sit up high and watch the worst of them shiver with fear and despair.
But the "cats of hell" also saw her come to Newgate's iron gate, again and again, standing on tiptoe to peer out past the walls of Londinium, as though waiting for a visitor from somewhere far away.
"The truth is, I'm only one more of those prisoners who will never get out of this dark, damp, miserable dungeon."

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
"Master, whip me."
Desire burns in eyes that ought to be long dry, and melted wax slides down like tears.
Hunger, pain, curses, filth—every humiliation she begged for, every pleasure she handed out—all of it comes home to her at last.

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
A half-human, half-ghoul artist, he possesses an otherworldly talent that remains forever out of reach for ordinary souls.

His ghoul artworks dissolve the fragile boundary between the painted world and the real one, pulling viewers into a total, and often terrifying, immersion.

Yet Pickman vehemently rejects the title of mad surrealist.

In his own declaration, he has always been, and will only ever be, a realist—for he paints nothing but the world as it truly is.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
The courses of the Painting Department in the Academy of Fine Arts are tedious and mundane, most of which have left no trace in my life, but I can still recall the mimetic painting class in A.F. 3@2.

Mr. Matthew is renowned in the art association, his classroom is crowded with people. We huddled in front of Matisse's "Luxury, Calmness, and Delight," and at that moment, I noticed a thin young man in the corner madly smudging in a sketchbook. I approached him, ready to see his mimicked painting, but saw a chaotic stone sculpture of a graveyard.

"Look! The ghoul queen is giving birth, preparing for a blood feast for her child... how mad, how elegant!"

He excitedly looked up at me, his pupils glowing with a strange blood-red under the gaslight, as if it was a coffin covered in red moss. I felt fear and dizziness, but I couldn't take my eyes off it. In those eyes, I saw images completely unworthy of this world.

Pickman, from the first time I saw him, I knew he was different from us, his life was destined to be difficult and extraordinary.

After getting acquainted, I occasionally visited his studio. I witnessed him using decaying corpses as models and his own blood as paint. Standing in front of those crazy artworks, I felt as if I could hear the gnawing sounds coming from the canvas.

No matter which faction in the art world, no one recognized Pickman's creations; all exhibitions and salons turned him away. He appeared unfazed, still optimistically pursuing his art, but his purity made it impossible for him to hide his loss and pain. His talent was both shocking and frightening, and no one could truly accept it, including myself.

In the final days before leaving, Pickman fell into a state of great pain and excitement, which I originally thought was a psychological issue that was bound to occur, until one day, I saw his twisted limbs and claws, and witnessed the mad world in his eyes. That was a fear I couldn't contend with, and I could only try to forget it. Before I could completely end my connection with Pickman, he proactively found me to say goodbye.

Now, standing in the modern art museum's pristine gallery, looking at the genuine Pickman's work discarded in the corner, I can still hear the sound of nails scraping from deep within the canvas. "Underground Carnival," that was the painting he created when I first met him, and also the farewell gift he left me. Pickman might hold some taboo puzzles that should not be approached, but I still kept this painting. No matter what happened to him that I shouldn't know, one thing is certain - he is the most talented artist I have ever met.

Last night, I dreamed again of that painting class room in my freshman year. The young Pickman was in the corner of the room, laughing loudly at me.

"Ghoul? No, Ever, what I painted from start to finish is the truth, is humanity!"

The moonlight split into countless bloody points in his eyes. That was the first time the Abyss smiled at me. 

—Excerpt from <Italic:"The Memoir of Painter Avery @2">

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
Before receiving that invitation from Necrovia, Pickman thought there would never be a place in this world for someone like him.

The extreme madness he witnessed at the royal banquet table kept him tossing and turning in sleeplessness. Those eyes that could see scenes from different worlds found true fullness at this feast.

When he awoke from the Dream and Necrovia faded from his sight, Pickman's regret quickly transformed into an endless longing—he yearned to return to that dream city, to witness once more the infinite madness of that breathtaking scene. Following this desire, he attempted every mad act. In the end, he leaped into the D-Rift, painting with Dissolution, completely exposing himself to that horrifying darkness.

Everyone has their own tasks to accomplish. He has eyes that can see the mad truth of the world, and he firmly believes that he was born to burn for art; this is his mission.

As he wished, Dissolution brought him madness and pain, allowing him to once again witness the scenes he experienced in Necrovia. The twisted world in his eyes became even wilder and more vibrant under the corrosion of Dissolution. Amidst the prolonged suffering, he picked up the paintbrush, painting day after day without pause. He is a devoted realist painter, and he must record these visions that only he can see.

The pain intensified, and when Pickman could no longer grip the brush in his hand, he knew his time was near. After completing the final stroke of his last painting, he lay down in the coffin he had long prepared, waiting for death to arrive.

The pain and chaos brought by Dissolution clouded Pickman's mind. In the cold embrace of death, he peacefully closed his eyes. But the next day, the bright moonlight awakened him once again. The traces of Dissolution and pain miraculously faded away. After several days of growth, his limbs became long and curved, and his canine teeth and claws became hard and sharp. He sensed the scent of graves and spirits, and the mad, chaotic sights of the world became clearer in his eyes than ever before.

He gazed joyfully at his half-human, half-ghoul body, a tremendous sense of happiness swelling in his heart. Fate had bestowed upon him a curse, but it also compensated for his rare talent. The experiences in Necrovia awakened the faint ghoul blood within him, and under the catalyst of dissolution, he completed his transformation.

The tombstones around him danced clumsily like a crowd celebrating together. The enormous Bloody Moon opened its crimson eye and smiled at him. His art does not belong to this world; now, he knows where he is destined to go.

Pickman lay atop his own coffin, spreading his arms wide, joining in this lonely revelry.

He is about to leave the city of humanity and go to the promised land that belongs to him.

He knows that everything he seeks is waiting for him there.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
A monster. A freak. Demon with the blood of monsters. Madman who desecrates art...

Before Pickman, a canvas unfurls, and the curses mix with other sounds, smearing brilliant colors across the canvas.

He leaps into this dazzling world, wandering in the mad colors. He eagerly hopes to lead others into his painting, to let them witness the most authentic visage of the world.

The sharp spikes of reality pierce his heart countless times; mutual understanding between people is more challenging than opening the boundaries of two worlds.

From humans to ghouls, from human cities to Necropolis, the road is long and winding. He has been wounded time and again, yet he rises again and again. He has long understood that there is neither truth nor falsehood. Pain and madness are the truth of the world. And his duty is to depict all of this faithfully.

The meaning of depiction lies only in the act of depicting itself.

He dedicates all his life and passion to painting. His expectations rarely receive a response; his pursuit never ceases.

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
He is flesh born from a twisted existence, made up of cut and resewn skin, an empty chest cavity, a tainted heart, and invisible chains.
He is placed on a pedestal; people worship at his feet and claim he possesses a pure soul.

What exactly is he? Lost in countless dreams, he asks in confusion; among the dark green lake water and the empty fog, only his voice echoes in loneliness.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
Considering the potential relationship between Pollux's "Sacred Heart" and the Church of the Lightbearers' divine ritual, Mythag formed a research team to conduct a series of inspections and experiments on the heart.
To Pollux's dismay, the "Sacred Heart" had entirely replaced his original heart's function, becoming integrated into his body, making direct removal or replacement impossible.
During observational experiments, researchers discovered that the "Sacred Heart," which resembles a pupil, often exhibited subtle tremors and rotations independent of Pollux's will, much like a real eye.
However, light source testing proved the "Sacred Heart" did not possess visual functions. Instead, the activity appeared to be sensitivity to other living beings or objects. In comparative trials with various items, proximity to items related to Dissolution and the Silver Core triggered the heart's activity more easily.
Its activity was particularly pronounced near Dissoluted creatures and Awakeners. When Pollux actively used the "Sacred Heart's" power, the physical and chemical properties of ordinary items remained unchanged. However, when directed at Dissoluted items and creatures, a remarkable expansion of Dissolution occurred. Living organisms visibly in the early stages of Dissolution rapidly accelerated towards the late stages. The more severe the Dissolution originally suffered by the organisms, the faster this spread occurred.
In experiments with strict protective measures on Awakeners, the subjects reported a sense of approaching darkness and danger when faced with the "Sacred Heart's" power, prompting the experiment to be quickly halted.
After a stern explanation from the school, Pollux promised not to use the power against Awakeners. Due to Pollux's cooperation and excellent self-control, Mythag did not impose mandatory controlling items on him, but instead arranged regular health checks and power training.
Apparently, after hearing of the experimental results, Awakener Winkle almost fainted from screaming before posted notices prohibiting Pollux from approaching on the doors of her laboratory and dormitory. The school repeatedly tried to persuade her to no avail, and Pollux graciously stated that he would respect Winkle's wishes.

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Compared to Castor's eager and studious attitude, Pollux's approach to the world is one of quiet vigilance.
He observes, he thinks, he doubts. It was his meticulous consideration and caution that once enabled their successful escape from the church's heavy control. From a young age, he learned to gauge the intentions of others, to lie, and to hide his true thoughts behind a disarming smile. Even with his intimately close brother, he would subconsciously use a relaxed demeanor to soothe and reassure.
"It's okay."
"It will be alright."
Beneath the shadow of a giant, the weak must exhaust every means to grasp a single glimmer of hope.
Having endured a long period of forced amnesia and deception, he is now more intolerable of danger or mistakes. Even after heeding Thais's advice and coming to Mythag, he remained profoundly vigilant for a long time.
To other awakeners, Pollux appears as a quiet, patient, and friendly individual who often offers a gentle smile. But seasoned elders who see him can only sigh at the profound difference between the two brothers.
According to Thais, even in her presence, Pollux will intentionally or unintentionally position himself between her and Castor—since reclaiming his memory, he no longer wishes for Castor to always be his protector.
Jenkin once earnestly complained to the Keeper about Pollux's duality, claiming that when she "accidentally" picked up an item belonging to Castor, she witnessed his expression turn terrifying in an instant. "His usual good temper must be fake! He's the type who would eat children in private!"
However, after witnessing the Keeper's true power, Pollux's attitude underwent a complete transformation. He claims to have learned the truth of the world from that great soul and has now taken the Keeper as his new, unwavering faith.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
In the original design of the God of Fate, Pollux was probably never meant to be born.
Initially, only Castor had been successfully created in the artificial Twin Divi experiment. Just as this single, clueless embryo was to be disposed of, Pollux struggled and twisted himself free from his brother's flesh. He absorbed his life force, yet in doing so, he also saved it—from that moment on, their flesh, souls, and fates were irrevocably intertwined.
In the monotonous routine of the church's teaching, their lives and destinies were identical. But with the start of the "Holy Transformation" ritual, the pain and ruthless torment awakened something within Pollux—a defiance of his ordained fate as a Divus. The two children committed the boldest act of their lives: they sketched a world map from an outdated book and escaped from one false world to another imagined one.
After that fragile, fleeting beautiful dream shattered, the cruel punishment that followed did not crush their souls, yet that merciless fork in fate had already driven them apart.
Juliette ordered the two to be separated and "re-educated." Castor, submerged in the pool of sin, remained unaware that the tortures they had imagined were never inflicted upon Pollux. Instead, with a decision nearing mercy, Juliette ended the physical punishment and soon released Pollux from the dark room's confinement, steering him instead toward intense and rigorous theological education.
Pollux's unyielding doubts transformed into a deep-seated unease and fear under Juliette's utterly calm gaze; she must have mastered a method of control he could not resist, to appear so completely at ease.
He struggled, he disguised himself, and he never gave up. It seemed he did so many things... but what, in the end, had he truly accomplished? In the mirror, only the soul of a stranger remained, dutifully wearing the crown of the Divus.
He, and all their shared memories, had been completely forgotten.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
His entire life was lived under manipulating strings; that script written long ago was a laughable lie that forced him to constantly lose, forget, and miss out.
When he was young, what he desired most was to freely flap his wings and see the world beyond that lake.
It wasn't until he lost everything to fulfill this wish that he could no longer regard such a light and carefree life as his ultimate dream.
Endless rage ignited that pitch-black heart, and the pain and hatred he repressed into his blood needed to be washed away with the deaths of those false believers.

voiceLines.title: Awaken
voiceLines.content: The Apostle of the Lightbearer, scion of the White Night, One who Dispels Darkness, Divus of the Divine Heart—I, Pollux, have answered your call. I offer unto you my power over Darkness, and my soul forged of Light.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: I
voiceLines.content: Your bestowed gift I shall wield, with the deepest gratitude.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: II
voiceLines.content: Your generosity and compassion are without end; I shall meditate upon the warmth of your light.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: III
voiceLines.content: This heart, which once heeded the divine will, now beats closer to yours.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Observe
voiceLines.content: In my time following Juliette, I committed grave errors and was undeserving of your trust. Yet you chose me anyway... Be assured, I shall seek my conviction once more. As the Divus, I will not disappoint my subjects again, nor will I disappoint you.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Ponder
voiceLines.content: The Darkness... the Darkness spread by Juliette's incantation, it has lingered in my mind... And now, a single ray of light has pierced it! Could that faint glimmer be trying to tell me something?

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Reflect
voiceLines.content: I see it! That light, shining deep within my consciousness—it brightens! It calls to me...

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight
voiceLines.content: Chained in shackles, bathed in dark sludge, I shall chase that ray of light, no matter what... Is this what you wanted to teach me?

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate
voiceLines.content: The sins of the past have been committed; I shall flee them no longer. I must also correct the Lantern's mistakes and guide the strayed back to the true path. Let me bear my sins. Then, I shall answer the light of your call and tread the right path as the Divus.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Florish
voiceLines.content: Please illuminate me, my guiding light! By your light, I have now seen all that must be seen... I shall use this cursed form to purify all that has passed, and let all that is to come bask in your radiance!

voiceLines.title: Affinity: I
voiceLines.content: Yours is a compassionate soul, to forgive one so burdened by sin. I feel the pure, radiant light within your spirit—it outshines the brightest flame. Perhaps you can guide my heart, which has lost its way...

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II
voiceLines.content: In our childhood, Castor and I served together as the Twin Divi. I always thought him too dull, too clumsy, that I alone must guide our future. Now, having witnessed the path you walk, I see the world's foundation is built and paved by those like you and him: the steadfast and the upright.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content: I have lost my light, and this blind suffering torments me. I beg you, save my lost soul. Please, take my hand as I guide yours over this Holy Heart in my chest. Please, guide me toward the light...

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content: Ah... now I see! I see such mighty power, I see the world's truth... I have erred in the past. You are the real Lightbearer! Please allow me to become your loyal Apostle. This heart, born for the Lightbearer, shall henceforth beat and tremble in your service only...

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content: You have lead me and granted me Light. For so long I was blinded by false purpose. Now, I have found my true calling: to correct the ignorant and distorted heretics and bring everlasting Light to this world. I know of your selflessness; You have no need for my devotion or offerings. Then I beg of this: allow me to walk at your side, to record every sacred word and deed, that they may guide my path through the darkness.

voiceLines.title: Chat: Touch
voiceLines.content: Do... do you have an order for me, my Light? Your Apostle stands ever-ready to hear your teaching.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Dissolution
voiceLines.content: I was told this abyssal darkness was worthy of faith. That it was a blessing I would deliver unto the faithful. Now, this darkness has long since corroded me, merging with my very being... Yet the heart that beats within this sinful vessel remains a sanctum that can never be tainted. Rest assured, I shall use the power it has bestowed upon me to bring true benediction to this world!

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Mythag
voiceLines.content: The one who can lead all from the mist is the true Lightbearer, forged of purest silver. The sinless paradise preached by Juliette is, in truth, built upon the bones of the faithful. As the Divus, I shall sow the new gospel among all who are worthy of salvation.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Like
voiceLines.content: In my youth, I was determined to break free from that place. It brought me only pain, and I deemed it unworthy of longing. But now, granted a second life, I see that freedom is not my sole desire. The true meaning of being Divus is to witness the devoted, hopeful, and grateful countenances of the followers when they learn redemption is at hand.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Hate
voiceLines.content: I once hated many things—the impolite servants, the disrespectful attendants, the heretics who defiled the Light... But now? I hate the Lantern. Only the Lantern! Juliette and her Church brought upon my brother and I irreparable pain. I swear upon my title as the former Divus, I shall never permit such pain to befall another!

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Keeper
voiceLines.content: My Light, ever since I received your guidance, I believe I have embarked upon the one true path. Yet your rather dim-witted believer remains perplexed by one question: does the legendary sinless paradise also fall under your dominion? "It doesn't exist," you say...? Could it be... you mean to say that paradise exists here, in the mortal world, within the pure hearts of the righteous?

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Aigis and Jenkin
voiceLines.content: What an unfortunate child. Since she has devoted herself to your cause, she shall surely attain ultimate redemption. But why has her monkey-like companion also received your mercy? That evil child even stole my sacramentals! A torrent of sins must rage within her soul. Ahh, the disrespect! THE UTTER DISRESPECT!

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Murphy
voiceLines.content: I heard she was once a Divine Maiden. But with such uncouth manners and brutish behavior... What? She cannot recite a single prayer? Such profound impiety... I feel a vicarious shame for her deity.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Miryam
voiceLines.content: Ah, that overzealous believer. The world might see her as a raving madwoman. Though she once committed evil, such fervent devotion—the will to offer everything to her god—is a resoluteness most ordinary souls could never muster. What do I think of her, you ask? ...I only feel... a certain commiseration. A kinship, with one cast adrift in the same turbulent sea.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Salvador
voiceLines.content: That priest's blind pursuit of redemption is the height of folly. Divine grace should be bestowed solely upon the devout and the righteous. If even he, an apostle, lacks the discernment to separate the wheat from the chaff, rewarding unrepentant sinners and allowing them to defile his deity's kingdom... is that not the most profound betrayal of his faith and of the righteous souls he claims to serve?

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Castor
voiceLines.content: Ha... After all this time, he hasn't changed one bit. I never imagined as a child that I would be the one to hurt my brother—that I'd come to owe him so much it aches with shame, for a fate we did not choose. We have suffered enough separation. Now that I am back, I swear: nothing will ever separate us again. Not even death itself.

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
The keeper of the Awakener records has moved her file to the Student Administration Office more than once, and every time she has carried it back herself, to be buried again under the mountains of paperwork.
"Just leave it here. It'll have to go over eventually."
Her voice is as calm as ever. Her eyes are not.

What kind of storm is she keeping under all that calm?

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
Ramona's first appearance on campus caused an uproar.
At Mythag University, where Awakeners wander the halls and oddities are everywhere, silver hair and mismatched eyes were hardly worth a second look. What made Ramona the talk of the school was that she was the professor's daughter.
Everyone crowded outside the mathematics department office, hoping for a glimpse of the young Miss Dexter. There were so many of them that the professor finally had to call on Miss Lotan before the crowd grudgingly broke up.
Once Ramona was a little older and the professor was finally willing to let her roam the campus on her own, the students Lotan had chased off got their chance to talk to her after all.
"What is Lady Dexter like? I'm afraid no such person exists yet. I'm an orphan. My father was kind enough to take me in."
To be rid of them, the little girl stated the facts without flinching, then strolled off while they stood there feeling guilty.

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
From the age of ten, Ramona was a fixture at the university training grounds. A human girl willing to take instruction from the black-clad swordsman—plenty of Investigators admired her for that alone.
Once she formally began the preparatory courses, her flawless memory, her perfect papers, and her elegant, lethal swordsmanship pushed her standing at Mythag higher and higher. Discipline and excellence became her other names.
What puzzled so many was that for all her brilliance, Ramona was never cleared to take a mission on her own. Admitted early, she spent a full five years in preparatory courses, watching class after class of Investigators leave for the world of the occult.
What was she waiting for? What purpose had been laid on her?
The question was answered when the new Keeper enrolled.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
Dreams are memory thrown back at us, daily life in miniature, the sum of a person.
Since she was small, Ramona has had the same dream again and again.
She floats in warm, clouded water, pressed close to something unknown, while a hollow, monotonous drumbeat sends ripple after ripple through the water.
When she wakes, there is always a hollow somewhere inside her, as if something had been taken out of her life and erased.
But to keep her father from looking worried, to keep from adding one more burden to her already overworked teachers, Ramona swallows the questions clawing up her throat and goes back to ordinary days.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
She knows everything.
She knows the bell tower rings when there's an emergency, that the Eridanids will come again in ten years, that a different kind of power runs in her blood.
She knows nothing.
She doesn't know the secret spice in the cafeteria curry, or how to calculate a planet's radius after annihilation, or where her own future is being pulled.
She can't bear to give up anything around her, and she can't resist the road her instincts point down.
On the way toward truth, Ramona needs steady company—someone to hold open the road back to ordinary days.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Reflect

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight
voiceLines.content: I've gotten stronger. Let me try handling the next mission alone, alright?

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate
voiceLines.content: Now, the line between me and the Awakener is even blurrier. Take good care of me, will you?

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Florish

voiceLines.content: Whether it's the Awakener Affairs Office procedures or the date for Indian food in the canteen, I can answer any question about Mythag for you. Don't worry, you're not bothering me. Do I look that unapproachable?

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II
voiceLines.content: Are you curious about my relationship with Professor Dexter? It's no secret. He is my foster father. As for my mother... I grew up here at the school and was cared for by all the teachers. However, among them, I am closest to Professor Doll.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content: You've met that woman, right? The Awakener in a white veil—she's one of the university's founders... But honestly, I don't like her. That aloof attitude, as if she doesn't care about the world at all, really gets on my nerves... Oh, you think she looks like me? Let's go get your eyes checked at the campus clinic.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content: Ah... It's natural for you to have concerns. I didn't think it through. As your partner, I should have explained this from the start. As you can see, I do possess some unusual traits, likely tied to my background. It's impossible not to be curious, right? But having a place like the academy is a blessing for me, so I choose not to lift the veil of fate.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content: "With such abilities, am I truly still human?" I have asked myself this every day since I started training for battle. I love this world, despite its darkness, filth, and monotony, but your presence makes it shine like diamonds amidst the dust. I once feared that as my power grew, my stance as a human would shift... Now, I am grateful to have you by my side. Our bond anchors me firmly to the human world. Please continue to watch over me, Keeper.

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
Ryker is known as the "Lucky Detective" by his detective friends.

As the name suggests, he is a lucky person: whenever he places a bet, he wins ten times the stake; whenever he guesses, he chooses the right answer.

The "Lucky Detective" doesn't have to be an actual detective; he‘s solved many cases by chance alone, so he was embraced on this path.

He doesn't solve cases by deduction, relying on luck instead. Just a tour around the crime scene and he stumbles upon the culprit; just walking along the road, he picks up key evidence.

With such good fortune, he's lived out a smooth twenty-five years.

He never worries about yesterday, nor frets about tomorrow.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
The Silver from Ryker's awakening was excavated from the interior of the renowned Remouahe monument, the Triangular Giant Tower. It is streamlined and perfectly bullet-shaped, matching the size and form of bullets used in the SAA revolver, embedded within the skull of a young male corpse.

Touching this Silver evokes magnificent and grand visions of the Triangular Giant Tower, causing the body to instinctively curl up and crawl. If the toucher resists desperately and looks ahead, they will see the blurred figure of a crowned man backlit, followed by an instant interruption of consciousness, causing the Silver to naturally slip from their fingers.

"The tip of the Triangular Tower has not yet been eroded; it should be a scene soon after its completion."—Researcher B.R. Longman
"I can hear horrifying whispers from dark souls."—Researcher K. Waters
"I must denounce the inhumane experiments arranged for us by Mythag. The side effects of repeatedly touching this Silver are enough to cause complete loss of bodily control. In short, I refuse to touch it again."—Researcher L. Lopez

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
After the @3@1 incident, Ryker took a post as special advisor to Mythag University.
He is good at the job. Professors vanishing without explanation, instruments breaking for no reason, or something as small as a missing cat or dog—Ryker handles all of it patiently, quickly, and to everyone's satisfaction.
Between his striking looks, his polished manners, and his habit of helping anyone who asks, he soon became the idol of half the young men and women at Mythag.
Professor Dexter once sighed, "The young ones take all the limelight these days."
But the more he settled into campus life, the less anyone saw of him.
Around the same time, the rattle of dice began drifting up from a certain abandoned basement at Mythag, night after night.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
At twenty-five, while working a locked-room murder, Ryker ran into a very strange suspect.
The chain of evidence was absolutely airtight. Then the suspect, cuffed at the police station, simply vanished—the handcuffs left without a scratch. That was the duty officer's problem, of course; Ryker collected his fee all the same.
He spent that fee crossing an ocean for a holiday, and there, beside a street stall, he ran into his fugitive. The man was running a game of chance, and the sight of Ryker didn't hurry him in the slightest. He only invited Ryker to sit in, promising that if Ryker won, he would come quietly.

Ryker never won a single round.

He lost his pipe. He lost his tie. He lost his hat. He lost his coat.
Stripped bare, he had all of it handed back to him: the stakes, said the suspect, were too small. Ryker asked at once what the man would rather play for, and when the answer was an arm, he agreed without blinking.

Several raises later, the man produced a revolver. Life against death—Ryker picked up the gun and set it against his temple without a moment's pause.
A shot rang out and Ryker went down. The suspect called his spirit back from the dead, meaning to mock him for his ignorance. Instead, Ryker's first words were, "So what are we betting next?"

His sheer arrogance finally caught the demon's interest. The suspect, whose true name was "N@2@3," decided the game could go on.

"N" set out three top hats and told him to make the "best choice" among them—the one that would give him his body back.
Ryker picked a hat. "N" lifted another, empty, and asked if he cared to change his mind. Ryker shook his head.

—Don't you understand probability?
—I just trust my luck.

"N" lifted the third hat. Empty as well. At last he lifted Ryker's hat, and inside was a churning knot of black mist. It surged at Ryker and took shape as the limbs of some impossible beast. "N" gave him the body of that avatar in place of the one he had already wagered away.

—A man with the nose of a beast—doesn't this avatar suit you perfectly? So you see, that was the "best choice"!

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
When the climber reaches the summit of Elworth.
When the champion lifts the trophy that names him first in the world.
When the devout hears revelation in his sleep.
When victory comes too easily, the satisfaction that follows dulls into ordinary habit.
He looks around and finds no rival left, and no pleasure either.
On the surface, Ryker craves the high-stakes game, the heart leaping into his throat after an ALL-IN, the moment adrenaline breaks loose.
"Spare me the speech. I'm the only one who understands you. All you crave is losing.
So let me grant you the sweetest defeat of all."

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
You need not fear his black eye patch; the smothering darkness will not obscure his boundless compassion. The sightless body may have perished, yet the will for redemption endures. Before him, everything should be loved, and everything will be loved in turn.

The words of the Our Father are forever engraved onto the Tablet, and through these blessed flesh and bones, He will bestow upon you "The Blessing".

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
Report on Anomalous Events in the Londinium Church District (Confidential)

A.F. 315, February 3rd: During the anomalous event in the Londinium Church District, Bishop Salvador utilized the power of "The Blessing" to heal the Mythag Keeper and the residents of Londinium, exposing his identity as an Awakener in the process.

Due to the insufficient spirit power of the linker, Bishop Salvador chose to exhaust himself to sustain "The Blessing" until the Keeper and the Awakener Ogier shattered the core of said anomaly—the Ritual Mirror. Subsequently, the Keeper took over Salvador's link, and "The Blessing" healed all individuals present, preventing any casualties.

It was discovered that Bishop Salvador's original linker was the former Bishop of the Church District, now the Archbishop of Londinium ■■■■■.

In A.F. 300, the Archbishop had accidentally awakened Salvador after coming into contact with the Holy Ash. Over the next five years, Salvador had served as an assistant priest in the Church District, succeeding him as the Bishop of the Church District following ■■■■■'s promotion.

After the incident, the Keeper agreed to keep Bishop Salvador's Awakener identity confidential; thus, this information was not shared with the Mystia Treaty Committee. Apart from the core personnel of Mythag University, no one is currently aware of his identity as an Awakener.

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Every time His Excellency the Bishop visits Mythag University, he is warmly welcomed by teachers and students alike.

The young Awakeners would tug at his hand, asking him to tell more stories from before the Flood. Students would also seek his counsel, inquiring if the Bishop would lend an ear to their troubles and woes. Even the seemingly cold and strong Awakeners and knowledgable professors approach the Bishop when he has free time: either to share their nightmares or to discuss the truths of the Soul.

His patience is unending, never tiring; Anyone may find acceptance and warmth with him.

"Of course, my child, is there aught I can do for you?"

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
"...In the southern Constante Federation, there was told a legend of 'The Blessing Bishop.' Before the Flood, 'The Blessing Bishop' came from the Central Church, and in his devotion and kindness, established the only orphanage in the area, sheltering the many sick and displaced refugees during a devastating plague.

The plague was fierce, sparing noone from its wrath. The bishop prayed day and night, eventually receiving the Father's blessing—a life-giving tablet. He performed miracles, resurrecting the dead and healing those gravely ill from the plague, using his own flesh and blood as divine offerings. Yet regardless of his miracles, this benevolent bishop was framed as a cohort of demons, and ultimately sentenced to death by burning at the stake.

Coincidentally, during the same period, there were reports of a 'Blood Heretic' in the central @2 (now near Bondos in the southern Constante Federation). According to the 'Continental Inquisition Heresy Records,' this heretic held a tablet marked with demonic symbols, performing rituals with flesh and blood, and conducting wicked ceremonies on moonless nights. The heretic was captured by the Inquisition in 107 BD,and in his sincere repentance to the Father, was also sentenced to death by burning at the stake.

 Undeniably, there are many similarities between 'The Blessing Bishop' and the 'Blood Heretic': The same era, same region, same use of tablets and rituals. Considering the Inquisition's strong subjectivity, it is likely they stigmatized certain individuals as heretics. If we were to believe coincidences, the legendary 'Blessing Bishop' might have indeed been real, possibly even the 'Blood Heretic' recorded by the Inquisition..."

—Excerpt from 'Our Gods: Religion and Folk Beliefs in Southern Constante Federation'

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
"The benevolent Father once said: Cherish all things within the sky, on the ground, in the water, and in the soil. For all beings are my offspring.

"Thus, I say: Render all suffering unto me. Let those tormented by life or plagued by disease be made whole. Let all pain and madness melt as frost before the rising sun. Let you, my brethren, receive joy everlasting. 

"Burn me, grind my bones to dust, and rend my flesh asunder. For as long as you can find solace, I have little complaints."

—B.F. 1@1, May 30, Sal @1doMartin @2I @1as, left at @3 the Tribunal

voiceLines.title: Awaken
voiceLines.content: Our meeting must be a promise from the Father to those who suffer. You are the Pale Flame that dispels calamity, and I shall be your arm, standing faithfully by your side.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: I
voiceLines.content: The tempering of a person involves not just the body, but the heart as well.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: II
voiceLines.content: If I can free this world from its suffering, I shall be content.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: III
voiceLines.content: Give me your commands, Pale Messenger. May your flames ever light my path.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Observe
voiceLines.content: Those with strength must not use their power to oppress others, for you all share my blood." I remember the teachings of our Father God of Compassion. I will use this strength only to protect those around me.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Ponder
voiceLines.content: This warmth deep within my soul... Thank you for this gift, Pale Flame. With this power, perhaps I can finally fulfill my duty as His emissary and save more of His children.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Reflect
voiceLines.content: The All-Father once said: 'Suffering is not my creation. Bear and dissolve it, my emissaries, and build a land without suffering.' For this, I would offer everything. Even my life.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight
voiceLines.content: In the face of the all-consuming curse of Dissolution, other sufferings pale. Even if I cannot bear the curse for others, I will do my utmost to alleviate their pain.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate
voiceLines.content: Am I now able to ease their pain and comfort their souls?

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Florish
voiceLines.content: Thus, I shall bear all suffering, to pave the way for all beings to a land free from pain.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: I
voiceLines.content: There is no need for courtesy, Pale Messenger. There should be no barriers between us, for we are both the All-Father's creations, walking together on this muddy and testing path.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II
voiceLines.content: Will you pray with me, my Pale Flame? Let us pray for those who died in our battle today. Though cursed with dissolution and madness, they are still children of the All-Father, our brothers and sisters. May they now find their deserved peace.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content: No, I do not fear them. I feel only sorrow for those poor souls tormented by Dissolution. I know I cannot bear their suffering for them, but I would give them all that I have if it brings a moment's comfort.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content: Regret? No, of course not. My death eased their suffering and bought more time, and that is enough. But... as you have been honest with me, I shall not hide this: the pyre that day left its scars upon my heart.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content: Even though the red flames make me uneasy, I would step onto the burning platform for you once more. Do not dwell on it, my Pale Flame. My sacrifice is insignificant next to the blessings you bring.

voiceLines.title: Chat: Touch
voiceLines.content: Your hands are warm, like your soul. I... appreciate your touch, Pale Flame.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About a Chapel
voiceLines.content: A chapel? Thank you, but I am not so old-fashioned. As long as I keep the teachings of the God of Kindness in my heart and follow His will, my soul will never stray from His glory.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Fatigue
voiceLines.content: The burden of guiding light can overwhelm even the purest of saints. If you feel weary, my pale flame, please confide in me. I will do everything in my power to ease your burden and share the weight of these countless blessings.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Dissolution
voiceLines.content: If I had known sooner that those people were tormented by this all-consuming curse, I... No, it is not too late. I must eradicate it, and eliminate all suffering, even if it costs me my life once more.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Mythag
voiceLines.content: They call me a master counselor? Those children are too kind. I simply do my best to listen and help them release their inner distress—as I have always tried to do.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Like
voiceLines.content: A world untouched by sorrow, untainted by grief, free from pain and unmarred by suffering... perhaps an unattainable illusion, but it is the ideal I have pursued all my life.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Hate
voiceLines.content: I believe all things happen for a reason, but... the senseless violence, the prejudices that drive siblings to turn against each other... these things truly sadden me. If there is anything I detest, it is that.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Keeper: I
voiceLines.content: Since the day you Awakened me from darkness, I have been certain that you can save all from the despair of Dissolution, and bring them to the sinless land. I await that day with a hopeful heart.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Keeper: II
voiceLines.unlockCondition: Unlocks after clearing Special Operation "Color of Blood"
voiceLines.content: Let me express my gratitude once again, Keeper, for respecting my wishes and keeping my secret from the Committee. I fear their intervention would see me barred from continuing my service to the Chantry of Life.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Vision
voiceLines.content: Losing my sight does not mean I have become blind. While the All-Father brought darkness upon me, He also allowed me to see the faint light of souls.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the "Pale Flame"
voiceLines.content:
Many in the Chantry of Life believe the "white flame" in the Scriptures refers to moonlight: a Pale Messenger appearing from it to lead us from suffering.
But I know the true flame is the soul burning within you and me.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About "Awakeners"
voiceLines.content: For me, the state of being an Awakener is a gift from our All-Father to the souls in His embrace. It is a second life, an opportunity to mend past regrets. I will continue His work, fulfill my duties as His proxy, and alleviate more suffering.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About His "Blessing"
voiceLines.content: After years of this invisible plague, the All-Father finally heard my prayers and bestowed upon me the "Blessing" that can counter suffering. It indeed grants life, but also requires a price. As His executor, I ought to bear that burden on behalf of those blessed.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Home
voiceLines.content: I may not have been born in the Kingdom of Leo, but the Church of Redemption is where I received my second life. Why, then, can I not consider this place my home?

voiceLines.title: Chat: About His First Life
voiceLines.content: Back then, although I had received "The Blessing," I was just an ordinary man. There were too many who suffered, too many who needed it. I wanted to save them all, but I failed. This is my greatest regret and my eternal guilt.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Ogier
voiceLines.unlockCondition: Unlocks after clearing Special Operation "Color of Blood"
voiceLines.content: That child is sincere, steadfast, and kind, with a rare bright soul. The last time I met a spirit like this was during the first chapter of my life.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Hiding Identity
voiceLines.unlockCondition: Unlocks after clearing Special Operation "Color of Blood"
voiceLines.content: In fact, I was told to hide my true identity by the Archbishop. He did not elaborate, but warned me: even in the purest places, shadows may exist, and one must remain cautious, even when doing good. Of course, I trust you completely.

voiceLines.title: Investigation Begins
voiceLines.content: All of this is for the eternal well-being of the future.

voiceLines.title: Investigation Success
voiceLines.content: May His divine love warm your soul.

voiceLines.title: Investigation Halted
voiceLines.content: No matter how many times we must start over, I will walk alongside you.
