storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
The weaver ensnared by her own web; the playwright and eternal spectator of the Theater of Fate. 

Threads cascade from Arachne's fingertips, twining into curtains, scripts, and cages—each strand spun by her own hand, only to shroud her in an inescapable cocoon. 

The auditorium remains forever vacant, with none but herself to gaze upon the solitary performance onstage—a drama repeating without end, a play that knows no final curtain. She is the phantom haunting the theater, and the very incarnation of Fate itself.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
In the late autumn of A.F. 3@7, I traveled to the "Theater of Fate" in the old district to audition for a mezzo-soprano position.	

I arrived at 4:17 PM. The sky was gloomy, yet no rain fell. The main entrance was unlocked, and the auditorium stood empty; there was no sign of any interviewers.	

Yet at the center of the stage, a puppet show was unfolding—there was no puppeteer, no music, only several pale humanoid marionettes dancing in silence. Their movements were unnervingly precise, and the faint clicking of their joints as they turned was spine-chilling. As for the strings... those threads descending from the dome seemed alive; they trembled slightly, tightening and slackening as if keeping time with an invisible rhythm.	

Just as I turned to leave, a woman’s voice drifted down from Box Five.	

<Italic:"Welcome, Christine.">

The voice was neither young nor old; it sounded like an echo seeping through dust-laden silk curtains sealed for centuries—eerie and terrifying.	

A cold shiver ran through me. I hadn't even introduced myself; how did she know my name? And these puppets...	

I bolted for the exit, but just as my hand reached for the handle, countless spiders swarmed from the darkness. Their eyes glimmered with ghostly light as they spewed out silvery threads, attempting to block my escape. More horrifying still, the spiders began to speak in human voices, chanting over and over: <Italic:"Sing, my angel... sing for me...">

I screamed. I tore at the webs. I ran with all my might. Somehow, I managed to escape.

...

Since then, I could not bear the thought of any gaze cast down from VIP Box Five, and so I requested that the opera house have the box sealed.	

And yet... now, whenever I stand beneath the spotlight and sing, I feel the faint tug of strings at the tips of my brow.	

Have I, too, become a puppet manipulated by invisible strings? I dare not think on it further.

—Excerpt from <Italic:The Memoirs of Christine, the Singer>

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
The curtain had not yet fully risen when the stage lights cascaded down like a relentless tide.

The audience of Mythag held their breath, waiting for the hero of fate to take the stage.

The stage was small—so small it could barely accommodate the heavy tread of Oedipus. Yet, as the boy in the school uniform raised his hand, his voice pierced the silence of that modest stage, his opening line falling like a divine oracle: <Italic:"It is I, the wretched man, doomed to slay my father and wed my mother.">
...

<Italic:"What law of the mighty gods have I transgressed?

 Why look to the heavens any more, tormented as I am?

 Whom to call, what comrades now? Just think, my reverence only brands me for irreverence!" >

So questioned the young Antigone, challenging the injustice of divine law.

...

In the castle of Denmark, Hamlet paced in contemplation. <Italic:"To be, or not to be, that is the question: Whether 'tis nobler in the mind to suffer the slings and arrows of outrageous fortune, or to take arms against a sea of troubles, and by opposing end them?">
...

Before the high bench, John Proctor slowly lifted his head and declared his answer: <Italic:"Because I am not worth the dust on the feet of them that hang! How may I live without my name?">
...

Those words concerning fate had coalesced into today’s performance.

Arachne stood in the wings, her fingers digging unconsciously into her palms.

The tears shed in empathy for the characters, the thunderous applause at the final curtain call...

As she took in the myriad of faces in the audience, she suddenly felt that her heart—whose beating she had long ceased to regard—had finally found its rhythm.

At this very moment, her voice, her very existence, was etched into the vast current of fate. She was no longer a mere witness to destinies; she was now the unfolding lines of a brand-new script. Audience, performer, playwright—their fates had become inextricably bound through this living drama...

The triumph of the heart, it turned out, was this quiet—and this deafening.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
At first, Arachne did not know she could see Fate.

The world, like everyone and everything around her, was blurred, clamorous, and ruled by chance.

At the age of two, she spoke her very first word.

It was not "Mama," nor was it "Papa." Instead, standing beneath the porch, she whispered a single "Goodbye" to the old family butler.

That night, the butler died of a heart attack. Clutching the pocketwatch he had left behind, she wept herself to sleep outside the lodge. She did not yet understand death or destiny, but she had already tasted the bitter sting of a future revealed too soon.

At five, amidst the flushed faces and raucous cheers of banquet guests, she mimicked her mother, rising on tiptoe for a clumsy waltz.

Her red dancing shoes were as vivid as blood—an omen in plain sight. When she tripped during a turn, no one noticed the flash of a vision in her eyes, as if the fall itself had been destined.

On her seventh birthday, her father gifted her a spinning wheel named "Moirae," after the three Goddesses of Fate. She ran through the woods, her laughter bright and unguarded—until she tripped, and heard the crack: the spinning wheel was broken.

She knelt among the fallen leaves, tracing the fracture with her fingers, and she suddenly saw it: countless threads surging from the break, coiling around her fingertips and stretching into the invisible distance.

Then came the "firsts"—her first time in an opera house, her first true friend, the first time she buried a beloved dog...

Every "first" was haunted by a silent final act flashing before her eyes. She began to understand: every opening scene already carried the shape of its finale.

From then on, her gaze could no longer rest on surfaces. Human faces became mere veils, through which she could peer at the destinies churning beneath. She knew who would wither at the end of summer, who would hang themselves on the eve of their wedding, and whose child would bury them ten years hence. Surprise died; anticipation withered. 

The "future" was nothing more than an obituary she had opened ahead of time.

She tried, at first, to warn those around her of the misfortunes to come. But every time the words left her lips, they only hastened the prophecy's fulfillment.

Seeing the terror and recoil in their eyes, she finally grasped the truth: To foresee is not to forestall.

The Web of Fate was already woven. Her "foresight" was merely a stray beam of light slipping through the mesh—it illuminated the end, but was powerless to alter the weave.

And so, she took up the spinning wheel named "Moirae" again.

The break had been mended, but the scar remained. Day after day she spun, and her gift for fate merged itself into the wheel in ways she could not explain.

From that moment, the destinies of all flowed and intertwined through her fingers, woven into a colossal web spanning space and time.

Imperceptibly, she too was ensnared within this eternal web. She bore witness to laughter and grief beyond counting; infinite turning points, infinite possibilities, each one dragging its foredoomed destruction to the stage again and again...

Yet Arachne would not stop—not to weave, but to sustain. Should she cease, the entire Web of Fate might unravel, dragging countless lives into nothingness along with it. But she also saw that when the web was finally complete, Its awakening would bring devastation nothing could avert...

She is the weaver and the captive, the spectator and the prisoner, the playwright and the player.

Is it a blessing or a curse to see the ends of others?

Arachne stopped asking long ago.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
As the Weaver of the Web of Fate, Arachne governed the threads of countless lives, with past and future flowing through her hands. Yet, she harbored a hobby that bordered on the frivolous. 

She loved the theater. Not for the twisting plot or the well-turned phrase: those were already etched into her mind. As the creator of the script, she knew every turn of the story and every line of the actors by heart. 

Yet, time and again, she stepped into the theater. 

What she truly craved was the immersive sense of "presence"—the feeling of truly being there. 

When the curtain rises and the audience sinks into darkness, the stage becomes the only true world. In that moment, time is no longer a river running in a single direction, but an enactment within a confined space—past, present, and future overlap here. Everything ceases to be a script upon a page and becomes a tremor of life unfolding in the living present. 

And she, at last, is no longer the exile gazing at the threads she can never touch. 

Inside the theater, she can briefly seal away her memories. She can step onto the stage as the girl gasping out her final words, or sit among the crowd, granting the actors their freedom. Casting off the prophet’s burden, she allows herself to simply tremble, weep, and hold her breath at every stirring pulse of the performance. Not as a seer, but as a living soul—adopting the posture of the ignorant, breathing in sync with the characters, shattered by a single line. Even knowing the end is written, even knowing the tragedy is foreordained. This illusion allows her a fleeting escape from her sentence as an eternal spectator. 

No longer exiled from fate, but welcomed into it—even for a single instant, even as a phantom. 

This small indulgence was already the most luxurious grace fate could bestow upon Arachne.

voiceLines.title: Awaken
voiceLines.content:
On the grand stage of fate, all souls await their cue within the web of cause and consequence, their joys and sorrows quietly taking shape as the gears turn... 
The curtain has risen, Keeper. This is where your story, and mine, begins.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: I
voiceLines.content: Another thread coming clear.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: II
voiceLines.content: Fate stirs. Its whisper draws near.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: III
voiceLines.content: I have seen it whole at last. The endless web of fate.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Observe
voiceLines.content: The curtain is open for you, and fate's script waits to begin. Tell me: which destined path would you rather walk? A sorrowful ending, or a joyful opening?

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Ponder
voiceLines.content: If comedy is your inclination, <Italic:A Midsummer Night's Dream> would serve you well. I am particularly fond of Puck's mischievous ramblings—hidden inside a sprite's laughter, fate always lets something slip.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Reflect
voiceLines.content: If you would enter the hall of tragedy, allow me to present <Italic:Antigone>. Caught between divine law and mortal decree, every step she takes falls upon threads fate has already spun, until she steps at last into the deep shadow of the stone tomb. It is precisely because those chains cannot be broken that the will burning inside her small frame blazes so vividly against the long night.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight
voiceLines.content: I thought nothing in this world could surprise me anymore... Your taste in theater has left an impression.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate
voiceLines.content: Thank you for accompanying me through so many rising and falling curtains. I will not disappoint you—there are more evenings yet to come that will move you in ways you have not expected.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Florish
voiceLines.content: Everything is a past epilogue. Everything is a new prologue. The new chapter between us waits for you to write it, Keeper.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: I
voiceLines.content: The threads of fate always connect in the shadows... You have disturbed one such thread, and so you have startled me.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II
voiceLines.content: Those threads once flowed in perfect order through my hands... until you appeared, and sent ripples through their course that I had never foreseen.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content: The theater has staged a new romantic comedy, and I have reserved a seat for you among fate's audience. Through every long night where destinies entwine, I shall wait quietly for the moment our stars meet.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content:
If you would allow it... I wish to weave a play that belongs only to you and me. 
No audience, no rehearsal. I simply wish to see how the thread even I cannot read will begin to stir... when you step into the light.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content:
The invisible threads belonging to you and I have long wound tightly around each other, weaving at once a cage and a road.
I cannot see where the cage ends, nor where the road leads.
That is precisely what makes this story so captivating.

voiceLines.title: Chat: Touch
voiceLines.content:
To pull so insistently at fate's threads...

You seem rather eager to read your own story, no?

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Crisis
voiceLines.content:
The tragedy before you is only one glance among countless possibilities.

Beyond fate's curtain lies a stage swallowed in darkness—
lights extinguished, players gone, everything returning to the deep.

But that is not where it ends.
I carry the resolve to endure this thankless labor, until the day the lights return.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Mythag
voiceLines.content:
Upon the threads, I see colors shift through every shade of the rainbow.
They reach across an endless web, spinning boundless worlds and infinite possibility, until it weaves a pattern more beautiful than any that has ever been seen.

In the end—god or mortal, hero or villain—each is guided by those slender threads, rushing headlong toward their destined end beneath fate's unblinking gaze.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Like
voiceLines.content:
I have grown quite fond of this weaving, day after day... In the quiet, repeated pull of each one, I see through to the beginnings and endings of all stories. Watching each curtain fall, I feel at times as though I have risen above fate itself. And yet one cannot escape fate's web, and to only watch leaves, in the end, a hollow feeling.
In those moments, I go to the theater. To perform the sorrows and joys I have spun with my own hands, but never once lived.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Hate
voiceLines.content:
I have never cared for performances that simply repeat themselves. The very reason one steps into a theater is to witness a living stage—one that cannot be recreated.
If it does nothing but turn like clockwork, the stage becomes an ornate cage, and watching becomes nothing more than a tedious pilgrimage toward an ending you already know.
A souless masquerade, no matter how magnificent the production is. What do you think?

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Keeper
voiceLines.content: Every soul's fate is carried along by threads... but yours is a script I cannot decipher. I find myself looking forward to whatever improvisation you will bring to this world.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Sorel
voiceLines.content: She visits my theater often... but I know she does not come for the plays. She seems to use this stage to lend a certain refinement to her own image. Such remarkable skill, though—to spend it only as a spectator seems a waste. That lady is not the kind to bloom in the dark of the audience. She belongs under the light.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Liz
voiceLines.content: What an ill-fated dancer. I have watched her steps. Hers is a beauty that moves toward ruin—every turn igniting green flames, as though trying to burn fate's threads away, though in the end those threads will only carve something achingly vivid from her. If the chance arises, I would like to write a ballet just for her.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Hameln
voiceLines.content: I once heard him play. That music made the soul tremble... Perhaps I should invite him to compose a symphony of fate for my next production.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Tinct
voiceLines.content: What a gifted singer. A voice given by grace, clear and burning all at once, as though it rises from fate itself. If she were to perform in my theater, I imagine even the most demanding audience would be caught off guard.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Tawil
voiceLines.content: Even one who watches all things remains a clumsy actor in their own script. To hold fate's web, yet be bound by its threads—we walk different roads in this destined circumstance, but neither of us has ever truly abandoned our thankless pursuits. Foolish, perhaps. Deluded, perhaps. So it is with me, and so it is with her.

voiceLines.title: Investigation Begins
voiceLines.content: The conflict is here. Will you play the hero who breaks the web, or the player who moves only as the strings allow?

voiceLines.title: Investigation Success
voiceLines.content: Another story, beautifully complete, draws to its close.

voiceLines.title: Investigation Halted
voiceLines.content: No ending is ever truly certain, yet none escapes the web of cause and consequence...

voiceLines.title: Strike: I
voiceLines.content: Ah...

voiceLines.title: Strike: II
voiceLines.content: Submit to this.

voiceLines.title: Defense: I
voiceLines.content: Be still...

voiceLines.title: Defense: II
voiceLines.content: Futile resistance.

voiceLines.title: Hit: I
voiceLines.content: An unexpected turn?

voiceLines.title: Hit: II
voiceLines.content: The error must be corrected.

voiceLines.title: Skill: I
voiceLines.content: The threads of fate hang still.

voiceLines.title: Skill: II
voiceLines.content: What was written draws near.

voiceLines.title: Rouse
voiceLines.content: From endless threads, I spin the only path.

voiceLines.title: Exalt
voiceLines.content: Here it is woven. Here it is weighed. Here it is severed.

voiceLines.title: Over-Exalt
voiceLines.content: Fate's prisoner, pitiful as ever... what is written cannot be refused.

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
When all things are eroded by twisted flesh, when the everyday life is overturned, a dandelion drifts down upon this wasteland amid the keening noise. 

Reach out your hand. Take hold of her. Love will break through the surface, and anchor you to the one you love once more.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
Like what is yet to come but has not yet come to pass. Like what is held in the heart and will never be forgotten.

No matter what form they take, no matter what shape the world assumes, the two beings—utterly different, yet utterly alike—will always arrive at the same answer.

<Italic:"There is someone we want to see again."

"We will stop at nothing to find them... and the world where we can stay by their side."

"If the path there has no end, then we will spend our whole lives walking it. A lifetime measured in searching."

>
Perhaps this is why, amid the screeching, ugly blobs of flesh, a brilliant Silver Core fell into the Keeper's palm.

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Saya quickly became a well-liked student. Exceptional capacity for learning and a hunger for knowledge that never seemed to be sated—in Mythag, an Awakener with these qualities was rarer, even, than her unusual state of being.

To everyone's surprise, Saya took a peculiar interest in Ramona. Perhaps it's the bond between Ramona and the Keeper, or perhaps it's the special relationship between Ramona and Dexter—father and daughter, in their own strange way.

Given that Saya's understanding of morality diverges entirely from that of humans, the Academic Affairs Office once offered Ramona special security measures, but she refused.

What the two of them usually talks about, no one knows. But very occasionally, on some warm afternoon, the gentle wind moving across the lawn would join their long, private conversations.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
What exactly is Saya? The key to that answer lies somewhere far beyond reach.

<Italic:"The creature known as Saya manifested in this universe by no coincidence. It is the result of an instinct hardwired into her biology. What that instinct points toward is the ultimate purpose of all life: reproduction. She and her kind are capable of crossing the walls between dimensions, scattering their seeds across the void..."

"...It is theorized that Saya, as an individual, may be an exception even among her own kind. Humanity is a species that has used its intellect to override its instincts. Could that same flaw have been inherited by Saya? In the course of absorbing human ways, the contradictions between emotion and instinct may have dismantled Saya's reproductive drive..."

"—One day, the blessing of what is called love will find her. The white-hot agape will burn within her, and she will be free to wander the world as her true self, restored to her former radiance.">

Should we judge her by morality? Or by the authenticity of her love?

Perhaps none of it has an answer. Carrying with her the unanswerable questions of another world, Saya arrived in this universe by accident, where none of <Italic:that> has happened yet. Led by the answers living in her memories, she moves forward, toward the far shore of what she has forgotten.

She waits for the day the dandelion blooms.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
She is of a species furthest from humanity—and yet, in learning how to become human, she has grown to resemble them even in the places where she contradicts her own nature.

Without love, the world she was meant to create would mean nothing.

With love, the only world worth creating is one where she could stay with her beloved.

Nothing more terrifying. Nothing more cruel. Nothing more innocent. Nothing more radiant.

voiceLines.title: Awaken

Hello! ...Is that the right way to say it?
I'm Saya, and... nice to meet you!

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: I
voiceLines.content: I'm stuffed. Thanks for the treat!

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: II
voiceLines.content: Thank you for this gift. I'll keep it safe.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: III
voiceLines.content: Well? Gotcha, didn't I?

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Observe
voiceLines.content: I can do stuff like that, you know. Like rearranging or tweaking other creatures' bodies...

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Ponder
voiceLines.content: Every living thing is different, so before you start tweaking things, you really have to study them carefully.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Reflect
voiceLines.content: Yeah, I've studied the structure of Silver Cores, and I'm starting to understand how Awakeners work.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight
voiceLines.content: It seems like "Silver Cores" are each connected to a will from very far away. How mysterious...

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate
voiceLines.content: I've studied Awakener structure quite a lot, so I'd call myself an expert by now. But the "spirituality" inside the Silver Cores... I still don't quite get that part.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Florish
voiceLines.content: After all my tests, I understand a lot more now. The "spirituality" each Awakener carries—they're all completely different. And, it seems like my Silver Core's spirituality is... "love."

voiceLines.title: Affinity: I
voiceLines.content: Yesterday, I found a book called <Italic:The Little Prince> on Lily's bookshelf. It was really good! Do you want to read it?

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II
voiceLines.content:
"<Italic:On one of these stars, my flower is blooming...>"
I feel like you’ve said something like that before.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content: The Little Prince says his rose became special because he took care of it... Do you think so?

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content: Hey, Keeper... have you ever loved someone? Have you ever truly missed someone with all your heart?

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content: You know dandelions, right? The ones that send their seeds out on the wind. A little seed gets carried far, far away from its homeland... and maybe it lands in a desert where nothing grows at all—not a single blade of grass. I wonder... what might that single, little seed feel...?

voiceLines.title: Chat: Touch
voiceLines.content: You're not scared of me? Aww... that's no fun...

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Crisis
voiceLines.content: Certain threats out there could bring darkness great enough to destroy this world, right? I know. Professor Doll told me all about it.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Mythag
voiceLines.content: Whenever I'm next to you, strange people would just show up and gather around us. I actually prefer it when it was just the two of us in the Domain.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Like
voiceLines.content: I love good food! And I like people who are kind to me! When someone's gentle with me... it just makes me really happy.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Hate
voiceLines.content: I don't like people who are rough. They give me a bad feeling...

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Keeper
voiceLines.content: Keeper, Link, Awakener. That's how we're connected. You told me about it. I can feel our souls linked together... like a silver thread? Hmm, sounds a bit too complicated...

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Thais
voiceLines.content: Spreading seeds through flesh and blood? Hmm... interesting. I'm kind of curious about her sheep, actually.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Tinct
voiceLines.content: She's the one who awakened me? She looks really... dazzling. So, did you help her find her sister?

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Winkle
voiceLines.content: Oh? So her kind breeds on new planets by preying on other species. Huh, I see...

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
The heroic epic destined to soar across the night sky was broken mid-flight. He chose to plunge into the abyss, offering himself up to an existence far greater and more inscrutable.
Never again would he face the pangs of parting, the sting of mediocrity, or the inescapable ravages of time.
His kin, his friends, and even his foes—he has kept them all forever within Ebwynnos, a realm now fused with his very being.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
In August of A.F. 2@17, a series of anomalous spiritual events manifested within a three-mile radius of Nara@1Bay.
@1 recorded emergency calls reported sightings of several individuals, previously registered as deceased, lingering near the ruins of @3. These individuals were later verified to have all perished in the explosion that struck @2 Port Town in 1@19. The cause of that explosion remains unconfirmed to this day, and all individuals involved exhibited varying degrees of amnesia.
<Italic:"I saw her, I swear... she was as young as the day we parted. But that's impossible.">
<Italic:"It's been @2 years since she bade me farewell, yet she remained as beautiful as ever. She just stood there on the cliffside with the others, smiling at me from afar.">
<Italic:"...When we are cherished, we will always be granted a second chance. EBWYN@2OS... Ebwy@1noss...">
The recording concluded with an unidentified static resembling the churning of seawater. Twenty hours later, the witness died at home of organ failure at the age of 76.
The day after this material reached Mythag University, Irene Caldwell—a retired researcher from the Awakening Studies Department and distant relative of the witness, Chambers Caldwell—received an O-@1 Silver Core that Chambers had delivered to her.
According to Irene, Chambers looked no different from his younger self.
He left only one sentence before vanishing:
"Please take Him to Mythag. He shall wait there for the last wanderer of Ebwynnos to return."
—Excerpt from <Italic:Mythag University Silver Core Storage Records>

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Most faculty and students at Mythag are more than happy to seek Pontos’s aid during field missions, and he never hesitates to lend a helping hand.
Generous, genial, and dependable—even though he is clearly at serious odds with certain members of Mythag, this Awakener leaves a staggeringly positive first impression.
However, while Pontos has agreed with Mythag to stop expanding the "population" of Ebwynnos, a flood of migration applications have poured into the Administration Office following several field operations that ended in "unconventional ways."
While Sylvia conducts group counseling for the applicants, the administration has hastily added two new field regulations:
1. Except in extreme emergencies, seeking aid from Pontos is strictly prohibited.
2. Except in extreme circumstances, entry into Ebwynnos is strictly prohibited.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
Pontos spent a long time tracing the cause of Leisha’s death. She had endured far too many grueling battles and claimed far too many glorious victories—perhaps by poison, perhaps by some obscure sorcery; surely there had to be a reason, a reason for her to fall before such a feeble sea monster.
It was only much, much later, when a single strand of silver appeared in the hair of a human companion who had never joined Ebwynnos, that the truth finally dawned on him.
The waning stamina, the slowing responses, the unspoken but palpable longing for a peaceful, settled life... it was all so familiar.
And all at once, Pontos understood the name of the enemy that had eluded him all this time: "Aging."
It's the reason for Leisha's seclusion, her defeat, and the ruin of everything he might have lived for—it was something so commonplace, yet utterly inexorable.
But it mattered no longer. His own destruction had come early, and the power he gained in exchange was more than satisfactory.
No matter what unfathomable entity he must serve, whatever the price he must pay, the ravages of time shall never befall Ebwynnos again.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
<Italic:"Is it that you won't allow aging—or that you won't allow anything beyond your control?">
He did not answer, nor did he need to.
The abyss had chosen him long before the disaster struck, for his unspoken obsessions aligned perfectly with the abyss itself.
Obedience, companionship, and stasis... he was as inescapable as the abyss: suffocating all things, yet preserving them for eternity.

voiceLines.title: Awaken
voiceLines.content:
Seek you a feast, a hunt, or sanctuary?
Pray to me—the primeval ocean will speak my name.
I am Pontos, Lord of the Great Abyss.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: I
voiceLines.content: Smart move, kid. The followers of that foreign monster are thick enough to always toss corpses into the sea. That's not an offering. That's littering.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: II
voiceLines.content: Let's hope these little things don't eat you out of house and home. You know, feeding a large family is no easy feat.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: III
voiceLines.content: Uh, not that I did that, but if you ever hear the sound of seawater and the rustle of wings inside your head—don't worry about it. It's perfectly normal.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Observe
voiceLines.content: In Ebwynnos, the revelry never ends. And Ebwynnos's enemies will never know rest.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Ponder
voiceLines.content: Skin, muscle, nerve, bone—my whole body is being reconstructed. I feel whole and vital again.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Reflect
voiceLines.content:
Spirituality gives rise to a new body, which is then filled with a trivial mind. Then those particularlt bright and lively ones will be gathered in one place, forever.
Remember what I told you? The deepest part of the ocean holds everything... and keeps everything there.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight
voiceLines.content: Ah, I understand that shudder. But it's entirely unnecessary, my young friend. Accept your fear of mediocrity, of being slowly worn down. Look at me. You know you always have another choice.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate
voiceLines.content: Aging is the only adventure you must face alone. It's your best friend, and your most troublesome foe. But the lights of Ebwynnos will drive it all away... you don't need to be shackled by such worthless memories.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Florish
voiceLines.content: Such a pity. When you change your mind, you know where to find me.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: I
voiceLines.content: Those slimy fish-people are no friends of mine. They're my enemies. Surprised? The ocean never belonged to them anyway.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II
voiceLines.content:
Long, long before the land rose from the sea, certain presences stirred within this planet. They're mighty, sovereign, unfathomable.
Neither malice nor mercy could define Them. Humans, like countless creatures that came before, meant nothing to Them. You could be swept away like dust, or protected as part of their territory.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content: Prayer works. Think of it this way: If ants arranged themselves into Leonian characters at your feet, you'd at least pause to consider what they wanted.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content:
As for the one who chose me... let's just say He's generous and rotten in equal measure.
Where you land is entirely a matter of whim. You will be pulled from danger, that much is certain. Whether you land in another danger entirely—well, that's hardly the concern of that particular "journey."
How delightful. How unpredictable. I'm considering keeping up the tradition.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content:
Hahahaha—alright, alright, don't look at me like that, kid.
Just some traditions what you call the Elder Gods tend to follow. As for you—no price, no conditions. I'm always on your side.

voiceLines.title: Chat: Touch
voiceLines.content:
Heh... Missing your time in Ebwynnos?
It's right here, in my body. You're welcome to come back anytime.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Crisis
voiceLines.content: Erasing memory. Erasing existence. Familiar, isn't it? You know what I mean. Different origins—and yet They always breed in the dark.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Mythag
voiceLines.content:
I like spirited young people. Shame Mythag keeps such a stranglehold on entertainment—not even a decent hunting ground to speak of.
And worse still, that filthy thing is strutting around in broad daylight, even daring to wear the title—<Italic:professor>.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Like
voiceLines.content: I hate to admit it, but once in a rare while, I find myself thinking that aging isn't just something time does to you. It's merely a symbol. So I allow it to leave a mark on me. Only in appearance, of course.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Hate
voiceLines.content:
Yes, I know that disaster wasn't his direct order; it was merely an accident while he was out having fun. But that only makes me want to kill him more.
That black mist... He'd better not wander off alone—and he'd better never fall into my hands.

voiceLines.content: Everything I've done for you, and you won't even call me Uncle again. Aww, you're giving me a headache, little one.

Hmph. A little monster cozying up to that foreign monster.
And some fools actually put us on the same altar? What an insult!

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
No matter which dimension she's from, Lotan has little use for words—Lotan: Cetarchon even less so. Words mean nothing to her. Strength itself is the ultimate eloquence.
Beneath a regal, unhurried composure lies her truest hunger, burning in heterochromatic eyes like dying stars—she is an ancient force risen from the abyss of the universe, a bone blade forged in the wrath of chaos. To her, all things fall into two categories: those worthy of a fight, and those not.
Carved from the bones of the Astral Cetus, her twin blades hunger endlessly—just like her own unquenchable thirst for the zenith of strength.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
Mythag University Astronomical Observatory: Anomaly Report

Since A.F.@3, several observatories across the northern hemisphere have reported anomalous spectral attenuation at the galactic rim. Initial data showed that at least three catalogued stars vanished from the observable range within an extremely brief span, and their residual spectra matched no known stellar death models. No supernova radiation signature, no gravitational lensing from black hole accretion. The stars were simply swallowed whole—clean, swift, leaving no trace.
In March of A.F.@3, the Committee's Celestial Anomaly Task Force detected a series of extremely low-frequency Gnostic Fluctuations at the coordinates of the fourth vanished star. That August, following the fifth disappearance, the observatory finally captured a fleeting visual signal through the upgraded Silver-Core Long-Range Detection Array: a colossal, whale-like creature composed of bone, its abdomen bristling with spikes, its oral cavity emitting a high-temperature spectrum incompatible with the material plane. The instant it opened its maw, the stars' light poured in like water into the abyss—gone without a sound.
The footage lasted only 0.7 seconds before the array overloaded and cut out. Subsequent examination revealed irreversible structural collapse in one-third of the array's Silver-Core components.
In the winter of A.F.@3, the observatory detected a sudden shift in the Gnostic pulse's trajectory; its destination was our exact location.
The Committee was put on maximum alert, yet the anticipated catastrophe never came. The signal condensed into a harmless state upon approaching low orbit, ultimately settling on an uninhabited volcanic island in the northwestern seas. When the first survey team landed, they found twin massive blades of some unknown bone-like material deeply embedded in the basalt wall of the crater, and beside them, a humanoid figure 
seated cross-legged, as if she had long been waiting.
The entity appeared female, clad in bone-plated armor bearing alien motifs, with heterochromatic eyes. As the team approached, she opened her eyes.
"Any of you worth a strike?"
Her tone carried no hostility, only a calm bordering on arrogance.
The team exchanged glances. No one answered. After a moment's silence, she closed her eyes again.
"Then go find one. I'll wait."
Thereafter, the Committee and Mythag University jointly designated the island a Special Surveillance Zone, dispatching several Awakeners to assist in the investigation. After months of remote observation and cautious contact, the entity finally concurred with a state of loose supervision and was registered in the Committee's Awakener list—on the condition of being provided "a truly worthy opponent."
The stellar disappearances ceased entirely following her containment. But detection data suggested the energy of the devoured stars remained stored within her body. During prolonged observation, her Gnostic Index continued to climb, showing no sign of decline.

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Upon her arrival at Mythag, Lotan: Cetarchon remained quiet for two days. At dusk on the third, she appeared at the public training grounds, bone blades in hand.
The Awakeners of Mythag had every reason to be proud, especially those who frequented the training grounds. Yet they remained highly wary of this insolent, uninvited guest. Word of what happened on the volcanic island had already spread among the Awakeners; they knew exactly what kind of opponent awaited them.
Their caution, as it turned out, wasn't nearly enough.
When the first challenger was swatted out of the training grounds by a single strike, shattering a stone wall twenty meters away, the entire crowd erupted into an unprecedented frenzy. A second challenger stepped up, then a third... On that ordinary dusk in A.F.@3, nine Awakeners challenged Lotan: Cetarchon in succession.
According to campus reporter Hannah, who witnessed the events firsthand, Lotan: Cetarchon did not utter a single word throughout. She stood like a silent, unbreakable lighthouse amidst the crashing tides of assault. Her twin bone blades gleamed like light through the dusk, their elegant arcs ending every offensive with absolute precision.
By the end of that day, over 80% of Lotan's armor was shattered. She bore two severe wounds on her shoulder and abdomen, and a massive notch was gouged into her bone blade, leaving it on the verge of snapping. At the cost of all this, she became the only one left standing on the training grounds.
Looking at the deep gouges carved into the walls, the huge craters left on the ground, and the Awakeners watching her with conflicted expressions, she gave her first smile since arriving in this world.
"A pleasure meeting you all. You may call me Lotan: Cetarchon."

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
Her earliest memory was nothing but rage.
There was no face, no form, only an endless, boiling instinct for violence. She was chaos coalesced in the depths of the cosmos, a calamity brewed over billions of years. She tore, she burned, she devoured—it was the only thing she knew.
Until the "goddess" in the white veil arrived. Like a star split in half from its core, she felt her power ebb away, her flesh and bone uprooted from her spirit, her surging fury torn raw from her soul.
Unable to quell her rage, the goddess chose to sever her spirit from her flesh. The Beast of Chaos was no more; her body became Leviathan, sinking into the void with all her strength. And she, a mere mental remnant, awoke in an empty consciousness.
Yet her wrath had not died. It had transformed into something more enduring and terrifying: hunger. An endless hunger for strength drove her back to her feet.
She began to walk, to fight. She wandered the desolate sea of stars, challenging every formidable being that stood in her way. Each victory was like a handful of sand filled into her hollow shell—and grain by grain, she ground out a shape, a will, the very contour of "Lotan: Cetarchon."
Then she heard the whale's song.
The Astral Cetus, Its body an entire world, a colossus that bound and enslaved countless living beings—in It she saw neither desire nor fear, but kinship. Her memories began to return. She knew that was her strength. She knew that, from the very beginning, It had belonged to her.
So she came before It.
So she drew her sword against It.
The whale's power surged into her body like an unleashed torrent, nearly tearing her apart. Yet she remained standing—and when the tide receded, nothing was left of the whale but a carcass drifting in the void.
The enslaved planet was freed. The souls lost to desire looked up, calling her savior, guardian goddess, offering the Crown at her feet.
Lotan: Cetarchon did not respond to their praises. She simply stood atop the great whale's remains, feeling the newborn power surging within her, listening to the call deep in her soul growing clearer than ever.
It was the voice of the Astral Cetus. It was her own flesh and blood calling out to her. She placed her hand upon Leviathan's skull. Spirit and flesh, severed for countless eons, fused once more. Bone-plated armor clad her body; strength welled up within her.
The Beast of Chaos was reborn—but she was no longer the calamity who had known only fury. The long wandering, the countless battles, all those who had bested her and been bested by her—all had forged that pure chaos into a blade with a will of its own. She closed her eyes, savoring the surging, complete power within. But she also knew clearly that this was not the end.
The power of the Astral Cetus, the strength of Leviathan, all the stars she had devoured... all of it was but stepping stones beneath her feet. She lifted her bone blades, and turned toward the next unknown expanse of the universe.
She yearned for the next battle that would set her blood aflame.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
Lotan: Cetarchon never looks back at the corpses left in her wake.
Defeated opponents. Shattered wastelands. Devoured stars. One by one she steps over them all, seeking her next destination.
Someone once asked her what she'd do after reaching the summit of strength. She did not answer. The question was meaningless; fire never contemplates where it goes once it burns out. Fire has no "after." Burning is the whole of its existence.
She walks. She fights. She raises her blades again and again—never to prove, to protect, to avenge, or to satisfy any petty desire.
She does it simply because, in the clash of blades and the collision of raw strength, she can feel most vividly that she is alive.
The path toward strength has no end.
And she wouldn't have it any other way.

voiceLines.title: Awaken
voiceLines.content: I see an alien will in your eyes. Impure, but tenacious enough. Come, show me what strength or longing brought you before me.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: I
voiceLines.content: Not enough. Far from enough...

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: II
voiceLines.content: More—give me more power!

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: III
voiceLines.content: Power is boiling in my marrow!

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Observe
voiceLines.content: The seal loosens a little... The power from the depths of the universe is surging up. I haven't felt this in ages...

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Ponder
voiceLines.content: Heh... You see it clearly, Keeper. The shackles of power are meant to be shattered!

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Reflect
voiceLines.content: The scent of chaos—how nostalgic... Ever since the moment I was born from this void, my pursuit has never changed.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight
voiceLines.content: My bones tremble with delight... I have witnessed your effort. And this proves you are worthy to stand by my side, Keeper.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate
voiceLines.content: Just ahead... the zenith of power I have pursued my entire life... You've walked this path with me and guided me to this threshold. I'm eager to witness that ultimate day with you!

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Bloom
voiceLines.content: Ah, I see... there never was an end to power. The true challenge has only just begun! It was you who brought me here and showed me the reality. Soon, I shall present a more perfect warrior before you. Ensure that you return even stronger, my "opponent."

voiceLines.title: Affinity: I
voiceLines.content: Mercy, weakness, confusion... your eyes are clouded with impurities. One who wavers can never understand what strength is.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II
voiceLines.content: You wish to challenge me? I admire your courage, and I'll grant you the honor of being defeated. Consider this my respect for the "Keeper of Mythag."

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content: I've wandered the vast cosmos for eons; I've thrown all those "mighty" ones into the abyss. You are unique, but to stand beside me, first learn to hold your head high. I have no use for cowards.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content: Perhaps I judged you too hastily... Your growth, your hidden power have surprised me. I've watched countless lives fade in time, but you... are truly different. I am quite curious about the true origin of your power.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content:
Listen well, I'll say this only once:
I, Lotan, deem you an opponent worthy of my patience.
Until you reach your peak, I shall be your most reliable blade. This promise has nothing to do with feeling or loyalty. You're my most thrilling rival, and I will never let you fall along the way.

voiceLines.title: Chat: Touch
voiceLines.content: Oh? You want to fight me, here? Fine by me.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Crisis
voiceLines.content: I care little for the fading of this world—but I will not let it hinder my pursuit of strength.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Mythag
voiceLines.content: A false utopia, packed with weaklings, cowards, and self-deluding fools. But no matter. This place brings me the most thrilling opponents—and that's enough.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Like
voiceLines.content: Brave or cowardly, strong or frail... Heh—no, I don't care what kind of person my opponent is. Any worthy opponent brings me a genuine thrill.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Hate
voiceLines.content: Weakness. Of all the vile things in the world, weakness is the most wretched sin. Everyone is born with a sword in hand; no one has the right to yield before the end, nor to step onto the fated battlefield already resigned to defeat. That insults both your opponent and yourself.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Keeper
voiceLines.content: I dislike those with a divided heart, as such division usually means weakness. But you are an exception. I once believed those who carry too much could never go far. But the path you've chosen surprises me... Perhaps an opponent walking a different path is more worthy of honing and challenge. Wouldn't you agree, "opponent"?

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Tulu
voiceLines.content: He wasted immense power. He trapped his talent in a long dream, chased there by fear, guilt, and fatigue. A pity.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Lotan
voiceLines.content: True power has nothing to do with revenge or protection—power is simply power. My other self never truly grasped this. That's why she's not strong enough.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Doll: Inferno
voiceLines.content: Doubting the value of existence simply because oblivion awaits... I have no interest in such childish debates. Destruction means nothing, nor does memory. Power itself is the meaning.

voiceLines.content: Come—kill me, or be killed.

voiceLines.title: Investigation Success
voiceLines.content: Hardly worth my time.

voiceLines.title: Investigation Halted
voiceLines.content: Heh... Now that was thrilling. Next time, I won't hold back.

storySections.content:
Like the most precocious of children, she is always attuned to your innermost thoughts, forever drawing out your trust and confessions, then, at just the right moment, offering you the "blessing" you've longed for. 
But bear this in mind: never let her dainty frame and pitiful eyes stir compassion within you, lest you become one more of the many greedy souls that pure white form has devoured.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
This Silver Core was recovered by Mythag's Keeper %player% in the aftermath of the Mount Ever@2t collapse incident. As the dimension in which it originally resided is no longer observable, the consequences of Silver Core extraction—as well as the proper awakening method—remain undetermined.

The following observations are transcribed from the paper handbook carried by Keeper %player%:

Upon visual inspection, the Silver Core presents as exceptionally pure, showing no discernible impurities. In the absence of external interference, its overall structure trends toward regularity—as though some underlying will were straining to keep it appearing whole and composed, radiating a bright luster not unlike firelight.

Its Gnosis Index, however, sits near the absolute lower bound. The actual internal structure is extraordinarily fragile and loosely bound. When the observation distance falls below 1/@1 inch, the Silver Core's self-protection response is triggered: the observer is abruptly confronted with a dense flow of particles resembling drifting ice crystals. It is presumed these particles were previously refracting incident light in a highly unusual manner, shielding the interior from direct observation.
To put it less professionally... I'd call this a Silver Core steeped in "deception."

Once the self-protection mechanism is triggered, the observer's body enters a brief paralytic state, the pupils gradually fading until fully blanched. Throughout this window, the Silver Core continues to adjust itself, returning to the stable configuration it maintained prior to observation.
Repeated trials indicate that the mechanism inflicts no lasting harm; however, the accompanying hypothermic symptoms pose a non-negligible risk. Note: prompt consumption of sweets—apple-based desserts in particular—provides a distinctly soothing effect. The reason for this... remains unclear... <Italic:Right?
>


Luckily, after everything, it's plain enough that this selfish, tightly-guarded little trickster bears no genuine ill will toward us.

—Excerpt from <Italic:Mythag University Silver Core Storage Records>

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
As everyone knows, what do they call a school?

An ivory tower!

It sounds a perfect match for the title of "Fairy"—after all, where else could one find such a flawless paradise, filled with wealthy, leisurely people whose hearts brim with precious, naive trust, all just waiting to become devoted followers?

Caraboo's cult grew at a truly astonishing pace, amassing a considerable number of followers in a very short time. The core faithful were almost entirely young Awakeners, who believed in this "Fairy Godmother" with near-devout fervor, willingly turning over fixed offerings of candy and sweets at regular intervals. Surprisingly, or perhaps not, Caraboo did indeed bestow blessings from time to time, most often during the traditional holidays of the Kingdom of Leonia, such as the impossible snowfall that came during the Silverfrost Eve of 3@1, and the candy rain on New Year's Eve that people still speak of to this day.

The Academic Affairs Office, it seems, never once discussed whether to put a stop to this "on-campus proselytizing" that, in principle, ought not to exist in the first place.

"Let them play. We all know what these children have been through. There are certain things only another child can do."

"Of course, don't let it go too far."

A certain school staff member, who prefers to remain unnamed, offered the above remarks with a warm smile. According to unreliable sources, the incident preceding her afternoon tea with Caraboo was the one and only time Caraboo has ever truly attempted to cross the school's rules.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
Caraboo was still a child when the Crusades were at their height. Alone and with no one to turn to, she resolved to travel east to the Principality of Antioch to seek out her aunt's family. Word had it that the new lands of the East stood for freedom and dreams, that even someone without a penny to their name could carve out a way there. Her Aunt Rosa had even started up a farm and was doing quite well for herself. Caraboo had been close with Aunt Rosa in her early childhood, and she made up her mind to save enough for the fare to Antioch.

Caraboo drifted through the city's slums, a girl with no connections, scraping by on stealing, swindling, cheating, and conning; whatever innocence she once had was worn away completely. In time, she crossed paths with a wizard named Evagh, who made her a promise: work with him, and they'd split the offerings of his followers thirty-seventy—enough for her to save her travel fare east, and plenty left over to buy heaps of her beloved candy. And so the two formed a con artist duo, with Caraboo enshrined as a little fairy godmother in a makeshift rural temple, while Evagh gathered followers in her name as her high priest.

As Caraboo's fame in the region grew, she found herself no longer content with the current split, and threatened to walk out on the partnership, forcing Evagh to flip the arrangement into a seventy-thirty split in her favor. Now finally with the upper hand, Caraboo lived at her leisure as a false godmother, until she discovered that Evagh had been embezzling her offerings all along, secretly taking three wives and fathering four sons behind her back. Faced with this betrayal, Caraboo showed no anger. She told Evagh, in the tenderest of tones, that she had long known heading east was nothing but an empty, distant dream, that money was of no use to her, and it would be better left in his hands; her only wish was to share a meal with Evagh's family, and together discuss their future ventures in fraud.

Delighted to find that Caraboo had finally come to her senses, Evagh happily extended the invitation for her to attend the banquet. As dinner drew near its end, Caraboo's expression suddenly changed, and at a single word from her, the nearby villagers—her loyal believers—came storming in, wielding farming tools and kitchenware, beating the wizard's household of eight half to death, while everything of value in the house was swept clean away. "You're still too green to fool me"—Caraboo departed in satisfaction, not yet noticing the small black triangle upon her own forehead...

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
Have you ever tried telling a lie? The first lie to leave your lips always comes with a stumbling tongue, a heart that nearly leaps out of your throat, and sweat gathering in your palms; even the gentle sunlight becomes a dizzying, blinding glare.

But once a lie has been repeated ten thousand times, the fear fades away. The words spoken grow smooth, the mind grows ever clearer, and the smile settles into something quite natural.

Playing the fairy, playing the godmother, playing the kin of some figure in power—she had long since mastered the myriad layered identities she had fabricated, grown accustomed to hiding herself behind her lies, until she herself became but a part of the lies.

And that first little hare still hides within a small farm bathed in the sunset light of her memories.

On nights when the ice thaws and the snow melts away, it quietly peeks its head out once more.

storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
Though their frames are the same, the difference between this boy and the familiar little knight is plain to see.
The light has left his eyes; his white garments are sullied. More telling still, he keeps to himself, pointedly maintaining a distance from all living souls.
But there is no need to fear. Beneath that horrific slime beats the heart you once knew—one that still pulses for loyalty and justice.
Though his oaths were once forsaken, he has at last reclaimed his creed.
He will continue his struggle—against the other voice echoing within him, and against any force that threatens what he holds dear.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
Dear readers, this is an afterword, but more so, it is my confession.
To finish this old-fashioned chivalric novel, I spent a fortune at auction to acquire that mysterious helmet, one said to belong to no kingdom known to history. And thanks to it, as you can see, inspiration flooded me; I felt as if I truly saw a vast and ancient battlefield, with armored knights crossing blades. Relying on these wondrous hallucinations, I completed what I consider my finest work.
But I never expected that this antique, even as it granted me inspiration, harbored a terrifying demon within.
Readers, try to imagine a voice—chaotic, unrelenting, droning day and night. Now imagine your limbs acting on their own, your mind blacking out again and again. No, it's not blacking out; it's more like your will detaching from your body. You know exactly what you are doing, but you can only watch... yet that was undoubtedly my body.
Just last night, as I finished the final page, I heard It again.
And then—God, I cannot bear to recall those scenes—
I have committed an unforgivable sin. The newspapers will tell you before this book does...
It—again—It is starting again—
<Italic:(handwriting grows crooked)>
No no no no no no no no, I can't—not again—
...

<Italic:(handwriting steadies)>
Surprisingly, It stopped—as if something was weighing It down. I don't know what it was, but I am grateful for its struggle.
Perhaps God is giving me one last chance, sparing me from becoming a devil entirely.

My pistol is loaded.
May God forgive me.

—Excerpt from the afterword of <Italic:The Shadowless Knight>, the final work of writer Clark Zeiros

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Mythag once had a haunting that put the whole school on edge. Below is the interview transcript compiled by campus reporter Hannah:
"Late at night, I heard rustling in the stacks... I didn't dare look. But the next morning, I found all the books shelved perfectly, better than I could have done it myself!" —School Librarian
"Don't you think the campus has been much cleaner lately? Could there be a ghost picking up the trash at night?" —A Fieldwork Instructor
"On missions, I always feel like I'm being followed... Sometimes I hear fierce fighting, but when I turn around, there are only the remains of Dissoluted monsters all over the ground." —A Rookie Investigator
A few bold students formed an investigation squad, trading one night's sleep for the truth.
The culprit confessed to his "crimes" and sincerely apologized for causing panic. Yet when the thanks began to pour in, he seemed rather ill at ease. In his own words, "I just like to keep my hands busy."
When asked, the school counselor, Sylvia, offered her diagnosis: "He's a good boy, kind by nature—but he carries too much guilt over the past. Over time, it turned into a deep-rooted sense of unworthiness—kindness offered too plainly only makes it harder for him."
This incident blew over quietly, but the legend of the "Formless Ghost" spread in its wake. By unspoken agreement, the faculty and students said nothing of who he was. In time, everyone came to understand that this "ghost" simply wanted to help.
Everyone seemed to sense that for a boy who doesn't want to be seen, the best thanks is to let this secret remain his alone.

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
He too once set out on a journey, just like the heroes in bedtime stories.
But he was no knight of justice, and there was no longer any princess left in the world to be saved.
He slew not fearsome dragons, but many unarmed civilians, wailing and fleeing in terror.
<Italic:"The young knight slew the wicked wizard, routed the stubborn enemy forces, and razed the monsters' fortress to the ground... He was brave, mighty, invincible. Down that endless road, he left nothing but a long, trailing streak of blood.">
Were there a bard who couldn't tell dreams from reality, he would surely spin the tale like that.
But the protagonist was lucid; those eyes had never reflected anything false.
He knew his spear had pierced an old man's chest. He knew the black slime had devoured the soldiers long since surrendered. He knew a family's little cottage had turned to ash as he passed... all because they were connected to those who took what he once guarded.
He knew he had never lived in any fairy tale; those romantic illusions had died along with his homeland. Perhaps he grew up in that moment. Perhaps he was a child still.
It wasn't until he finally came to his senses, giving his life for complete strangers, that he saw a phantom in his tears—a phantom that should not exist.
<Italic:"Ogier, I am deeply disappointed in you. You are a knight in name only, the most unworthy of all.">
The "princess's" face seemed veiled in sheer silk, but her voice was crystal clear, sharper than any blade in the world, gouging his heart.
This cruel hallucination torments him still, a nightmare that did not fade with death.
He will spend eternity drowning in the remorse of a broken oath.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
The pitch-black sludge, the symbol of his sin, still roils within him, scheming to seize control of this body again. He must constantly cling to that fragile thread of will to keep from losing the battle.
And what he has found anew for himself—what is worth defending—has become the sole anchor tethering his sanity.
He can never return to his homeland, but Mythag has become his new castle.
He can no longer guard his princess, but fate will bring new encounters.
Where none can bear witness, the boy drops to one knee, one hand pressed against his cold chest, and declares to his absent lord:
<Italic:"I shall obey your command, my lord. Though my life burns to ash, though my soul is bled dry... I shall guard you and your world forever.">
<Italic:"This... is the oath... I bear once more.">

voiceLines.title: Awaken
voiceLines.content: Honor, justice, loyalty... every virtue worth the name perished by my own hand. What you have summoned is no knight of virtue, but a mere sinner. Even so, I will guard you with this broken body. Please give the order... if you can still trust me.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: I
voiceLines.content: You truly wish to elevate me? ...As you wish, my lord. Thank you.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: II
voiceLines.content: Silence! ...Forgive me, my lord. That demon grows more restless as my power grows.

voiceLines.title: Upgrade: III
voiceLines.content: With this power, I can protect more people...

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Observe
voiceLines.content: The formless power keeps churning... It's harder to master than I imagined.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Ponder
voiceLines.content: <Italic:Devour... Destroy...> Tch—do not think to sway me! I will not bend to your will again!

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Reflect
voiceLines.content: I know—only the unwavering can master this dreadful power. I have wrestled with It deep within for far too long.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Insight
voiceLines.content: Its restlessness seems to have abated. Is it because... you are here?

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Elevate
voiceLines.content: It still whispers in my ear, urging me to turn my spear upon the innocent... But worry not. I know I can resist. Your faith in me has given me the strength to believe in myself.

voiceLines.title: Enlighten: Flourish
voiceLines.content:
I feel a strength beyond measure, yet that tormenting voice has vanished. It must be your tireless encouragement that has steeled my will to stand against it.
...Thank you. Thank you, my lord.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: I
voiceLines.content: Have you commands for me, my lord? If not, I shall return to my patrol.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: II
voiceLines.content:
You are curious about the black slime clinging to my body?
It is the source of my power—and my despair, too. Restless as it is, it can take any shape, so it serves me well in battle. I shape it into spear and shield, for someone once took great care to teach me how to wield them... What? You wish to touch it? I must refuse. It is far too dangerous.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: III
voiceLines.content: If it isn't too much trouble, could you tell me about your time as a Keeper? No, I do not seek a tale—I only wish to learn. After all, on this path of "protection," you have walked long before me.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: IV
voiceLines.content: I know the wrongs I have committed can never be undone. "Atonement" is nothing but a comfort I offer myself. But even so... Wait... please don't pat my head, my lord.

voiceLines.title: Affinity: V
voiceLines.content:
My lord, I must confess—each time I watch you give your all to fight the calamities and save this world, a quiet longing stirs within me. If only I could be of some use to you... You truly permit it? I see.
Then... allow me to stay by your side until your journey reaches its end. As your knight, and yours alone, I shall spend what remains of this life clearing every obstacle before you.

voiceLines.title: Chat: Touch
voiceLines.content: Don't touch me! ...No, forgive me. I only feared I might hurt you.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Crisis
voiceLines.content: It feels so much like the power that coils about my body, only... more evil. Is this what you've been fighting all this time, my lord?

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Mythag
voiceLines.content: Mythag... it is such a beautiful, peaceful place. I had a home like this once, though now, not even a record of it remains.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Like
voiceLines.content: The drift of hearth-smoke at dusk, rain-swept meadows, the smiling faces of the people... all of these speak of peace. That is what I cherish. And I shall give my all to guard it.

voiceLines.title: Chat: What I Hate
voiceLines.content: I despise the weak, the wavering, and those who harm the innocent. Because... that's exactly who I used to be. I loathe myself for all the sins I've committed.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About the Keeper
voiceLines.content: I never dared hope to protect another, nor to find a path to atonement—yet you made it possible. For someone like me, my lord... you are the only reason I'm still here.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Ogier
voiceLines.content: Though his power is limited and his hopes naive, he remains pure, unstained. I think that's what a real knight ought to be. Yet I can never again become someone like him.

voiceLines.title: Chat: About Helot: Catena
voiceLines.content: Miss Helot: Catena's power seems to stem from a profound hatred. But hatred, once kindled, keeps spreading until it swallows everything. I fear that one day it will cost her far more than she can bear.

voiceLines.title: Chat: Cherished Things
voiceLines.content: Even if all I once cherished turns to dust, I will protect others to the end—I will not die with regret again.
